title: Atlanta Falcons players speak to the media post-practice at AT&T Training Camp | Press Conference
text: Touch with the guys. >> Oh, yeah. It was a blessing. Um, you know, things uh I had a little situation over in San Francisco. So, you know, my biggest thing was just getting on a team where I know I can contribute and you know, help win games. So, and then when it lined up I'm coming back home, I mean it's just two blessings in one. So, excited for the opportunity. >> How about from Charlotte to to to Atlanta? How was that journey? >> Yeah, it's crazy. Um, even taking it past Charlotte, just uh growing up here, you know, I remember coming up to the practices sitting in the stands watching. So, now to be on the other side of that it's kind of a surreal full circle moment. So, it's just a blessing for those I grew up with and you know, watched me come up through elementary, middle school, high school, I get to come back and play for the home team. >> How was it suiting up in the preseason game and running out into the Benz as a as a Falcon? >> Yeah, it was dope. Uh, you know, that's an experience I've never been on. I've been on the other side of it, but coming in feeling the energy from the fans, the I mean it was it was surreal in there. So, it was happy and I can't wait to get back in there and put on for the city. >> How do you think the group responded, just the team overall responded today after kind of the way the first preseason went? >> Yeah, you know, anytime you strap up you want to get the win. So, when you don't, you know, you got to go back, be honest with yourself, you know, from coaches on down. I feel like we did that and um we were just intentional coming out starting with energy and um I feel like we did that today, came out and we're working in the right direction for sure. >> What was the situation in San Francisco you said? >> Um, yeah, you know, signed there in free agency. Um, just a bad timing with a slight injury. Um, so you know, we had to pivot, but you know, uh God works in mysterious ways. Everything happens for a reason, so I'm where I'm supposed to be. >> Knowing the situation you're walking into with Pearson Jaywalk, what's your plan? How do you approach that and what have those conversations been like with the coaching staff coming into this new >> Um, yeah. So, um I mean I hate it for those guys, you know, Jaywalk. I haven't really got a chance to meet him, but I saw the work he put out there. I know I know he wants it bad. From being around JP, same type of attitude. So, you know, hate it for those guys, but for me uh my approach to the game is indifferent. You know, I prepare I prepare to be the starter every week, you know, that's my mindset. I want to not only play, but know that I want the team to be able to count on me to play 15 snaps to 65. So, that's just my mindset. So, I've just been getting overtime with the coaches, coming in learning the playbook. You know, I just got here like 3 or 4 days ago. So, you know, that's uh that's probably the biggest challenge getting back in game shape and learning the playbook. So, I'm just attacking it head-on. >> Ken, how would you describe your play style and kind of what you're bringing to this defense? >> Um yeah, you know, um I got that kind of F you mentality out there, you know, physical, you know, I want to set the tone. We dictate the tempo and um just a guy who can get it done from multiple spots. I can play outside, I can rush inside. So, just kind of that chess piece up front and going to bring the attitude to win. >> Did you get the sense that that is something that was intentional about bringing you in is that F you mentality and what they kind of want to add to this defense? >> Yeah, definitely. From talking with DC, you know, Coach Odom, you know, all the coaches, you know, we want to you know, for good teams you got to have a nasty defense and you you kind of that has to be like contagious around from secondary to linebacker to D-line. So, you know, more guys we getting with that mindset, the better we going to play this defense. >> Ken, tell us a little bit more about this mindset. Where does that come from for you? >> Um I think it's just really been instilled to me since like little, you know, come from hard-working family. So, my mom used to bust her ass, my dad used to bust her ass. So, they kind of instilled that in me. So, I've always been a hard worker my whole life. Um coming out of high school under recruited, I was just always head down working mentality. So, I mean that's I'm not where I want to be, but that's got me this far so far. So, there's no reason to switch that up. So, I take pride in that. >> For some players, a switch kind of flips for them when they get on the field. It doesn't feel like a switch really needs to flip with you all that much, but describe the mindset when you're stepping on the field. >> Uh yeah, I mean it's it's killer be killed, you know, you know, actually y'all getting to know me, I'm a good personality guy. I joke around a lot, but >> [laughter] >> when it's between the white lines it's war. So, you know, you got to have that balance. You know, for other guys it takes different things for them to get ready, but I just make sure when I step on the field I'm I'm always ready to roll. >> It's been 3 or 4 days, you don't have a large sample size, but what's your first impressions of this defense? >> Um I like it. Um up front, you know, they want us to get after it, set the tempo, be nasty. We got some athletic linebackers who can cover range, uh fit off of us. And um just from watching last year and even here, we got DBs who go up and make plays on the ball. So, that's what you want. So, it's all about just building as a team, coming together, and make sure when it's time to roll out we're one to be a unit. >> Traveling traveling to Indy this week, how do you measure success with joint practices? >> Um yeah, you know, I think it starts with individual battles. You always want to win your one-on-ones. So, especially as a D-lineman, you know, I want to beat the offensive front of me, but just just making our presence felt as a defense. I feel like whenever defense makes an impression on the practice against the offense, you're doing something right direction. >> How much do you enjoy those, you know, breaking up the season and having facing another team? >> Uh you know, it's good. You always want to um you know, we get work against each other all the time. But, you always want to test your sword against uh you know, guys around the league cuz we go against these guys every day. So, it's kind of easy to pick up on tendencies and stuff, but you know, you play a different opponent every week. So, it's good to kind of see a new face out there and put put a helmet on someone in a different color jersey. >> Do you get more out of um joint practices or the preseason games? >> Um good question. I feel like it just depends on your rep count, you know, you know, I know how it's structured. Some guys might play more in practice than the actual game. So, just maximizing your reps. So, whether that's in practice or in the game, you just got to do your best. >> you? >> Yeah. I just want to roll. I want to get the playbook out and roll. So, you know, I mean uh anytime I strap up, I just it's a eval for me. So, you know, I want to put my best foot forward regardless. >> Any reflections on your time in Cincinnati or takeaways from that period in your career? >> Um yeah, you know, it was a um you know, I'm always grateful to them. That's the team that drafted me, you know, changed my for me and my family's life forever. So, nothing but love and respect for those guys over there. And um you know, from going to a Super Bowl to a AFC Championship and not getting back to the playoffs, you know, I kind of realized, you know, as a rookie going to Super Bowl, you feel like, man, I might do this every year. It's easy. But, you know, the league's not like that. Uh you see the challenges every year. So, now I've been like itching and clawing to get back. And I know we got guys here who've been in the playoffs, some who haven't. So, I think we're all kind of pushing to the same goal. So, just focus on getting back to the playoffs. >> Has Jessie here helped you a little bit? >> Yeah, that's my guy, you know, um when I got drafted, I think Jessie was probably the first Bengal to reach out. And you know, he was like that big brother for me coming to Cincinnati, you know, made sure I was good and all that. So, I didn't tell him I was coming here until I wanted to make sure everything was official. But, I saw him in the hallway. It's good to always have a familiar face in. So, that's my guy. I love to be back with him. >> What What his reaction to you in the hallway? >> Uh it was uh he didn't recognize me at first cuz I grew my beard out. So, he kind of did a double take. He was like, "Cam?" And we dapped up, uh, chopped it up for a little bit. Um, told me about how good of an opportunity it was here and just to, um, lock in and maximize it. So, I told him, "You know, you know what I do." So. >> The run defense didn't go off the way that you wanted on Friday. Kind of what do you guys want to accomplish as a group up there in the middle of the show? >> Yeah, you know, you, uh, you always want to make a team one-dimensional. When a team can run the ball on you, that opens up play action game, drop back pass. So, we want to stop the run and go have some fun. So, I think we want to go up there put our foot down, stop the run game, make them one-dimensional, just pin pin our ears back and go get money. >> You mentioned the fact that this is a new opportunity for you several times now. Aside from the fact that you are coming home and that's a big deal, obviously, what does this opportunity truly mean to you? >> Um, it means the world. Um, you know, I, uh, I tore my Achilles a couple years ago. So, that kind of changed my perspective on the game. Not really like I was a guy who took it for granted, but when you have a whole season kind of taken away from you like that, it kind of just makes you more hungry, want to maximize the opportunity. So, now I got my feet back under me. I'm fully healthy. So, I just want to go out there and put my best foot forward and just maximize the God-given opportunity. >> Cam, do you have a favorite play you've ever been a part of? >> Ooh. >> High school, college, pros? >> Uh, man, a good question. Uh. Yeah, probably, um. I'll just go with college. Uh, my senior year, uh, my first game of senior year, you know, the off season was funny cuz during COVID, we didn't even know we were going to have a game. Um, so, our coach kind of sent us home, said, "Work out. Hopefully we'll play. If not, I mean, good luck." Basically, but uh, so, we went there to South Alabama. I think I had like seven, eight tackles, uh, two sacks, um. One in the last drive of the game and, uh, a couple of friends that ended. So, that was just like the good stepping stone in kind of trajectory of my NFL career and trying to put my name on the map. >> How are you going to manage ticket requests for all your friends and family? >> Ooh. Um, you know, uh, so, I got a system in place. I kind of funnel all that through my parents and they're kind of the sticklers about it. So, I mean, close ones can hit me up, but I kind of funnel it to the parents and they kind of they kind of keep it easy for me, for sure. >> So, if you get directed to the parents, that means you probably don't get a ticket at all, though. line. >> Um, you know what? They So, it'll go through the parents and they channel it back to me. We'll see what's going on. But, just so they're not blowing me up all week, especially now, you know what I'm saying? Just kind of keeps the funnel. So, some of them are scared to ask the parents, so that kind of helps too. >> Or they're hard. They're like >> Yeah, you know, my my parents don't play. Yeah, they don't play. Yeah, for >> Just overall, how did you feel the team's energy was, you know, coming into this practice after that first preseason game? >> I think we brought more energy um today out for practice than um you know, we probably had uh in our first preseason game. So, uh the improvement was good. >> What was the biggest takeaway just uh from you and the defense really after that first game? >> Uh just more celebration uh between um each other. Uh just bringing more energy. Uh even as this, you know, a little trash talk to the offense a little bit, you know, just something that just, you know, brings some camaraderie to our side of the ball. >> With Jessie out, how valuable is this opportunity been for you in this portion of camp getting all these reps? >> Um you know, anytime I'm on the field, you know, I'm treating it, you know, like I'm a one. Um so, you know, I definitely value every rep I take on the field, you know, no matter who I'm in there with, no matter when I'm called, you know, just taking, you know, every rep as a one rep will just, you know, help me in the long run. >> What do you see from from Xavier getting to play next to him now for a couple weeks closely on the field uh just in terms of how he's grown from his first year? >> Uh you know, X is a great player. Um he's somebody I, you know, I like to call a gamer. Um you know, he does a lot of things that you know, is you know, you know, you you know, just looking at the plays, you you know, you wouldn't really think that that would be, you know, maybe his play to make. But, you know, he just has a really high football IQ. >> What do you like about joint practices? >> Uh gives us the um you know, the ability in the preseason, just like we do in the regular season, to you know, scout our opponent a little bit more. Um you know, as we're also you know, evaluating each other. Um you know, evaluating the offense um as an opponent is good. Um and joint practices and um you know, it also gives us, you know, just some extra leg up in the game as well. >> What do you like the focus? What's been the focus for you specifically throughout training camp up to at point in the off season? >> Um really just the same approach every day is for me is just to be a pro. Um, just taking one day at a time. Um, you know, no matter, you know, you know, when my time is called or or what role it's going to be in. Um, just, you know, being ready for my opportunity whenever it comes. >> Do you like joint practices more than preseason games? Like which one do you think you get the most value in? >> Uh, I like preseason games. Um, just cuz I like being in the game. Um, I like really being able to, you know, hit. Um, you know, not really have, you know, a coach telling us, you know, to dial back a little bit or anything like that. So, I'm much more of a player that likes to play in the game. >> How would you measure success with joint practices? >> Um, really just who executed the best. Um, you know, who had the less amount least amount of penalties. Um, who could get the opponent off their game. Uh, whether it is, you know, them getting false starts, you know, starting a little unnecessary bickering, you know, just just winning the day, you know, just winning the day. You know, that's winning the joint practice to me. That would be a win. >> respect for the Colts. Um, y'all had a good game, clean game with them over there. And respect will be a big part of keeping the practices clean. >> Yeah, for sure. I, you know, I'd say our coach Stefanski, um, you know, that's one thing that he's preached to us, you know, just to, you know, start, you know, and just be a be a team first type of players. And a part of being a team first guy is, you know, allowing everybody to get better. Um, you know, and fighting at a joint practice or anything like that, that can end a practice early. Um, you know, that can, um, you know, just prolong, you know, getting better. So, definitely it's a respect on our on our side. Uh, it should be respect on their side. You know, we just want to have a collaborative practice. >> Marco, what did coach Wilks say about the front defense in particular from from Friday? >> Uh, just, you know, just being more stout. Um, I think that that ties into all three levels of the defense. Um, just playing more stout, playing more downhill, and you know, just, you know, things that we that he saw that were good and uh, you know, things that we can improve on, of course. >> Just to get back on the field real play. >> Being stout and being more on it with that. I've heard of that. How would you describe like how do you get better at that? >> I mean I I I really think everybody watches the tape um as an individual and you know critiques their own effort cuz they only know how much that they can give. But uh you know from a a just play style standpoint, you know, just being more downhill um as far as that goes. Tightening up as far as our safety play or you know just playing more downhill once we recognize run pass. >> What was the defense reaction just overall um when the James Pierre-Louis came out and kind of what was the message to the team? >> Um honestly it wasn't really a message to the team um and that's something that James has to deal with. Um you know it's something that we supported him on. You know, really just as a team and as a player for myself, I really try to focus on things that I can control and you know you know James' situation is really out of my control. >> One thing that Kevin Stefanski said specifically about the James situation after the game was that he has showed up to work every day to try to be a good teammate and to try to get back to what he was doing before. What can you say about his approach to training camp and the way he's been working every day? >> Yeah, that's one thing that I can say is um you know James has been a great teammate. Um he's approached practice every day uh you know with a great attitude, great effort in practice. Um he's very attentive in meetings so you know from what I can say about James is you know he's definitely you know came to came to work every day you know with a with a good mindset. >> With James out and with the Jaylen out for the for the season, talk about any pressure that all of this puts on your room and you safeties in the gaps. You guys going to do while this cloud of uncertainty kind of clears >> Uh I don't think it puts any extra pressure on our room. You know, I feel like our room is ready to handle whatever pressure comes with you know playing the defensive side of the ball, playing DB. And uh we definitely have guys that we feel can step up uh in those pass rush rooms and the defensive line rooms as well. So you know, I feel like we'll be fine. >> Who do you think has stood out to you kind of and can kind of step up? >> Uh I really [snorts] pay attention to my room a lot, but uh, I really think everybody on the D-line has a chance. You know, I It's hard for me to call out any one player specifically without feeling like, you know, I'm miscrediting someone else. So, I really feel like the whole D-line has really taken that up as a room to, you know, step up for JP and James. I mean, uh, Jay Walker and uh, James while they're down. >> How do you feel like you've grown with Jeff Ulbrich as your defensive coordinator? >> Uh, really just my, you know, my joy, my joy for the game. You know, I think as a defensive player in the NFL and, you know, sometimes as a young guy who has a lot of high expectations for theirself, um, you know, I think sometimes you lose your joy for the game. But, um, you know, Brick has really, you know, just, you know, brought that mindset uh, for our defense and, you know, really just for everybody on our team from being a player in the league for a a good time and to just, you know, he calls us lucky, you know, just lucky to be out here, um, and just be able to do something that, you know, uh, for a long time I did for free. Um, you know, just to have this be my job now is a blessing, um, that I try to, you know, whenever I do get frustrated, I try to, you know, take a step back and realize that I'm in a blessed position. >> Um, how do you feel just like the energy was in practice today, kind of bouncing back after that game? >> I think everybody came today with some good energy knowing that we did some things we need to get better on and just coming out attacking and still like pushing through everything. >> What was kind of your biggest takeaway after the the opening game? >> Uh, the biggest takeaway was just for us to keep crafting on what we all knew. We still all trying to gel together, so the big thing was just keep trusting the process and attacking the things we know we need to attack. >> How much are you looking forward to facing another team for a couple days and doing practices in Indy? >> Uh, I'm looking I'm excited to cuz, you know, you It puts a place where you guys are and then allows you to work on your game against someone else. We don't really know you after having a couple weeks of training camp with some guys, so it's just good to attack somebody else in their scheme and their plays. >> You got a lot of reps with the ones, it would appear. How how comfortable are you in that role here? >> I'm pretty comfortable. I mean, I'm never You never say you got it. You know, there's always stuff you can work on, but uh definitely comfortable with the guys around me. They push me and I push them, so it's a fun thing. It's fun process. >> You played under Kevin, right? You played with him? >> Yes, for a little bit. >> So, why did you want to come back here and play under him again here in Atlanta? >> I mean, I feel I believe he's a great coach. He really know what he's doing. I mean, he took Cleveland to a playoffs a couple times, so it's like and he know how to push his players, too. He's a motivating coach, so I'll never like not want to play for him. >> So, how how does he push you then? Like, kind of >> I mean, he knows who you are. He He takes time with his people, so he'll see you and like, you know, be you, you know, attack and do what you doing, what you best at. >> You talked about the different things that he likes to look for in joint workouts. What are you looking forward to most in those? >> Just to keep progressing my game, keep getting closer with my teammates, you know, um and just you know, being a standard that we trying to set in this defense. >> What was the defense's reaction when they heard that James Pierce was going to have to miss half the season and who's going to really be able to step up in his absence? >> I think everybody just got around him, you know, picked him up cuz it's still, you know, a down thing, even though he probably knew it was coming, but uh everybody got around him, you know, kept his spirit up and like, you in these playoff game um preseason games, you know, show what you can do and just go out there work, you know. >> We did see number three back out there today. What did it mean to see him out there working out? >> Thanks. It's always great cuz he's a great leader and he brings the energy, you know, and like, he see being back there, he see things you don't really see, so he helps you out a lot, too.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski AT&T Training Camp Press Conference | August 17, 2026 | Atlanta Falcons
text: Okay, good week uh coming up here. It'll be a great day out there. It's going to be warm. Um great day for practice this morning with the guys. We'll then bring them in tomorrow for some meetings, a workout, and then get on the airplane to head to Indianapolis. Two really good days planned versus the Colts Wednesday and Thursday. Have had uh great conversations with Coach Syken and their staff on things that we're going to try to get done over the two days. Uh I think it's always good to go up against a different team in practice. you know, the proverbial different color jersey, all that stuff. Uh but also just a different scheme. So, good for our defense, our offense, our special teams to see a different scheme in the course of practice. Uh and then obviously have the game uh there Saturday. So, big week for us. Excited about it. Um with that, I'll take any questions. >> What do you want to accomplish there? >> A lot. You know, I think a lot of situational football uh will get accomplished. We'll get a lot of good reps for our starters. Um, they'll get the majority of the reps, which is by design, and then they will not play in the game uh on Saturday. But a lot of a lot of football to to get practiced and and the competitive part of it, too. You know, you get to do one-on- ones versus players that you don't have a a book on, quote unquote. Uh so I think that's important for our guys in the competitive aspect of it and then for the football team just to be exposed to different schemes uh I think will be really important. >> What stood out to you from Friday night after you watched the film? >> Yeah, a lot of areas that we want to continue to to work at uh work on a bunch of things that that I really liked as well. I thought, you know, starting special teams, I thought there's some really good efforts out there, some really good plays and things that we can teach and coach off of. uh in in all those phases. I thought uh defensively uh some good from you know turning the ball over there in the second half was obviously a positive. I thought too grabby in the back end which is something to learn from. We have the officials out here every single day and we'll continue to work on those type of things. And then making plays when the ball's in the air. I thought there were some contested catches that they came down with. So that's an area that we'll look at. Offensively, the efficiency in the run game has to be better. I think that's where where we'll start and obviously there's uh opportunities we feel like in the past game. But also positives I thought uh you know Vance Joseph does an excellent job bringing pressures and and did throughout that game which you know we needed to see and I thought by and large the protection responsibilities were really good. >> What right tackle did anybody separate themselves there? I >> think it's too soon to say there's separation. I think it's still a great uh great for us to to work through different guys. uh as we continue uh through camp. >> Would you want Taylor playing those joint practices? >> Uh he's going to practice today and then we we'll see how it looks over the next couple days, but I would anticipate him being out there. Yes. >> Any update on Jesse Bates and Xavier Watson? >> Both guys will be doing a little bit today. >> What do you get um more out of, I guess, when you're evaluating your players? Is it a preseason game or is it the joint practices that you really can see them more since it's two days? you you typically you'd say the joint practices because they're more controlled setting where you can there's things that specifically you want to see. You want to see the red zone, you want to see a two-minute drive. Uh you get to see them in competitive uh drills versus another team. So, I'd say that's probably the answer. Having said that, you know, I think anytime you're under the lights like we were or you're uh in a position where they're keeping score and and it's alive across the board and the quarterbacks are live, that's also extremely valuable. So, I think they're both important to the evaluation process. >> The the run defense Friday, obviously Denver is a really good line. They playing thirds. I don't know who you have that need, but what did you take away from the way that >> Yeah, c certainly can be better. Uh, you know, there's things that you can do schematically uh to try to get an extra hat, you know, in the box and those type of things, but you also want to see how your guys are, you know, defending block. So, it's a balance there defensively where we want to make sure that we're not doing too much scheme and allowing our ability to evaluate our guys versus a good offensive line like you mentioned. Uh, but there's definitely things that we can do schematically. Uh, but in the interim, I think there's it was a good uh evaluation for a lot of our young guys. >> What was your biggest takeaway after watching the offense and their performance on Friday? >> Offense in total? >> Yeah. >> Uh, yeah. Obviously didn't score enough points, didn't move the ball enough, first downs, etc., et, etc. Uh, but that that's why we're working. That's where we are in the in camp. And, uh, I'm I'm looking forward to this work week. I'm looking forward to this practice and then pra practicing versus Indie. Uh, but plenty to clean up. >> With regards to naming a week one starter, is there something that you want to see more from Tua in particular before you name him, or is it down to maybe Mike potentially coming back and getting to see them compete? >> Yeah, nothing. Uh, no, I wouldn't speculate in in that way. I'd just say we're continuing on our process, continuing where we are, keeping uh the main thing, the main thing, which is these practices, the practices this week. I think again will be good for everybody, including the quarterbacks going up against a defense that they haven't seen. So, all of this is important as we get ready for week one. >> Some of these some of these teams do two p two joint practices, some do one. >> It's become common place. How important is it like to find the right fit to do this? Because some of this stuff gets sideways and most times it seems to come off without much of a hitch. How important is the fit? >> Very important. You know, I think philosophically there's different ways of looking at it. I know there's some teams that don't practice against other teams. I believe Andy Reid comes to mind in that regard. Um, some teams do two uh times with with teams. Some teams practice against two different teams but only do it for one day. Uh so there's so many different ways of doing it. Uh last year in Cleveland, we practiced against Carolina for one practice in week one. Then we practiced versus Philly for two days in week two. So there's a so many different ways to do it. I like the rhythm that we have right now u in terms of you know the practicing here in week two versus somebody. to your question though, I think what I'm always looking for is an opponent that we're not playing, number one, and then the schemes should be different. I don't think there's a ton of value when you go up and practice versus somebody where the scheme is so similar than what you've been seeing throughout camp. And then the final piece, which I think is important, is is my relationship with the other head coach. And you know, Shane's somebody that I know well, and I know what he's about. They just practiced last week up in uh New England with Coach Ra. So, uh, it's somebody that I I can partner with and feel really good about the plan that we put together. >> How's Jake Matthews doing after Friday? >> Yeah, doing better. He's not going to practice today, but doing better >> this week, you think he will? >> I I feel good about it. Yes. >> When you have a a player um now they're going to miss most of the season due to a suspension um like James Pierce, do you address the team in that regard? Do you have him address the team? Like, how do you kind of handle that? Overall, >> I'd say generally speaking, I I wouldn't get into the details of those type of things. Those are conversations that we have, you know, as a football team. Uh, as it relates to James, very, very confident with the plan we have, comfortable with what we have, uh, how he's worked to date, and we'll continue to work. >> Thoughts on Dax Strand after you watch the tape back? >> Yeah, always room for improvement. you know, proud of him in the first time out there, you know, and really it's a it's a testament to him from what he was able to do early in camp when he was uh really the the one guy standing there and and took a bunch of reps and then to be able to go out there and and operate and move the offense, score a touchdown, all those things I thought was really good. Having said that, like any rookie, so much to work on and and that's the fun part of working with our rookies and and Jack in this case, uh Jack's got a great attitude. Love how he is in the meeting room. love how he is on on the grass. So, he he wants to get better. >> How late are you comfortable having a starting quarterback, at least in your own mind and internally out there. >> Uh yeah, I'm very comfortable with where we are right now. Um and and that's kind of where I'll I'll leave it. I I feel good about where we are. >> Any update on Mike's health? >> No update. Yeah. >> Doing well. >> You don't expect him to do anything more in India? >> I expect Yeah, India. I expect the same plan that we have. We have seven on seven both days. >> Will you talk to Sten? Did you talk specifically about like kind of some seven on seven periods? >> We did. I for Yes. And that's obviously that's something that they do as well. But just making sure that we have it both days. And then, you know, when you're going somewhere really, we're the guest. Shane's the host. So, whatever he wants to do, we'll do. And he says how many minutes this period is and how many plays that is. And and we'll give our feedback if it's something that we need. But, uh, we're we just plan on being good guests. Kevin, going back to James, with him being here for two weeks and then, you know, he's going to be away from the team, you know, for an extended amount of time. What do those two weeks look like in terms of what your focus is for him, what you want out of him before, you know, kind of break off? >> Uh, continue to work. Yeah. Nothing real special really. Just continue to work. Do do his job every single day, which he's doing. Uh, we'll continue to get him uh, you know, understanding of of this scheme and and getting better on the grass. uh and then you know play him in these games, let him get get those game reps under his belt and then we'll deal with uh the future when it comes. >> You barely missed a sack um in the game of the night. Your thoughts about what you saw from him in game? >> Yeah, had some good rushes. Uh I thought, you know, good to have him back out there and moving around. Um, you know, so much of the pass rush game is applying pressure to the quarterback and when they end in sacks, that's great, but we're also just trying to affect the quarterback period. And then when we get can get those pressures, they turn into sacks. And when they turn into sacks, we want to turn them into sack fumbles. But we focus a lot on on trying to pressure affect that QB. And I thought there were some really good good um examples of that the other night. >> Seen Kendall Daniels wearing the green dot here in practice since, you know, Devine's been down. How do you kind of evaluate the job he's done kind of doing all that job? >> Yeah, from the green dot running the defense has been excellent and and that's you know again I give him credit. I give Barrett RDE credit our coaches in getting him ready but that's kind of who Kendall is and we knew that going into this is in college played multiple positions really is a student of the game uh in that regard but the operation and handling that has been excellent. How much can you take away from Shu's performance when it was kind of like a really small sample size? And I guess how much like does that go into the quarterback bottle when you're evaluating it? >> Obviously, we evaluate everything. I think I've told you guys that before. You evaluate everything that our players do uh on the field, in the meeting rooms, etc. Uh obviously, nine plays the other night. He wants to be better. Our offense wants to be better. Our coaches want to be better in those nine plays, but uh our our focus will be continuing to get ready uh for this season and and not getting too far ahead of ourselves. We want to be where our feet are, try and improve on on some of the small things that that we identify as coaches and correct them this week and then looking forward to a really good work week this practice and those two weeks, two days, excuse me, versus the Colts. >> So, will Cooper Rush then start on Saturday or Josh Strand? >> Haven't gotten there just yet. what you're saying about being where your feet are and evaluating this game. Like obviously you can say a preseason game is nothing like how do you feel like you know more about what your team can do? >> Sure. >> Obviously more than just one one preseason game. Like how do you kind of evaluate and value what what happened? >> Yeah, preseason games are important and listen if they're keeping score you want to win. I mean the competitive nature of how we operate. Uh if there's a drill that's going on we want to win it. So when you go out there and it's offense defense pass rush drill and it's also a pass pro drill for the offense and the tackle's trying to win that rep and the defensive end is trying to win that rep. So the competitive nature never changes. I do think you have to also zoom out and make sure that uh you're you're focusing on on the all the things that that you're trying to work on as a football team. And I think as the as important as that game was the other night, I feel like this practice here at 9:15 is as important. I mean, these these are work opportunities for our guys and uh that's what we'll do. We'll keep our head down and continue to work. >> What goes into your decision on whether to carry two or three quarterbacks each year or maybe each week on a 53 man? >> Everything. I mean, that that's it's I've been a part of different makeups of the roster in that regard, but I think you have to take everything into account and uh look at where your roster is and can you afford the the luxury of keeping those guys? And sometimes you can, sometimes you can't. Uh, but we'll work through all those type of things over the next couple weeks. >> Health, I would assume, is a >> sure part of that equation. >> And and the new rule in terms of the emergency quarterback, how much >> weight do you put in that? I know. >> Yeah, it's uh it's interesting. I mean, there there's certainly some value to it. As you know, >> the times that you get to an emergency quarterback are very very rare. Uh, and I think the the numbers bear that out, but uh we'll work through all of it. Anything else? >> Ken, um, now that the situation with James has reached a resolution, is there anything you'd want to know for fans of what happened, what the allegations, and James and how that represents the team? >> Yeah, I understand the question. But I I would tell you I'm very comfortable in in uh in us sticking to this process, including what the league is is doing in this case. And and I'll I'll make sure that we're in total compliance with those type of things. Uh I think James, for his part on this football team, has done everything that I've asked him to do, everything that his coaches have asked him to do, and we'll just continue to follow the uh you know, the protocols, follow everything that's in place uh from the league. >> Okay. Thanks guys. >> Thank you. [music]

title: Dave Canales: ‘They're going to get another opportunity this week’
text: All right, first of all, big shout out to the Pal Panthers. Just finished off our practice. There's a couple situations I missed throughout the day, so I was able to get a fourth and one on the one. Um was able to get a little bit more second and long situations right there, but there was some some really good tackling and I had my flag just in case, you know, the guys get a little unruly uh sometimes, but it was great uh to be a part of the community and for the guys to show up. It's where it all started. >> Dave, how much will the starters play during joint practice and the preseason game? >> Yeah, I mean, the joint practice, they're going to they're going to get a good load. Uh we've been working with uh Coach Koen, Shane Waldron, one of my friends from Seattle. Uh we've been going back and forth just making sure we have um throw a great practice and hit some different situations, so and then uh the plan is to play them all in the game, too. And then of course it just depends on how we come out of today, how we come out of tomorrow uh to see where guys are at. >> What is your plan with Waller this week? >> Yeah, just right now it's just where is where is his base level of fitness at? He had a great day in our TCP. We just started him that way. Uh got him tired. Uh 117 index today, so a perfect day for that. Um we need it. We're going to Jacksonville this week, so that's a phenomenal opportunity for us and who knows, you know, uh Chicago game one could be like this uh just depending on on what it is that week, so um great reps for us, but you know, getting Darren Waller, um we'll get him a day to recover. We'll ramp it up a little bit more before we throw him out there in the mix. >> Is that why he has a shot Wednesday? >> Uh I I don't think so. Not in that uh setting. Uh it's a pretty combative type of deal, the joint practice. Uh chance that he goes for goes out for Indy um just to get he and Bryce throwing some and doing that, but uh we got to see how he recovers from the work today. We got after him pretty good today. >> Is that why you moved the practice to one to try to take advantage of this heat? >> It was really just a matter of timing. Uh they had a day off after the game, so we needed to look at the film. A lot of stuff to learn, a lot of stuff to grow from from the film, so we took that opportunity early this morning, and that just bumped everything back a couple hours, but I was glad to get in the heat, so. >> How are you feeling about your interior offensive line? Chandler moved to center, um getting Jake some first team reps. >> After watching the film, how do you feel about the way your depth is right now? >> These are guys we know. I'm expecting what we've always gotten out of Chandler and Brady. Uh guys who can step in and fill multiple roles. Um and uh they've they've done a good job. They've done that well, so uh we'll just continue to push those guys, put them in different situations. Chandler's been snapping some. We know Brady can as well. All those things uh will bode really well for them as we start to evaluate for the uh 53. >> When you said Saturday that the starters didn't earn more reps, >> Yeah. >> can you elaborate on that? Because obviously they're eventually going to play in week one, and if they're not playing well, how do you kind of How How do you differentiate I understand you don't want to get anybody hurt, but how do you differentiate that? >> Oh, well. Well, I mean, I wish people could see what's happening in the practice. We're beating the crap out of each other out here. Um last week, we practiced four out of five days, really physical practices, and one of the first times I've had to like step in front of the room and say, "Hey, we need to bring these things back a little bit in some situations because of the tempo and how we're playing uh that way. In the game, the plan was to get no more than three series. The plan was to get them out of the game at the first quarter. I would have liked it to have looked different. I would have liked for the guys to extend drives, get some points, and see what's been happening out here come alive in a game. They're going to get another opportunity to do that this week. >> Hey Dave, in what ways is Bryce Young different than last year? Just in terms of his growth and the progression. >> Just a year older, year more confident, leadership, all those things. >> What What does that mean? What does that look like? Especially when you say leadership. >> All those things, just the whole thing coming together. >> Dave, um Cam Gill, Justyn Ross, uh what's his name? Yeah, uh Justyn's got a sore calf. We're going to image that today, see what that is. Uh came out of the game okay, uh but then things kind of start to present themselves a little bit in the days after. So, we're going to check that out. Cam had a shoulder. He finished the game with the shoulder. Really sore today. We had him on the side just getting his conditioning. He will practice on Wednesday and we expect him to play this week. >> I know the Bears activated Traveon who had that same similar injury as Iffy. >> Yes. >> I understand everybody's got different. >> Any update though on Iffy? >> Iffy's doing great. He had another great day on the field. He's going in right now to get his lift in. He's progressing really well. Again, every case is different. We just got to take it with the information that we have. Consult our experts, consult the surgeons, all those things, get re-imaging and make sure we feel confident before we put him back out there. >> Is he ruled out for week one? >> Uh I I don't know. I don't I wouldn't say that necessarily. But I do know he's progressing really well. >> Haynes King? >> Yeah, right now week to week still. He won't make it back this week. We'll re-evaluate him for the Houston week. >> And then Will Levis? >> Yeah, Will left the game with some groin tightness. Um we were hoping for the best. It turned out to be the best that imaging came out pretty clean. Still really sore today. He had a really big week. Was feeling it. Was able to push through, show up in the game and take a bunch of reps, but we're going to get a little bit more more back into the tank for him before we put him back out there. >> What do you want to see from the team as you head into this this joint practice on Wednesday against Jacksonville? >> Just what I've been seeing every day in practice here. The physicality is show up. Our style of football. That's been the standard. That's what it's looked like. I just want to see that that consistency to happen in the in the practice. The competition will elevate some. Getting new fresh faces to go against. Different schemes, different style of fronts, different style of offenses. Those types of things. But just seeing our guys execute and play with our type of physicality. >> How have preseason games changed for you now knowing like this is what you're going to be doing during regular season not having to call plays? >> Uh yeah. It just it changes the focus of of what I'm looking for and um trying to be able to take advantage of situations and see if I can, you know, talk to the officials and get more information uh than I could in the past when I was calling it on the offensive side. A little freer when I'm on the defensive side, of course, but um now it's just those types of communication and really I would say the biggest piece in the last two games is just the immediate feedback I'm able to give players as they come off the field. As guys are subbing in and out when the drive finishes, I'm able to go right to somebody and capture some technical part. It could be his approach on a tackle. It could be the way that he was going down to the ground carrying the ball. Um it could be the quarterback extending the play and keeping his eyes downfield. Whatever those I could just give coaching points more immediately and and really take advantage of that small feedback window that's the most important. >> In the past, would you do all of that or like relay that message or would you take it for next time or >> I was usually, you know, on the headset talking to a position coach. Make sure you talk to so-and-so. It looked like this or that. Now I can just go address them directly for myself. So, they know that I'm watching. I care about what's happening so that they can refocus and improve on the next drive. >> Expectations or what what are your hopes, I guess, for for Waller and what what he might bring? >> Uh pass threat, what he's been doing. Um versatility, he can play him like a tight end, he can play him like a receiver. He's huge. I mean, just, you know, standing with him out there, he's all a 6'6 and a half. Um he's lean. He can run. All those things. Um it's a unique element, you know, that he brings to whatever offense he's been a part of and so um the goal is to just throw him into that room, challenge that room, and see see which guys want to elevate and create that role for Bryce. >> Did he look like he showed up >> He looks He looks like he's is phenomenal shape. Yeah, and uh I mean, he he was leaking out here. This is a different kind of 117 index than Vegas is where he lives. And so, he mentioned that, you know, he's soaking wet, but it was a good opportunity to just kind of see where he's at. >> Dave, we saw Clod Brom with the ones. Where does that competition stand out after that second film out of B and Trevion Williams from Saturday? >> Yeah, those guys are neck and neck. They're both showing great things. Trevion has played a little bit more ball with this group, but Clodius has to play over the last couple of years. And we're challenging both, you know, you saw what Devin does. You know, we want the guy next to him to fit the same play style sideline to sideline showing up angry. And that's going to be the the determining factor is who ends up playing with that type of play style that we're looking for. Devin setting a great example made some amazing plays on Saturday. And we want that whole group to be cohesive that way. >> Thank you, coach. >> Thank you. >> [snorts] [music]

title: Darren Waller addresses the media for the first time as a Carolina Panther | Carolina Panthers
text: Darin, how did all this come about? When did you first hear from the Panthers? Why was it important to to agree to terms on the day that you did? >> Uh I heard from the Panthers Wednesday morning when my agent called me. Uh I was just going to wake up and go train and got a call. And I was like, waiting on anybody that offered me a job, I was going to play, you know, like so I'm grateful the Panthers offered me the opportunity to come play. And yeah, I'm excited to be here. >> Where are you at? I mean, you were productive last year. I know you missed some time, but were you a little surprised that you had to wait as long as you did? >> Um not really. I know people take into account uh where I'm at age-wise, um durability concerns, rightfully so. Um so I understand those are things people take into to account when they're mitigating risk, but um yeah, I was just allowing the process to be what it was. Sometimes it you know, it can be uh like damn, I'm doing all this work since the day after the Super Bowl, you know, like when is it going to happen, but you know, and so that's kind of the name of the game. Uh I'm new to this free agent situation, but it is what it was and I'm grateful that it happened in the time that it did. >> You haven't been here long, but what are your impressions so far? >> Um I mean, I'm been welcomed by all the support staff, coaches, players. Uh everybody's been kind to me since I got here. Uh I'm just getting introduced to the tight end group. Uh I'm really impressed by how well they know their assignments, how well they approach in practice, how hard they work, how composed they are. Uh I think it's going to be a really good group that's going to help me get acclimated, help me learn how to do things, how how the whole team does things around here. So I'm I've been impressed by the culture so far. >> You said this is your first time through free agency. I'm assuming this is also your first time. Was this your first time just coming into the team in the middle of training camp? >> Uh yes, at this point, yeah. >> and then what's your mindset coming in kind of in the middle of a team that's already somewhat established? >> Yeah, um I mean the success teams want to have in this league is they it it starts getting built in April. And really February, your individual training as a team is April to June. That's very valuable time uh that I missed and uh you know, for me, I just got to take it as like this is where I'm at in my journey and do the best that I can each and every day. I may not be where anybody else is with as far as how they know the offense and they're adapting with everything that they're asking us to do, but in time I believe my ability to learn and adapt fast and uh feel like I could, you know, just take it every day and earn a role out here. >> Since you are coming in so late, what have they communicated to you as far as your role within this offense moving forward? >> Uh I think roles are roles are earned once you start practicing, uh once you get out on the field. Um and I think it's really just bringing value to the offense in a multitude of ways. Um of course, you know, there'll be opportunities to make plays in the passing game, but everything's asked of me in the run game, things asked of me just, you know, leadership-wise, passing wisdom and experience on, but as of right now it's just getting myself ready to be out there practice and uh just learn offense, learn my assignments and just keep keep it simple for me. >> Darren, why did you ultimately come back to the NFL last year? And then what does this still drive? I really feel like there was uh you know, something greater that was pushing me back into the game. Uh I felt like there was a lot left and I feel like at the time that I was on the field last year, I felt like it was really clear to me that I still had a lot left and uh and in taking that into account, I felt like it was super important for me to respect the process from like I said in February up until this point as far as my body and being way more callous this year showing up to training camp than I was last year. So, uh it's really just about playing the game, uh enjoying each and every opportunity I have now. You know, I don't know how much time will be left, but I'm grateful that I have an opportunity to play this season. I'm super excited about it. >> What did you do? Dave said you're in great shape coming in today. What did you do to kind of keep that callous up? >> Uh well, I mean, last year going into camp, my first thought of playing football was mid-June, late June. Uh but I as soon as the season ended last year, I was like, "I'm getting started the the day after the Super Bowl and doing everything that's necessary throughout that whole process, week in week out." I took a week trip to Iceland, it's the only week I took off. So, yeah, just night and day from last year to this year. >> Darren, you mentioned the age. Do do you feel like though that that year that you were gone, you know, the year that you you didn't have the wear and tear? And how how do you factor that into the equation? >> Yeah, no, I think that's definitely an element of it for sure. I think through my training I was able to this year to get back to places I feel like explosive wise, top speed wise, getting out of routes just as good as I have at any point in my career. So, that's very encouraging, you know what I'm saying? Cuz a lot of guys not only don't have this opportunity just deep into their career, but but yeah, just to be able to move the way that I'm moving at my age, I feel like it's a blessing and just continue to do everything I can. Lot longer warm-ups, activations, you know? But it's it's worth it. >> Darren, we haven't been able to kind of meet Darrell Bevell at all, but what did you learn from him and what do you view him as kind of a play designer, passing game mind in the NFL? >> Yeah, I mean, he's been around for a long time. I mean, I didn't even know he was in Detroit earlier in his career. He's see all these places, I thought he was in Seattle. Just a wealth of knowledge as far as like, you know, fundamentals. Like he's heard every tip, everything. Like everybody every product you see out on the field comes from having a good base fundamental wise. I feel like that's where he comes in allowing guys to take those fundamentals to then go into your practice reps and your game reps and being at ease because how you do things is so much in your muscle memory that you can just go out and play football and play free. Cuz if you're not playing free and having those things in your muscle memory, it's going to be tough. You're going to be moving a tick slower and every tenth of a second matters in the NFL. So, I think him just all that wealth of experience as far as like the basics and then we can build on that. But yeah, just there's there's so many things. >> When you came back last year, were you surprised that that you were still able to, you know, create openings, create create space and >> Got some balls. >> Um so my first game was like the fourth week last year. I was before the game I was like I had some limited practices cuz cuz I got hurt right right when I got to camp and I was like I don't know how this is going to go. Like I'm this is my first game in almost 2 years. And the first third down of the game got a first down and it was like it's all right, I know what this feels like and I can still separate like just that quick and that was an amazing feeling, you know, cuz like I said to be in your 30s and have opportunities to to do that, to even come back from retiring, like that's a it's a blessing to be able to just even have that opportunity. So just try to build on that. >> Any questions of Bryce? >> Uh they're super composed, man. They're I mean, you see the the heat out here, so many elements. There's the portions of defense, the practice of the defense was uh really getting after him in the in the early part, but you don't see uh any type of emotional fluctuation from him. And I feel like that's the kind of composure you need from the quarterback position. I feel like different arm angles and throws, pushing the ball down the field, um weathering adversity from what I saw today. I I was very impressed by him. >> Uh Aaron, going back to Steve's question. So week five was against the Panthers and it was your second game back and as you said, 2 years. Was it uh and you obviously had a great game. Was that emotional at all for you? What what if you could take us back to that game against the Panthers, what was it like? >> Um it was kind of surreal uh cuz like I said, like the first game it was like um a few targets and it's like I've always prided myself on being efficient with the number of opportunities that I'm getting as opposed to saying I need this many opportunities. Uh so it's like then going into the Carolina game in the first half and it's like okay, like third down conversion. Okay, here comes a couple more completions and it's like you're not even really aware of the the stats or anything, but it's like I feel like I'm just almost doing what I want to do out here. Um which is like, you know, you have I haven't played in two haven't played in 2 years, it's like it's just hard to process all that but it's like just really trying to get back to a place of gratitude that I can go out on the field and be impactful for my team. With that time off so just trying to just appreciate the fact that that's a possibility for me. >> There were a couple of times there were two more there were two times when the tight ends would come off during team drills we saw you talking to was that giving them advice picking their brain on the playbook here what were those conversations? >> A mix of things I always like to be the first person to go one of the first people to go congratulate somebody when they make a good play so that's one thing uh reading the play sheet to them so that so they can stay locked in on the play and what they need to hear um asking them what certain words mean cuz the script sheet looks like Mandarin Chinese right now but soon it'll be uh something that I understand a lot more but yeah just asking them questions asking communication cuz there's a lot of communication with the O line and there's things you got to see as far as stunts on the fronts and coverages rotating so it's like it's a constant dialogue amongst the group I feel like at any given time anybody can be a student and a teacher so just trying to stay in that mindset. >> Jared last one last week Mari of course who knew you from Vegas said that you have a different type of skill set for that position do you feel like that size speed combos is something that this group could really benefit from? >> Um I mean I think there's already guys that have those skills in the room right now I think everybody in the room has some unique skills that they bring to the table and I feel like I do as well and I think together we'll create a group that really brings a lot of value to the offense this season. >> Thanks Jared. >> Good luck good to meet you guys. >> [music] [music]

title: Luke Fortner: 'Protect Bryce is in the job description' | Carolina Panthers
text: Luke >> How do you think you guys' interior offensive line performed against Buffalo and where do you think you guys can improve? >> Yeah, I think we didn't didn't perform well. I think that's clear from the tape and the stats and and kind of how we did in those first few plays there. Uh I think we just got to improve playing as a group and I know it's cliche and coach speak and it's coach speak for a reason, right? Uh as you guys know in this league, uh you hope for no injury, but injury happens and no matter who runs out there on on game day we got to be able to play well together. So, I think uh more and more reps and we've gotten, you know, the extra game and you know, that thankfully that was only preseason one. We got plenty of time, so more reps. >> We've seen you out there kind of take charge and somebody's kind of threatened an offensive player. Uh where does that come from? What What is there like a certain big brother, fatherly sort of protective thing that you have going on or is it just, "Hey, my Leave Leave my teammates alone."? >> Yeah, I think like I said, we got an extra week of camp and we're we're running into each other for an extra week and so I think uh now that we get in these preseason games, we'll start to to hit other people. It'll feel a little more, you know, "Hey, we are on the same team." you know, cuz those first few weeks, right, you're pitted against each other cuz you're trying to compete and get better and that's just the way it goes and so uh yeah, tempers flare, but uh we're all teammates and it's all love for everybody. >> Nick as he mentioned it, think of Alex as a you are justice seeker, right? >> [laughter] >> I am a justice seeker. >> I mean, do do you I mean, would that fair Is that a fairly accurate description? >> Oh man, that's a that's a crazy uh uh uh you know, I'm I'm out there and you know, if one of my teammates gets hit, I want to be there for him and that's kind of the that's kind of the deal. Whether that's, you know, within the confines of practice or not or whatever, you know, that's coach's call and you know, and he after he said, "Hey, appreciate you guys, you know, protecting your brothers, but you know, you can't do that on game day." And so, that's the end of that. >> In a couple of those occasions, you were appeared to be coming to Bryce's defense. Is that a natural center quarterback deal? >> Yeah, that's like on the the job description. It's like, play ball, protect Bryce, you know, all that is all kind of included, so. >> Did you get to see the film on the belly-to-belly suplex? Check out the form on that. [laughter] >> No, no, no, no film of that. They cut that out for us. >> Speaking of Bryce, what have you what have you learned about him so far? >> I think just the the type of person he is and the way he works is very admirable and he he's you know, in first, out late and you know, the way he approaches his business is just you know, it inspires confidence in the rest of the team. >> Do you think there will be like emotions for you going back to Jacksonville this week or is it something that you'll just think about once you get there? >> Yeah, I can't wait to see those guys, man. I I love all love for everyone in that building and all those players and all that and they're they're a good team, a good defense, so it's going to be a great practice, but all love for them. >> How does 9:15 a.m. Jacksonville humidity compare to 2:00 p.m. Charlotte? >> Uh I I don't know. Maybe, you know, I don't know if the grass is greener. It felt pretty hot today, but I'm sure it's it's still just as heavy as I remember down there. >> How do you approach joint practices in terms of like importance and intensity? >> Yeah, I think they're super important. I think they're almost as important as those preseason games. I think getting out there versus another live defense and you haven't gone against them, you know, you get to spend a little time studying them pre you know, pre-practice and everything, but to be able to go go out there and get those live reps is just as important as any of those preseason games. >> Anything else? >> Are you the oldest? >> [cough] >> I am the oldest sibling, yes. I have a younger sister and a younger brother, yeah. Thanks, guys. >> [music] [music] >> Woo.

title: Panthers Training Camp Live | August 17th Practice | Carolina Panthers
text: Well, we welcome you to training camp live. Third time we're doing this this preeason. Anise Shro, former Panthers great and defensive back Kurt Coleman. Now Kurt, I always think about this when we talk about the preseason. We're football starved. It's such a small sample size. Football is such a week-to-eek sport that we take what we see and we draw large conclusions. Having said all that, you played in those games. There are some things that are very real from the preseason. When you kind of zoom out, what do you value that happens and takes place in a preseason game? I think the the more important thing that I value, not just from a game, I think when you talk about just preseason in general, is what kind of culture and identity do you want to be? So regardless the coaches, you'll hear coach Canales and really any coach say it doesn't matter if it's the starters, the second team, third team, it that does not matter. The product should be the product and who we look like should be the same. I think that's my biggest takeaway no matter what game I'm watching is what is our identity on offense, on defense, and special teams. Now, the product's not going to always look the same. When you have your starters out there, you're expecting a certain level of performance, execution, almost that eliteness, and everything else. Sometimes if you're dealing with a rookie, you're like, "Okay, he made a mistake." So, there's some forgiveness. But everything that from a body of work from 50,000 ft high, you should say, "This is the Panthers that we look to expect to see from start to finish throughout the game, but also through the entirety of the season." I'm expecting a team that a they know how to win. We've seen that in critical situations. We'll talk about that later in the segment as far as uh the two-minute segments of driving a team down the field or trying to get a team stopped in a crucial situation. We've seen that out of this team, but in those other moments when you just flip on the TV, what will you see? I think that's what this preseason I think that's where coach Canalis and crew, they're going to say, "Look, we need to get back to who we are from start to finish, from first team to set last team. That's the team that we want to see." >> Yeah. And you look at game one and game two against Arizona, starters didn't play. Uh backups played very well. In fact, the Panthers scored on six of their last seven drives. The starters got three series on offense in the game against the Bills on Saturday. Three three and outs. There were two missing offensive linemen. We'll talk about all that later. There's also a new addition today. Darren Waller signing. There's a little more depth now to the tight end room. Uh we'll see if he practices, but uh his signing went official today. One area defensively where the Panthers invested in the offseason was in bolstering the pass rush. They gave a lot of money to Jaylen Phillips. Kurt, uh, from Saturday's game, if there was any indication that his money well spent, he had one sack and if it wasn't 65 240 Josh Allen, he probably would have had another >> and he might have had a few more and pressures that come along with the things that bring I think that is the money that you could say is best well spent. I think the way he knows how to attack the offensive lineman and he sets up his games really well. I think that's the cool thing is because he has the ability to speed rush, but then if you watch on this sack right here, he comes on a counter, he fakes up and then comes underneath.
