What can you two do for this offense this coming season? >> Everything, man. Everything. Me and Denzel Me and Denzel, you know, we we compliment each other so well, um him being 6'4, you know, the bigger guy me being 5'11, you know, um me being 5'11, you know, I can do, you know, all of the underneath things, all of the all of the intermediate things, so yeah. >> You've seen Denzel, you've seen some others fielding punts at practice, and obviously you guys were returning the kick. Do you have a sense yet of how often you are you'll be back there returning punts? Is it going to be an every time thing? Is it going to be sort of a mix based on what your usage is in the offense, or have you not really gotten that >> I mean, I personally haven't really gotten that far, but any chance I am able to affect the game in the in the punt return game, you know, I will I will always be up for that challenge, so. >> Anything surprising you in your first NFL game with the long deal preparation and things? and you know, if you were not not expecting but just kind of stood out to you in your first NFL >> Yeah, anything surprise me? Uh, how many TV timeouts there is. >> you doing during those breaks like? >> Just um talking about teammates. Laughing and stuff, dancing and stuff, yeah. You know, being me. >> I know you like to ball in your hands. So, how much do you enjoy being involved with end arounds, jet sweeps, and even like bubble screens? That kind of thing to get you the ball. >> Yeah, I always enjoy, you know, any chance, you know, any chance that I am able to any chance that I am able to any chance that I am able to receive the ball, you know, I am going to always be happy. You know, um you know, um it doesn't matter the way that I can get the ball in my hands, you know, um it's just about, you know, getting the ball honestly. >> When you were drafted, you know, your separation is supposed to be one of your powers and speed, quickness, but catching the ball in traffic, here at camp, had no problem with that. Do you think that went underrated in your college scouting? >> Yeah, I felt like I felt like it did kind of go underrated a little bit. I think that I was one of the top college guys whenever it came to con- contested catches, um you know, I take very much pride on if the quarterback throws me the ball, it's my ball, you know, I can't I can't I can't never let a defender dictate whether if I catch the ball or not. >> KC, on Thursday, you're going to have an opportunity to go up against the Bills defense. We won't be talking to you between now and then, so I wanted to ask you about that now. But, you'll have a chance to go up against I'm sure their starters for like a long period of time and really test your skills against some of the best defenders in the NFL. How much are you looking forward to that? >> I'm looking forward to, you know, always, you know, uh Like I said before, I love to compete. Um I love competing. I love grinding. So, whenever they come here, you know, um I'm just ready to work. >> Kickoff returns are a little different skill set than punt returns. Are you getting reps there? Would you like to do that? >> Yeah, um I've seen I've seen some uh reps at uh at kickoff return, you know, um I haven't really did it too much, but again, um if there's anything that I can do to help the team win, you know, I'll do it. >> How's the hangtime of the ball, is it? >> As a punt returner, you're trying to track the ball but knowing where those defenders are coming at you. So, how's the hangtime of the >> Um I mean, right now, you know, right now, you know, I've done built up so much confidence back there, you know, it's not really as difficult as it as it um seems. It's not really as difficult as it seems, but you know, I always have to keep my head up on a swivel. >> All right. Thank you, Taysom Hill. Thank >> Thank you, guys. >> I saw him one day >> I ain't saying anything, Yo. >> So there we have seen you kind of mix it up with the offensive line and kind of go at it but Spencer kind of gave iron sharpens iron. What's that been like? >> No, I don't think it goes over the edge at all. I think fighting is necessary when you get to football. You have to have that, you know, that edge. I talk crazy. I'm very disrespectful when it comes to uh the way I compete. Especially, you know, when I uh try to drive my teammates to another level. So I wouldn't expect him any less than to uh retaliate cuz that's the type of player he is. He he's a very uh magnificent player. And to go on against him, you know, he's gotten so much better in these past couple weeks. It's What is it been a month? I don't you know, camp's been running all along. But, you know, in the time he's we've been together he's gotten so much better. And you know, because he's getting better he's getting to the point where I'm starting to learn things from him. I'm starting to learn a little bit about my tendencies and what he's picking up on. So it's making me a better player as well. >> So what did he show you by not backing down then Saturday practice? >> That that boy got heart. I mean, a lot of guys would uh go into a situation, you know, against me, against you know, top edges in the league and stuff and kind of back down, kind of like, you know, be a little nervous, a little bit timid. But no, he he has never uh he's never shown that. >> Along those lines, I know you mentioned during the during the game that you kind of challenged him not to give up any sacks or pressures. So after sort of being able to watch it back a little bit, what was the consensus on, you know, how how he performed in the game last Saturday? >> Yeah, no, he did he did good. There's a couple things I want to talk to him, you know, off air and everything like that about uh you know, fixing just a couple little small things. But for the most part, he dominated. I mean, he ain't giving up anything like that. I mean, he showed exactly the reason that the Browns took him where they did. I mean, he he's a great player. >> Your your obviously that your your style of leadership but have you seen other guys on this team on the defense kind of embrace that too and maybe follow your lead when it comes to being aggressive and and being dominant out there on the field against the offense >> Yeah, 100%. I mean, when you see uh the way I attack the game, I'm very physical, very uh violent, very loud, very uh expressive is a very good word to use for it. And you see everybody else's personality start to mesh. I mean, you know, with a lot of people when you're mixing with a lot of different people, you can't show your full personality on the field. I have no problem with that. But when you see somebody like me go out there yelling and screaming, you have no problem showing your true character. You see everyone's uh personality start to flourish on the field. >> How much are you looking forward to going against Josh Allen and that Bills' in practice Thursday? >> Oh, there's I've been waiting for this for a minute. I think joint practices are the most important thing during this, you know, preseason time frame cuz you know, a lot of teams don't uh play their starters in those games. So, going up against, you know, Dion Dawkins, Josh Allen, these elite dudes that they got, you know, the everybody across the board, running backs, tight ends, wide receivers. Like they they got some dogs across the board. So, I'm excited to just get back there and get some work in. >> You mentioned Dion Dawkins before. You got some kind of professional relationship with him at all or you just respect him as a player? >> I respect him as a player. I mean, my rookie year, me and him we played each other and it was a it was a good game. We had gotten each other's ass, you know, it was a loud and violent. It got to the point that we were making dumb errors on both sides. I'm jumping offsides, he's false starting because like we were just in each other's head to that point. So, it's going to be good to uh go up against him and see how much uh I've sharpened my sword. >> Have you sacked Josh Allen >> No, I got him close, but that that dude's a uh that's a hard person to sack. I mean, when you when you go up against somebody that's your size and your weight, it's uh you got to hit him a little bit different. >> Jae, there's a lot of young players you look up to on each side of the ball. Who are some of >> Yeah, I mean I I think uh future's a important to look at, but I'm more so focused on the present before anything else. I think we got a lot of talent, but talent's just that if you don't put in the work to you know pull the most out of it. I think we got a lot of people that can do amazing things, but we need those amazing things today. We don't need them 2 3 4 years down the line. We need them today. >> Have you always talked as much on the field or in the practice or games that you know? >> Yeah, believe it or not I start to calm down during games. Yeah. I I talk a lot during games, but more so it's more so like just a self help myself up help self preservation more than anything. >> So, where does this the whatever need or desire to talk as much as you do on the practice field? Where >> I think it just hypes everyone up. I mean, think about it like you have 10 practices in a row. You get tired, exhausted, you don't really want to go out there and practice no more. And then you know you go you go through individual warm-ups, you're exhausted, meetings all day, then you go up and you got some dude who just got to the team like 3 weeks ago yelling in your face saying you're not enough, you can never block him in front of a building or facility full of fans. You like you going to turn yourself up and that's going to turn everybody else up and it helps to bring everybody to another level. >> How many sacks do you think get left on called during practice? >> You know, we got to run through the plays, man. That's how I'm answering that. >> Um who talks more, you or Quincy? >> It depends on the aspect of it all. I mean, if you talking like on the field it's probably me, but if you talk about like on a you know team situation team bonding trip it's probably Quincy. >> So, it's my understanding that the Browns are trying to sign Zadarius and that it could happen even as soon as today. What would it mean to you to have a guy like that? I know we talked about this with Jeremiah a little bit, but what would it mean to you to have a veteran like that on the team? >> Yeah, it's a similar aspect of as it was with Clowney, you know, having that vet presence is something that you know I I look forward to having you know, somebody that I've never had before kind of be at that level above me where they can teach me a little bit more. They see a little bit more of the game and everything like that cuz you know, those old dogs, they know a lot more than anybody like me. >> And then just to go back to the joint practices, like how valuable is it for you guys up front to I mean to your point about keeping everyone amped up with your talking, just to see that different competition and get a chance to go up a different O-line. >> Yeah, I mean that you think about the pad days or the days we have against each other, it's so much held back cuz we don't want to hurt your teammates. You didn't You don't chip the guard's hip. You don't run fully through the tackle. You don't, you know, light up a running back or, you know, even just you know, you're still not going to touch the quarterback. But you don't do all that extra stuff. But you know, when you're in a joint practice, I don't really like hold back as much. Like it's more so, okay, I'm going to take your hip. I'm not going to do anything dirty, but we're going to play it like it's a full game. The only body that The only person that's not off limits or that's off limits is the quarterback. >> So, you know, you played three snaps against Chicago, I think. Probably won't play a game. Oh, so that means So, is the joint practice enough to satisfy your thirst to hit somebody else? >> Uh it'll be it'll it'll get me a little bit good. It'll tide me over till uh the first game. >> And with the Rams, McVay doesn't play anybody. Did you play in preseason >> No. No. I mean not till Saturday. >> Okay, this is the tackle that you've gone against the most that talks the most. And is it almost a little more unsettling going against a guy that doesn't talk at all? >> It's probably Deion. And uh no, not [clears throat] really. I mean when when people don't talk, I take it as like you can't mentally handle it. Like I feel like you've already broken down if you don't say anything at all. Just take it. >> Hey, what about quarterbacks on the same preseason that have been hit before or nothing changed? From your perspective as a rusher, you know you can, you know, put a little bit of a little bit of How do you see quarterbacks change once they go from taking the the red jersey off so now they're they can get >> Their eyes get a little bit wider. Cuz I mean you know, in the presea- like then in the preseason during those little practices and everything like that, we can't touch you. You know what I mean? You're you're you're blind side's is that. It's a blind side. You don't have to worry about it as much or anything like that. Like you might know oh he might he's coming that way but you you're not fully alert on it. When that real season comes like they they are a little bit more alert. They're a little bit more antsy, especially those first couple games. >> You're into it now. What's biggest difference about this camp to the first couple you were with with the Rams? Does something stand out? >> The the load. It's a lot heavier of a load because we have a lot more work to do. You know, we got a lot more we got to make up with a bunch of younger players on the roster, a bunch of people that still have a things to prove to themselves, to their organization, to you know, their families and everything like that. So it's just a it's a heavier load mentally on you and physically. >> I hope you don't mind me asking this. Mary Kay Henry >> How happy do you find yourself here? A lot of people thought that you were going to be distraught leaving the Rams. You don't seem distraught but how happy do you find yourself here so far in this year? >> Yeah, I like it. I like it a lot. I mean, you know, in California it doesn't really rain that much. So yeah, I was outside yesterday just enjoying the rain, sitting on the back porch just like taking deep little breaths, seeing deer run around. I didn't do anything like that. It was cool. I I like it here. But it's I wasn't really distraughted at all like after the fact after the kind of the initial shock wore off. I was like all right, cool. Like I'm a Brown. Let's work. And I love the organization. Especially the first day of camp, you see all the fans out there. I'm like damn. Like these are my fans. Like the fans was they was lit out there. They was they was lively and they it's they bleed orange and brown. I love it out here. >> Just to go back to the load part of it. I know you had 15 tackles have been pretty beat up. I guess is there any concern for you about how those guys might bounce back these last handful weeks here? >> Yeah, no. I mean, the load's heavy but Monk Coach Monk, he takes good very good care of us. He makes sure like oh yeah, if you're feeling this, we're going to lighten up for you a little bit today. You know, hey you can't do this, you can't do that. And yeah, we got D-tackles fall out and everything like that. But they're going to be good. I'm not worried about anything like that. They take care of their business. They're in the treatment room as we speak taking care of themselves, getting themselves healthy. I don't need anybody this week. I don't need anybody next week. I don't need anybody when we get to Jacksonville. >> How are you going to feel about snow? >> Oh, I like it. I got my coats ready. Thank you. >> Thanks, sir. >> you, sir.

title: Cowboys Players on Von Miller, Joint Practice vs Saints, & More | Player Interviews
text: How do you learn to appreciate joint practices knowing you don't really play in the preseason? >> Yeah, I think they're huge. Um like you said, the preseason games, a lot of those young guys getting to work, but that joint practices, um you know, it's a lot of their ones. It's usually their starting defense going against our starting offense. That's where we get a good read of, you know, what we're looking like, what we're feeling like, what we need to clean up. And um you know, we had that one against the Rams and we came out firing. There's a lot of things we need to clean up. Um but like I said earlier, it's a good tell. >> You got a lot of young tight ends in your room. How do you think they've been progressing? >> I think they've been great. You know, um Zach Kuntz coming in, you know, essentially getting thrown into the fire. Um he's handled that really well. And then Trey and DJ, the two rookies, you know, they've they're coming in. They're they're soaking in all the information they can get and then they're really applying it to the field. Um it was really great to see both them get out there on the field. And um you know, I'm just excited to see how they go throughout the rest of camp. >> How's your camp been so far? How would you describe it? >> Um you know, I I'm not comfortable. Um I never want to be comfortable. Um there's a lot I want to do. I wouldn't say I'm where I want to be. Um there's a lot I know that I can do and there's a there's a spot that I want to be at. And I know I'm not there yet. And you know, that's the point of camp is get get better each and every day, each and every practice. And you know, that's all I'm trying to do is just keep trying to hone in on my game and and and really perfect my craft. >> How do you get there? >> I think it's just consistency. You know, not getting complacent. One of my favorite quotes is complacency kills. Um as soon as you get comfortable, as soon as you get, "Oh, I don't need to do this." or you know, "I don't need to work as hard." or "I don't need to lock in on this walk-through." or something like that, that's when it that's when it starts to hurt you. So, just being consistent in everything I do and um the little things, focusing a lot more on the little things. >> Reuben joined you as not playing in the preseason game. What have you seen from him just in terms of his development and where he's at right now? >> Yeah, I mean, I've I knew him in college. Um he's always been the guy who's going to put his nose down and work. And that just proves that to the kind of player he is, the kind of guy he is. Um he's done that ever since he he's gotten here. And you know, him coach giving him, you know, the green light, the the ball cap on Saturday is just a testament to how hard he works, what he does on the field, off the field, and how he approaches this game. >> Why is the leadership council important to you? >> Yeah, I think uh I think it's really important because, you know, there's a saying it's the best teams police themselves. Um it's one thing to, you know, have have a coach or have somebody saying it, but when you got a guy who cares enough, a brother who cares enough to tell you and and to hold you accountable, but at the same time who knows you and knows how to approach you on certain topics, that's what it's all about. And and that's how you create that brotherhood, that's how you create that strong brotherhood. And that's all we're trying to do. >> What kind of memories do you have of Von Miller just watching him as a player and obviously maybe going up against him since then? >> Yeah, I've I've blocked him a couple times. Um Yeah, I'm excited. I'm always excited when we get a new addition. So, it should be a good one. >> Rashaan, just talk about uh the reaction to the Von Miller news. You know, what kind of excitement you have to be able to work with and learn from a future Hall of Famer like him. >> Oh yeah, man, it's an honor and privilege. Um you know, getting a chance, like you said, to work with a future Hall of Famer. Um you know, I've been able to work out with him um in the off season, got to pick his brain. So, it's going to be completely different, you know, having him, you feel me, right beside me, able to, you know, get tips and things like that on hand. But just talking about what he's able to bring to the defense, bring to the defensive line, man, more pressure, more confidence, and more swagger. Um a lot more guys that you need to account for. So, happy, excited. >> Is it amazing to see what he's still capable of this deep into his career? >> Oh yeah, man, uh not surprised. Uh that's Von Miller, like I said, we talking about a future Hall of Famer, man. And uh he puts up numbers uh on a consistent and that's what Hall of Famers do. >> Game respects game. So, what do you as a fellow pass rusher truly appreciate about his game that media and fans would never recognize never having played the position? >> Yeah, uh you know, just how smart he is, man. He's a true football player. Understand the formations, understand how to get his opponent, you know, to play inside, you know, his will. Basically, everything he want to do, man. So, this is his approach to the game. >> Everyone talked about what the Rams have done in the off-season, their acquisitions. What message do you think they're sending? What message do you think they sent today by getting a guy like >> Um today, beginning of, you know, the off-season, every move that the Cowboys did is the series about winning and winning right now. >> What can you I mean, obviously, you're waiting to see what what kind of teammate he is here, but Shady talked about just how he'll help help so much on and off the field. What have you got to know about him as a person working out with him and getting to know him as a guy? >> Oh, yeah, man. You know, he he's a leader. He's a leader, man. And he's a he's a coach. So, being able to have a guy that, you know, played at a high level, won Super Bowls, Defensive Player of the Year, things like that. Um you know, just being able to pick his brain, things like that, man. That's all you need. So, having a guy like that to the team and to the room is great. >> How have you seen Maliek grow since the first day he got here in the off-season to where you are right now? >> Yeah, my boy Maliek. Just his confidence, man. His confidence and his belief that he could beat the guy across from him. And him being consistent in his technique. Maliek at this point of camp, he understands, you know, what he needs to do to beat the offensive lineman, what he needs to do to get in great position in the run and pass. And just making sure that he's pushing to be consistent, but all I've been seeing is daily growth, man. And when he has made one mistake, he's been, you know, next day coming in and not making the same mistake. So, he's been getting better and better every day. So, I really can't wait for the season. >> Have you seen a little bit of yourself in him when you were a young player? Just the growth of, you know, worry about what happened on the Tuesday cuz you got another practice. >> Yeah, no, just really the hunger, man. The hunger for the information, man. Not scared to ask the quote-unquote dumb questions. You know, even you know, in in a practice, man, he feels like he could have been better at the rep. You know, I'm watching every play. So, he's coming to the sideline, you know, where I could be better. And then him going out next time and doing it, man. It's great It's great for him. Kudos, but uh you know, everything's clicking at the right time for him. >> Tyrese Wheat had a really good game Saturday night. Looked like um this is second swim through Dallas, but what are you seeing from him and just in the past few weeks where has he stepped up? >> Yeah, man. Uh he's been the same person um you know, from the off season, man. Just head down, um ready to work, and ready for his opportunity, man. Uh guy like that, when you see him have success in the game, it's not surprising because he comes out here. You see him in individual going balls to the wall. You see him in team making big plays. So, you know, what we always talk about, you know, practice to game, and that's what he does. >> I know you thought a lot of that rusher group that you guys have, but adding Von to it now with you, Donovan, and Malachi, and all the other guys, what do you think of what you guys can be as a group this season? >> Oh, yeah. Uh talking about us as just as a unit, man, we could be great. Um the sky's already the limit. Um adding him is only going to make anything better. So, like I said, uh you know, having a guy that won Super Bowls, that won, you know, Defensive Player of the Year, things like that, that played at a high level for a very long time, uh it's going to be great for me and the whole entire room. >> reaction >> I'm excited. I'm excited for him. I'm excited for what he brings to the team. Uh I've been talking to Von since I met him last year for the first time when I moved out here. Um and you know, there's something that we we discussed the possibilities of. So, it'll be exciting. I think he'll be a really good help to this team, but to me as a young guy, as a young edge rusher, >> He made no secret of the fact he's been working out at the star, and this is something he'd kind of wanted to do. Do you think this this might happen? >> Did I think it was going to happen? Yeah, I thought it was going to happen. Like I said, I've been I've been talking to him since. Um and you know, he it was it was in the air, and we were talking about the possibilities, like I said. Um but I know they had to get some things right on the contractual side, whatever the case may be. I don't really know that part. Um but yeah, I I pretty much I I thought it I thought it was a possibility for sure. What do Yeah, you know, he's been in the game for a while. all-pro, pro-bowl guy, Super Bowl MVP, Super Bowl champion. Uh he brings a lot of knowledge and experience, especially like I said, you know, myself, Mali, we're younger in the Um and it'll be a great help to us. And he That's something that we discussed. You know, he want to he he wants to be that guy and that teammate for us as well as contribute, obviously. >> Did he talk at all about the relationship he had with DeMarcus Ware when they were in Denver together, how he learned from him, and then and helped win the >> That's That's exactly what he said. He said he Yeah, he said he wanted to be the D Ware for him, to me, if that makes sense. Um and coming from a guy that's a Hall of Fame guy, you know, he'll be a first ballot, in my opinion. Um that means a lot. Um that means, you know, he sees the potential in myself, but not only just me, and Mali as a young edge rusher, too. Um Maliek Collins. Um so it it'll be a great help, like I said. >> He said it like Kobe when he would ask Jordan all the questions. >> Exactly. Cuz I I remember the first time we met, too. I We We talked for like 45 minutes, and I was just trying to pick his brain. And now, him being my teammate, it'll it'll be really good. >> Shady talked about the alignment between BT Jordan, Von Miller, those guys know each other really well, but also Chadera, in terms of teaching pass rushing. How much does that help a young edge rusher to have everyone in the same corner? >> It It helps a lot. And And you said it best, you know, everyone in the same corner. So, you know, the same coaching points, and then then even even to that point, they'll even get more detailed, and you know, Von might say, you know, [music] certain things that he's, you know, learned over the past few years, and Rashan RG might say the same thing, and and it'll it'll just, like I said, help me develop as a pass rusher. >> I'm sure you've been asked about it, but you talk about the excitement of playing with a guy like Von Miller, also learning from a guy like him. >> Yeah, it it's it's going to be very exciting. I I told him to his face a couple times when I was at the sack summit, too. I I started playing football the year he got to the league, and you know, being a defensive player, being an edge rusher, you know, in high school, whatever, I studied his film a lot. I told him that to his face. Um so, him being my teammate is is pretty cool, for sure. >> What can you learn from a guy like him? >> Everything. Everything. Everything. What to do on and off the field at times. uh but especially on the field cuz we play the same position. So >> about seeing the other number six out there Saturday night? >> Yeah, he who? Can Can Brown, he who? It was uh it was it was really cool cuz you know, people like, "I know that's not you, Don." Obviously not. I don't play receiver. But it was really cool watching him. >> text messages like, "Who's this guy?" >> I got I got a couple. I got a couple for sure. >> Yeah. >> I told him he got to get a new number. >> Oh, he know that. Oh, >> [laughter] >> oh, he know that. This is this is camp number. This is not college. Yeah. >> Do you have a favorite Von Miller move? >> I'm sorry. I'm sorry. Go ahead. Okay. >> Favorite Von Miller move? >> Uh I mean, I mean, studying his film, uh you know, he he's he he his ghost rush is is really cool, but and he'll say the same thing. A lot of his rushes come off of power. Um and obviously his get-off. So, it starts with the get-off and then, you know, he'll power rush fall inside make a play, but then, you know, that kind of sets up for the ghost move. So, >> Shady said he's spoken to you guys after the meeting broke with Von. Uh maybe kind of bring us in the room a little bit about just what that was like and the reaction. >> Um just, you know, letting us know that, you know, what was going on and uh you know, what he'll bring to the table and and what he expects out of myself, RG, Nelly, you know, James, Sam, Morris, you know, the guys. Um that's pretty much it. It wasn't anything, you know, too crazy or anything like that. >> Was it excitement or just kind of business? >> It was a mix of both. Mix of both. We understand that this is the NFL and, you know, bringing a guy like that, a Hall of Fame guy, into our room, it'll just help us be better and help this team. >> Sorry about that. Was the sack something that the first time you met him? >> No, I met him last year when I first got out here to Dallas. >> Did you have a kind of fan moment of like, "Hey, I used to watch you. Like, this is kind of crazy." >> Yeah, I I I'm not like a fanboy or anything like that, but I did tell him, you know, who's you know, whose film I studied and he and he knows that. And it's it's it's kind of cool. You know, he's a person at the end of the day. So, you know, it's never really like, you know, too high or too low, whatever the case may be. It's just cool. What What made that, you know, you two stay in touch and know that you would be back one day? >> Yeah, definitely kept in touch with us, Spags. But at the same time, it's like I just knew it was something for me still in Kansas City. And you know, when you have that in back of your head, you know, whenever there's opportunity or you try to come back and that was my goal and uh I'm glad we was able to make it work. So, >> how much did uh Chris influence you coming back here? >> Oh, you know, I know Chris. I've been knowing Chris since draft prep, you know, big character guy. Uh love Chris. Um but yeah, he's a worker, you know, as allpro. But yeah, just being back with him is a different it brings a different energy. You know, he inspires me, I inspire him. So, >> what did they tell you about coming back and what role did you fit in with the team? Oh, just whatever they need me to play. Um, just uh attack whenever my name is called and I'm ready to go. So, >> what do you think of Peter Woods and Armason Thomas so far? >> Talented. Talented. I loved watching them out there, you know, the game last week. But it was good seeing them get after the quarterback, you know, playing the running well. You know, they're they're young, but they're definitely talented. So, >> was there a challenge to see from afar the Chiefs go on to win two more after you? You know, you know, every time you uh I watch the Chiefs play, you know, I get a little salty, you know, but at the same time, I'm rooting for those guys. You know, I know a lot of them guys that were still here when I came here when we won it. But, you know, it's always ruin. It's always love. Obviously, when we play against them, I want to beat them. But, you know, when we don't play against them, I usually root for them, too. >> The league for a long time. What yourself do you want to prove this season? >> Just I can still play. You know, I keep going, keep getting better. You learn every year. you know, you you you try to push yourself push yourself as much as you can. You know, I still got a lot of football left in me. So, you know, I just want to go out there and just keep balling, you know. >> How would you evaluate the the year Jacksonville? >> What was that? Sorry. >> How would you evaluate last year in >> Uh, it was cool. Um, it was different. You know, I was with camp, familiar face with uh in Miami. So, camp was cool. Defense was solid. You know, my role was, you know, whenever they needed me to and I was ready for that role. Uh, but uh but yeah, it was cool. We went far. We lost to the Bills in the playoffs, but you know, it was a it was a good season for us, I would say. >> You were having a career year here in 2019 before the injury. What was that? What was that what was that like for you to have that? And you mentioned want to come back. Is there some unfinished business element to it, too? >> Yeah, it was a it was a mindset coming in because I just got traded for Cleveland. So, I knew I was coming to a new program and I had to prove myself, you know, that was my whole mindset going in just to prove myself um to say I still still got it. So yeah, that's what my mindset was in 2019. >> What's the challenge coming back from camp [clears throat] at this stage of camp and kind of trying to get caught up with everyone else who's already been out here for a couple weeks? >> It's definitely tough. You know, they said football shape is different. I would say that, but you know, the more reps I get, the better, the more comfortable I get out there. Um, but yeah, just learning the playbook and getting after it, you know. So, all good. >> You have that Super Bowl ring somewhere safe? >> Oh, yeah. It's in my set. It ain't going nowhere. Yeah. Thanks, Emanuel. >> Thank you. All right.

title: Isaiah Pola-Mao, Keyron Crawford and Charles Grant Presser - 8.17.26
text: How y'all doing? >> You picked off Kirk today. >> I will, I will, I will. >> Yeah. >> What was that like for you? What was today like for you? >> Uh, you know, it was just a step in the right direction. Progress, you know, we're all trying to get better each day, so. >> What did the joint practices do for you and the hopes of getting ready for tomorrow? >> I mean, it's it's another day for everybody to get better together, you know, going against another team uh it's just a good challenge for us. >> Do you feel you learn more out of those than the preseason games? >> I'm sorry, can you say that >> Do you learn more learn more out of those than the preseason games? >> Yeah, absolutely. I mean, you know, preseason coaches don't want to show everything, but joint practices definitely. We'll see some things that, you know, we haven't been working on, so it'll be good for us. >> Adam talked specifically yesterday that that the joint practices should be mayhem. Do you feel that way that that's what the joint practices are going to be? >> Yeah, definitely. So it's a little bit chaotic. Um you know, you got guys out there definitely ready for a fight, but uh you know, that's our mindset as a defense, you know, every play we got to go out there ready to punch somebody in the mouth. >> It always seems So that the the defense I mean, you guys were conditioning after practice a little bit. It just seems a little more intense this week. Is that Is Is that accurate to say? >> Yeah, I mean, uh you know, it's you know, it's starting to get into what what is this? Week four or something, but you know, everybody's tired, you know, it's time for everybody somebody to step up and, you know, I think coach has started off practice with a little bit of intensity get everybody else going. >> How different is your role in Rob Leonard's defense from what it's been in the past? >> Uh, it's it's different, you know, Rob you can I can see a little bit of influence from everywhere he's been, but uh you know, my my it's the same role as I've always been, you know, but I'm just trying to be the best teammate in whatever capacity that is. >> Do you feel Do you feel like the old guy now? >> Yeah, definitely. I mean, going into year five now it it definitely feels like I'm a little bit older, but uh no, I Chan and Terrance still got me on that. >> Did you change up any of your preparation in the off-season? Like or do anything different ahead of the season than you have in the past? >> Uh it's been more about taking care of my body, you know, like I said, I am getting a little bit older, but uh just trying to make sure that I'm staying on top of, you know, whatever injuries that I had in the pre-season or in the past, you know, I am coming off of surgery from in January, so that's been a little bit different, so yeah. >> What was that process that rehab process like for you? Just getting through that. >> Yeah, I mean, it's it's a grind every day, you know, coming from a a major surgery uh shoulder injury, but um you know, just trying to take it day by day, trying to figure out, you know, how it's feeling, making sure that I'm confident. >> How are you feeling right now? >> I feel good. I mean, I do feel confident. I don't even think about my shoulder, you know, so it's a good thing. >> Did it take a second to build that confidence back up? >> I mean, absolutely, you know, especially an injury like this at this stage in my career, uh it definitely was a a big hit to my mental, but uh you know, just working every day, it's it's preparation builds confidence, and that's what I've been doing. >> When did you feel like you kind of turned a corner and felt like yourself again? >> Uh I'll probably say coming into OTAs, definitely feeling a lot better. Um and then once we got pads on, you know, get a couple pops in, it's like, all right, we're good to go. >> What kind of mental fortitude does it take for you to push through when you're getting rehab and the injury and knowing that there's going to be some young blood in here in the safety room and all? >> I mean, that's everything uh at this stage at this uh level of football, everything is mental, you know, so it's all about you. Everybody's big, fast, and strong, you know, so it's that's the only thing that separates us is our mental. >> On that same note, uh Coach Kubiak can talk about, you know, a competition at every single position. Did you see all that competition, and how did you feel like you stepped up to it? >> Yeah, I mean, absolutely. Of course, we got some young guys coming in. They're young and hungry and eager to learn. So, I mean, uh them just being here has pushed me, honestly. Um you know, the coaches have been pushing me, so I take it upon myself to, you know, it's on me. I got to uh push through and uh just make sure I'm on top of everything and uh make it a difficult decision. >> What is What has Taron added to the room with his veteran presence and kind of versatility that he can give? >> I mean, he's played a lot of ball, you know, he's he's seen things, he played in big games, so it's it's good to just hear how he sees things and try to learn from him. >> It seems like he's playing a little bit of a different role than he's played in the past here in Las Vegas. What is it like to have a veteran come in from a different team who's had success elsewhere and kind of buy into what the vision has? >> You know, it's good that he's been in other systems because, you know, he he kind of picks the brain of the DC and he's able to kind of give us some insight on what he's been in and and seen, so, you know, it's been absolutely great for him to be here. >> What's the biggest improvement you you and your position group are looking to make against the Texans? >> Uh against the Texans, we we just want to go out and show our physicality. You know, that's what the DC and the head coach has been preaching, so that's what we have on our on our brain. >> Isaiah, what areas do you feel you've grown at, you know, heading into year five? Where where are you experiencing growth as a player? >> Uh it's more on my communication, making sure that, you know, we we can take command as a unit in the back end and make sure everybody's on the same page. >> Thanks, Isaiah. >> Yeah, thank you. Appreciate it. Excuse the ref. >> training camp? What was the experience been like for you? >> Uh it's been really good. I just be being able to get adjusted, then being able to um be a part of the team, but also being able to be around a good group of guys to develop in um crack that eggshell and just come out of my comfort zone to get better each each and every day with the guys. >> In what way have you come out of your comfort zone so far in training camp? >> Yeah, it's it's really just more so just uh the hesitation, uh just being able to play fast and physical, uh and remember what I'm told, remember uh the basics and remember the um the things that I that I got drafted for. >> How similar or different is it to what you expected? >> Uh it's it's definitely different, but it's also just being able to compete with the guys, and being able to um know it's it's all about the team. Just being able to um look at the bigger picture and the the end goal is just to win. >> You're heading into your your heading into your first ever joint practice. What are some things that maybe the vets have told you to expect and how to handle that situation? >> Um it's going to be intensive and have great competition. So, it's going to be a a dog fight. >> How are you looking to maybe make a bigger name for yourself in this opportunity at the joint practice? >> Uh just being able to stick and stick to what I'm told what I what I've been taught. Just going out here. Nothing's going to change as far as the work ethic and the things that all the guys come in here and put the work in to do. So, we all going to play as one and compete. >> You talked about in the spring reaching out to Max and and trying to learn things from him. Just now in in training camp, what have you picked up from him and kind of what's your relationship like with him? >> Uh that's my Max. Yeah, he he's that very dedicated and intentional on everything he does. I just sit back and observe and I take take what I can and apply it to my own self. But, just having a guy like that to be around and study and just like being able to watch and take from him is is definitely is definitely honorable. >> Are there any other veterans that you're learning from other than Max Crosby? >> All right, every every veteran that we have in the D-line room, wide receiver, defense, offense, quarterback position, they all they all speak vocally. They all uh have those leadership traits and have that that winning mentality that's going to change the program around. >> It's still early, but how do you feel that your transition from college ball to pros has been? >> Uh I can honestly say I've gotten better each each and every day. Uh there I started off pretty rocky just because the mindset, the expectations, and the pressure that I built on myself. But, also just being able to stick to what I'm told and be able to like fall back on your training, and not worry about anything else, and then just go out there and play fast, and be physical is the main one. >> What do you think has surprised you about the process so far about your game? >> Uh not really. It's just more so of the the the inner thoughts and the mindset could the the mental aspect can be a big part of everything. So, if you really just take take everything out and no worries, no none of that, like you'll be fine. >> What helped you kind of break out of that mentality of pressure on yourself? >> Uh just going back and watching my old tape, remembering the guy that they drafted, remembering like I'm here for a reason. Everything happens for a reason, and just going out and like say F it, and just like you know, just go play fast. >> Your college tape? >> Yeah. Yes, sir. >> You you went through a little bit of an injury. Is that was that something that kind of you're trying to ramp up for the season and you had to kind of take a step back? >> Uh it it was just protocol. I had to just deal with it. So, just I was hell of a happy to get back. >> What was that was that first preseason game experience like for you? >> Uh it was it was fine. I actually like as I was saying like each and every day like that game just took a stride. I felt like I played fast, physical, and hard, and like that's that's who I am. So, just being able to do that and being able to be a part be a being able to be a part with the guys, it was fine. >> What was the game speed like for you going into the the NFL first action? >> Uh it it it was good. It was good. It because we were playing drives and series. So, coach was trying to he was trying to wear us out. >> What have you taken away from coach Kubiak so far? Coach Coach Leiter? >> Uh he's definitely they both are very intentional and have high expectations for both sides of the ball. So, being able to be very critical and detail in everything we do, there's always uh how can you get better? There's always uh, all right, why is this guy not improving? What do we need to do to help him improve? So, it's just they they want to put us in the best situations so we can be able to, uh, win successful as a team. >> How much did going to this outside summit in the off-season help you not just to hone your skill set, but also to see how this D-line that every single one of you guys was there to kind of bond together? >> Yeah, uh, it it was shout out to Max because, uh, he's a great mentor and great, uh, great leader. But, just being a being a part of that, it was it was mainly the what I found, the best part about it was how we all like every all the edges and D-tackles got in one room and we all was just talking ball like all the vets was just speaking up. They were playing tape on the, uh, film and we were they was just like speaking and they was just like telling us like what they saw, why they do this, why they do that. So, just being able to learn, uh, and just observe and soak in that, uh, knowledge was definitely important. Uh, I feel like my game is just very dominant in run, pass, and anything that I do. I just being able to, uh, my I feel like my biggest one is just being able to be dominant on special teams and just being able to find my role, but also impacting the game on defense. >> Thank you, K'Lavon. >> Thank you. Appreciate it. Thank y'all. How are y'all doing? >> How was today for you? >> It was it was good, you know, I think we're trying to lock in. You know, get ready. We have a big couple days coming up. So, I just focused on focused on that. >> What did you guys see on your film preseason and all their offense that you >> Yeah, yeah. Well, I'm more so looking at the whole team, you know, not one man man can get the job done. So, it's how do we do, you know? And I think we did good. Definitely room to improve, but I think we starting to lay a good foundation. >> Did you see how strong the Houston Texans defense was last year? How much has it kind of excite you guys to rally you up to go up against them? >> Oh, yeah, It's It's a great opportunity to improve and compete. You know, getting ready to play the best. So, we got to show that we can work with the best. >> What do you want to focus on the team rather than like Washington rather than obviously pretty good blocking and two things that kind of back in that block? >> Uh shoot. In In the moment, it kind of surprised me for real. But, uh you know, looking at it, the thing that stands out is everybody blocking. Like, everybody was half for half. It took all 11. Even the receivers blocking downfield. That's what That's what was able to spring that big run. >> Did you feel that game film overall is the best one you put out? I mean, I haven't really had too many opportunities. So, just trying to keep improving. I don't even don't even really focus on that. Just how can I get better? >> How much different do you feel this strength camp from last year? >> You know, a lot more a lot more comfortable for sure, you know. Been Been in the program for a year and been able to go against the guys. Uh Yeah, been able to go against and work with with the team. Just keep improving and I feel feel a lot more comfortable. >> How How'd you approach the offseason going about that goal of improving and getting better this time? >> Yeah, big thing for me was uh just being with the O-line. Uh we had a group of guys here training. So, just trying to get most connected cuz most connected O-line is a a good O-line. >> How do you feel as though the O-line is is connecting up to this point? >> Yeah, I think I think we're doing we're doing good, you know. Uh last year, new new coaches. Uh I think we're able to uh take what they want and make it ours. >> Just want to get back to you. You said that it surprised you on that play. I guess what just like the way that you sent a guy flying? Like, what what actually surprised you? shoot. I was blocking and then I was on the ground. I was like, "Oh." >> [laughter] >> Oh, okay. >> What's how London Bond brought to the line so far? >> He's brought I'd say he's brought He He knows what success looks like. And a team that is trying to chase that, he's he's brought what it looks like and something that we can look to to keep getting better. >> Do you feel like there's more of an emphasis on communication with the line this year? >> Uh 100% 100%. Everybody has to be on the same page. We're five guys working as one. So, everybody has to know what everybody's doing in order to get the job done. >> Does the system kind of feel different than last year's? I'd say there's there's definitely things that are different, you know, uh good for good for good or bad for for better or worse, there's things things that are different. I think it's up to us to take those differences and just make it our strengths. >> What's it What's it been like learning from Rick Dennison, you know, a guy who's been around the league a lot of time? >> Yeah, it is nice, man. You know, he has a lot of wisdom that I'm trying to get. So, uh it's like he's he's thinking he's thinking on levels that I'm not thinking yet. So, just being able to be in the same room gets me thinking at a higher level. >> Coach Kubiak talked about competition in every room from day one. How does that help the line as you guys are also trying to be cohesive as one, but then also push each other to make sure you are, you know, working on it? >> Yeah, well, you know, they say iron sharpens iron, so as we compete, we're getting stronger both sides. >> And how does your skills set really complement the zone blocking scheme and everything that Kubiak is trying to do in this system? >> Yeah, uh I'd say you know, you got to you got to be an athlete to play this sport, and I think I'm an athlete, so uh just just trying to learn learn everything and just use my abilities to the best I can. >> What's it been like working with Kirk Cousins, Fernando Mendoza, um just the quarterback room? >> It has been great, you know, we got uh Kirk Cousins, he's he's a guy that's has has done it and been there, you know, he's kind of like the dad of the group uh to an extent, you know. So, uh he's he's able to keep the joy going on on those tough days. And then Fernando, you know, he's a young guy, but he also has that he has a good joy a nice joy to him. I always smile I mean, so you can't help but smile when looking at him. >> Have you Have you watched much of the Texans defensive line? >> Yeah, I've I've been I've been watching, yeah. >> What uh what what do you take from them and how much of a challenge do they present to try to get you ready for the season? >> Yeah, I'd say uh that we are they're definitely a up-the-field type of team. They like getting up the field. Uh you know, there's teams like that across the league that try to get up the field, so you know, start at the best, everything else will be Yeah. >> You and Caleb came in together. It seems like you're taking a a similar leap this this training camp. But how how do you guys feed off of each other? >> Yeah, so we're we're always in our each other's ear, you know, he sees something and he he's talking to me. I see something I'm talking to him. Just keep trying to encourage each other and keep pushing each other. Nobody can do it by themselves. >> Speaking of this just a little bit more generally, what does a a fullback add to a running game from your perspective? From >> perspective, I say extra alignment that can catch the ball and run, you know. Uh he's going to get he's he's going to get in there get his hands dirty and uh open up the hole even more for us. >> How does a fullback help with the running game? How can a fullback help with the run? >> Yeah, so uh I mean, you you see you see the fullback blow somebody up it's like damn he can't be the only one, you know, I got to I got to get me a body, too. >> What's the most dad-like thing that Kirk Cousins has said or done? >> Uh shoot, I'd say we were getting ready for something and then one of the teammates was like, "Hey man, I like your shorts." I looked down. Yeah, like big cargo shorts on. And I was like, "Oh yeah." I looked Yeah. >> Just got to Looks All right. Thank Thank you, guys. >> Appreciate it. You guys have a good week.

title: Colts Cover-2 Podcast: Recapping preseason opener, looking ahead to Atlanta joint practices
text: Hey there Colts fans. It's Nathan Brown, Colts insider with the Indianapolis Star here for another edition of the Colts Cover Two podcast. We've got uh last week's preseason opener to discuss. The Colts ending in a tie in New England at Foxboro um taking on the Patriots. We had two more training camp practices to cover over the weekend as the Colts got back. actually our our last two traditional training camp practices ahead of the pair of joint practices that we have with the Falcons. It's actually the last two normal Colts training camp practices that the Colts will have at Grand Park, oddly enough. Um feels like the uh the weeks here have flown by. Um been a as as we'll maybe discuss here a little bit a fairly as calm as you could you would imagine. um training camp for the Colts. Don't want to jinx it. Knock on wood. Um so obviously have a week to go and still two preseason games. We got still a handful of roster spots to uh to watch. We got Alec, we're still on Alec Pierce watch. He was again out on the fields but um not in cleats yesterday. We'll get um into the latest on him here in a second. Um Joel was in the press box, one of the few watching last Thursday's preseason opener for the Colts against the Patriots. Um feels like there has been a um the the winds have switched a little bit from some of our thoughts coming away from Thursday night to what we've seen in the last couple preseason games. Um most notably maybe the backup quarterback battle as well as the kicker battle. Um where do you feel like those um you can take which whichever one of those you want to start with. Where did those things stand at the moment and and why do you feel like we maybe saw so much different Thursday compared to what we saw Saturday and Sunday? >> Yeah, that's the interesting thing to me is like so Thursday night you come away feeling like okay Anthony Richardson turns in his best day. Spencer Schrader shows kind of what he can do again. Um, you know, why why they why they're still doing this, I guess, is the right way to put it. Why they're still uh chasing um the idea that he could be uh the next guy, that he could be the kicker when when Groupy has been so far ahead of him. And you could see it like you can see it there. I I don't want to minimize that. You could you can see it in uh in that kick because of of just the the how far he can kick it and at the height he can kick it. it the the trajectory of his football when he's really really really um when he's when he's really on is just different and it'd be very hard to block. He can you can see why they like him. Then he comes out the next day and he missed then he comes out the next day or not the next time they kick we see him and he misses two of his six kicks. pulls him to the left. Same issue he's had the whole time. It it just it just sort of feels like, you know, this is this is just he just can't quite get out of it with with pulling the ball right now. And at some point, I do think that the Colts are interested in that potential, but at some point you wonder, as much as they said the preseason kicks matter more than than anything else, at some point is it just do you have to just go with the fact that the numbers are just much much better for Blake Groupy? I believe he's 33 of 36 now >> after all six of his kicks yesterday. I believe Spencer Shrader is 24 of 36. um which is a terrible number. Now, obviously it flipped in the in the preseason game, but I don't know if you can credibly tell the roster like, "Hey, we're going to go with this guy um at this point unless something changes here in the next couple weeks and we're not going to see much more." Like that's the other thing is that part of this podcast is we like the us having a ton of information on what's going on in practice. This is the last week for it because the Falcons come, those are the last two practices we see. They play that preseason game and then we are back at the facility and when we get back to the facility, we are in a um an an inseason we're in an inseason mode where we see maybe the first 20 minutes practice, but we don't see all of it. Yeah, we'll see warm-ups. We'll see um some positional drills and maybe a little bit of team work, but very little. Um yeah, you you lose a a decent chunk. Well, I mean, the the kicker stuff, if they still have two kickers on the roster beyond um the preseason game, um we'll we'll just have to rely on what um what Shane Stiken tells us or or Brian Mason or who or whoever we get a chance to talk to basically. Um it's >> Now, I will say this, if you're going to talk to somebody about a battle, you want to be Brian Mason >> 100%. Yeah. >> Because he'll tell us what's going on. But realistically, by the end by the end of that third preseason game, uh they have decisions to make. They have they have to have cuts done by that Tuesday after it, I believe. So, um there there's just not a lot of time yet for for groupy to fall off or Shraider to really lock in what we saw in the preseason game. No, you I mean it's it's hard to really even imagine what would have to take place for group E because I mean what we've seen again we've seen only one preseason preseason game. They still get two more. Um assuming that they keep both around up until then but um we got to see groupy um you know he missed a 61 yard that was not a terrible miss. It was a little short and it was um I think a little right. Um not you know if you saw someone kick that in a regular season game and they miss like that I don't think it would be all that surprising um quite frankly and you as great as kickers are nowadays in the NFL um you're going to miss some 61 yarders and when you only have a chance to see one um missing one is is not all that surprising. Um, and it kind of goes to what we think we know and understand about these two guys. Um, groupies, I mean, it seems like at least as the the kickers who they are right now, um, groupies floor is a little higher. um ceiling maybe a little bit lower, but we we see that um perfection out of Spencer Shrader so rarely in the practices that we've seen, the joint practice action. Um the little bit that we saw in preseason game, I mean, that was that was far and away his best kick. Um I think it would have been good from several more yards. Uh yeah, definitely. But you just you don't see that trajectory um the high arcing right down the middle um end over end type of ball flight. Um even even a lot of the ones that he makes in practice um from Spencer that kind of they're starting to tilt a little bit um and they're starting to drift a little bit left and they they squeeze in. Um again, he's at a kind of a 67% clip right now. um he's making um you know a little bit more than every other one, but we don't see too many of them that just look really really good still right now. And um I if if you took us back um a week or two in in training camp um back when we were seeing a lot of this the uh to to start things out, I think we still felt like maybe there was a chance that the tide could turn. But um outside that one really good kick in that game on Thursday, it just kind of feels like we're seeing a lot of the same. Um and that's not that's not a shot um against Spencer. Um there's a lot that goes into a kicker coming back from an injury like this. We don't see that very often. Um just because kickers don't suffer these types of contact injuries all that often. Um and and I do think he's good enough to be on an NFL roster at some point. I think he's probably I mean there's no reason to think anything other than him he's going to get better as the summer turns into fall and we we get deeper into the season. So whether he lands on a roster week one or he hangs around on the sidelines until someone wants to make a kicker switch and he's the first guy off the board. Um I think we're going to see Spencer Shrader kicking kicking in the NFL in in 2026. It it just seems a little far-fetched that it's going to be in Indianapolis. >> Yeah. And I think this is the this is the way the preseason goes too. Like so I I would say teams know this is important to say. teams do know or they have an idea what's going on in practices around the league. There are staffers I I know this for a fact. There are staffers on on teams whose job is to um figure out what's going on in camp other camps try to get information on players they might want to pick up um waiver claim trade anything at the roster deadline. that's that's part of uh that's just part of of the game at this at this stage. title: DeMeco Ryans training camp presser | Full Q&A
text: With the joint practice tomorrow, we're trying to accomplish you know, two good teams going out competing against each other and going against some different schemes. That's the the biggest emphasis, like being able to see some different things, tendency-wise, play-wise, going against different players. They have a lot of good players there, starting with the defensive end, Max Crosby. It's going to be great for our guys to go against him. At the quarterback position, you know, having Kirk Cousins and Mendoza, you know, two really good quarterbacks, so we're excited to see our group going up against those guys. Can't forget Brock Bowers as well, one of the best tight ends in the league. So, personnel different, all right, scheme different, it helps us to continue to develop and grow our team throughout training camp. With Tank, he's on his own plan. So, however that looks, whatever it entails, it'll be all geared toward what's best for Tank Dell. >> Are there moments where you have to kind of sift through some practice stuff where it's like, "Hey, don't make this play cuz you're familiar with it, like make this play because you see it as the play is happening." Cuz you guys go against each other enough. So, I think sometimes maybe it doesn't come familiar for the guys. You try not to have that be a disadvantage for a rep. >> We have a lot of variety to what we're doing offensively and defensively, so it's never, you know, one rep that's the same. Guys have to be on it, you have to be deliberate in what you're doing, you have to trust your eyes, trust your techniques, and be where you're supposed to be. I think we had, you know, a couple plays where uh like one play we had yesterday with uh Huzzy playing the nickel position, right? He's gotten better, he got beat on a similar route a couple times, and yesterday he was able to play his technique a little bit better, a little tighter. He was able to step in one and make an interception. So, that's the type of growth you see. You know, although it may be a different route, different look, different formation, can you just trust your technique, be where you're supposed to be, and make a play? And Hussey was a good example of that yesterday. >> When it comes to winning a job, a lot of times we look at the preseason game and like this guy's ahead of the job. What percentage would you say when it comes to like practice and the preseason game is is what decides that? >> There's no percentage. To me, it's all I take everything into account. All right, and it's not just one is heavier than the other. I just look at how guys are working every single day. How are they improving every single day? That's what I'll take into consideration. And also, you get, you know, towards the end, you're talking about backup guys, role guys, like you know, how many things can that guy do for us, right? Where is his versatility? And versatility helps a lot when you have to limit the roster. You have You need guys who can do multiple things on game day, so that definitely helps. >> The value for uh somebody like CJ with these practice reps against the Raiders, and also perhaps if if we see him in the preseason game, what is the value for him at at this point in his career I I guess these new faces and different looks? >> Yeah, the value for CJ is you get to see again different coverages, right? You get to see different players and how are they responding and reacting to your movements, right? You discipline, keep your eyes down the middle, being able to move, you know, hook players to your advantage, like seeing him go out and still execute his discipline, his techniques the proper way. Really, for him it doesn't matter who you go against, but it's also like are you trusting your process every single time that you go out? So, he's done a great job all camp, and I don't expect anything different on tomorrow. I expect them to come out and have a good day. >> Coach, with the trusting the process, how do you help player balance out that that fine line between athleticism and instinct, but also reading your keys and you know, but sometimes sometimes reading your keys and doing the doing the same thing over and over again can be monotonous to some of those players, especially when they're very athletic, very instinctive. But how do you balance that out? >> For me, consistency is key. You want to be a really good player, the great players in this league, one thing you can say about all of them, like they're consistent. They were consistent in what they did and the plays that they made, it wasn't about the wild plays, but they make the wild plays because they're consistent. And you add in great instincts and anticipation with being consistent on your technique, that's when you become a really great player. So, it can get monotonous and boring at times. That's by an old lineman, for instance, just being able to stay inside, right? Protect inside out, inside out. You may hear the same thing over and over again, but the one time you don't do it, then disaster happens, you know, for for the play. So, you just have to remain consistent, have to remain confident in what the coaches are telling you like is right, it works when you try to do it the right way. So, consistency is key. When you're looking for a team to practice with, what that practice was, how important is for you on the body of the opponent finding teams that have very different structures up front? How do you like the defensive because that equals the offense? Do you guys go against the period for which you defensively see which of [clears throat] the front structures that you go against? >> Ideally, when I'm going through and picking a joint practice, it first starts with our scheduling and we don't get to get to pick our schedule, but it works out a lot of times in our favor where offensively we're consistently going against a four-man down front, which we run defensively. So, if I could get the opportunity to go against teams that present five down fronts and different structures, different coverages, that works out great for us because again, it's developing our offense to make some different calls, different communication checks up front, making sure they're on it because we know we're going to see a ton of five down teams throughout the season. So, if we are able to get that work early on, right in August, that definitely prepares us for the season. Brett's played in this league. He's done a really good job. He's He's won a couple games in this league, so he has the experience. So, I'm not worried about that from an evaluation standpoint. He's He's His track record has proven that he can go in. Smart guy. Picked up the offense already. Done a great job with the plays that we've given him. So, uh no worries there at all. When it comes to the responsibility piece for all of our guys, it it goes to whether you're a young guy, old guy, like how can you help us on game day? All right, we only get 48 guys on game day. So, who can go out there again and do multiple things? So, if you're a receiver, you can't just line up and be a starting receiver. You have to be able to provide something for us special teams-wise, whether that's returning or, you know, helping out in some of the other phases. So, the more you can do the better. With the joint practice, we definitely communicate with the other coaches. Myself and the other head coach, we communicate. Also, our coordinators are talking. So, you know, you want to try to get some some things schematically that we haven't seen a ton of, so we can do that. We want to work that for sure. And then you know, from my mindset, let's put the ball down and let's go to work, right? It really doesn't matter. Like, throw your playbook at us. Let's see how our rules and things we're teaching our guys, how do they hold up? So, it's not a lot of coordinating. Hey, I want to see this, want to see that. There's some one-offs here and there, but for the most part, man, we want to see our guys go out and just compete. Let's go against a really good team. >> From your perspective, you know, you got three valuable defensive backs that can pick the ball away. Is ball skill something that you can really develop, or is it more like something you just have to have? It's kind of innate. From your perspective, how do you think that can be developed? >> Yeah, from my perspective, when you talk about you know, taking the football away, in my short history of of doing this and coaching and evaluating guys, guys who have taken the ball away in high school and college, they tend to take the ball away in the NFL. Kalen Bullock, for instance, he's he's done it at a high level in college going up taking the football away. Of course, I think his baseball background has something to do that, playing center field, being able to track the football. I mean, he's has really great hand-eye coordination and confidence in his hands. Derek Stingley, another guy, we're doing our ball meeting a couple years ago and coach Deion pulled up a old high school clip of Stingley, you know, picking the football off, and he picked it off exactly the same way he picked it off versus Denver, overhead, going up, picking the ball. So, did I coach Stingley to do that? No. >> [laughter] >> It's just God-given uh great ability that that God has given him that he has a knack for going and taking the football away. So, I'll try to find guys who have production in their history, high school, college, and it will definitely translate to the NFL. Same way, if a guy hadn't caught any in college, I can't give him too much of a hard time when he doesn't catch one here. Yeah, when you take the ball away, you know, and know you know. You have to have that confidence when when can I step in front of a route and really take that take the ball, or do I just need to play it safe and just, you know, bat the ball down. So, there's fine line for players, and you just know in those split seconds. That's why these guys are as great as they are, because they can make those split-second decisions that only they feel in their mind that they can make. Like you talk about taking the ball away, I'm thinking about Stingley last year versus Jacksonville Jaguars. Like he has a shallow route, he's chasing him backside. Most players are probably just going to try to Hey, I'm kind of behind the route, I'm kind of just going to play the ball. But Stingley and trusting his hands and his ability, he goes and snatches that ball one-hand, one of the best plays I've ever seen. Thank you, guy.
