title: Minnesota Vikings Team Press Conferences | August 17 | 2026 Training Camp
text: I know that Jamal Adams was just here for a short period of time, so it wasn't like it was implemented in the full game plan, but it it's never fun to see somebody go down. >> Yeah. Uh I mean, it feels like he'd been here uh for a while, man. He's uh the kind of football player like we love in this building, the kind of football players we like to bring in, especially for this defense. And uh you know for him to you know have the impact he had on us in these few weeks and uh to see him carving out a road for himself to see him working so hard to you know claim his name back and uh his position back in this league and for that to happen man it sucks and uh you know it's not too much I can say but but it sucks cuz you know it hurts heavy on my heart. you know, this a guy I told you guys weeks ago when he first got here, you know, I looked up to, you know, a lot and I modeled my game after him a lot and uh you know, I was very excited to play with him and uh you know, to to to get that cut short. Obviously, it's tough, but uh I mean, that's the name of the game and uh we're here to honor him in the way we play. Um it's not my first rodeo in this type of in this type of world, but we're definitely sending our love and prayers to him and his family. >> How do you feel about the defense right now? >> I feel amazing, man. I think uh for one, we're deep, you know, which is always nice to see. you know, you come out and you see the guys uh go out. You see, you go out and you see the guys coming in even more hungrier than you. Um it's uh it's a good feeling. You know, those guys uh you know, that we got in that second, third group, they want to play. You know, they're they they you know, they're coming. So, it's uh it's definitely fun to uh see, you know, things coming to fruition and see the guys start to gel and the chemistry build. Um you know, the things we've been able to do in this defense, you know, are only getting better. Uh so, yeah, I'm excited to uh get some new blood in here and uh go attack this week. >> What's the Baltimore scrimmage like? Uh it's going to be physical. Um you know that that's a a organization that's known for their physicality. Um a team that known for their physicality. Their leaders are very physical. So you know we we know what we're going to get. Obviously uh you know new blood you know new feeling on for them you know but obviously they're trying to reclaim their stake in their division and their you know their place in the league and you know us the same way. So uh two very hungry teams going out there you know trying to see where we're at going into the week one. So I'm I'm excited to get their best and they're going to get ours. What have you made of um just how quickly Jacob Thomas has picked this up? >> Yeah, it's uh been amazing, man. Uh I think >> especially being an undrafted guy, you know, you try to learn your role. You know, he he's probably not thinking he's going to play defense, thinking he's going to be a special team, you know, that's his way to make it in. But, you know, even through OTAAS and not him getting reps, him not getting reps, but him being able to mentally take everything on. And, you know, you can hear it in the meeting rooms and way the way he was confident in the stuff he was saying gave the coaches confidence when, you know, guys started to go down to throw him in there. you know, at one point, uh, a couple weeks ago, he was getting one reps, but he was talking like he was a one. So, you know, those kind of things, you know, coaches like to see and then for him to have a good camp and then to, you know, not really make enough plays, you know, throughout the first couple weeks, you know, he has some times where we're like, Jacob, make that play, make that play. But for him to when the lights are on to make those plays, man, it was special to see. So, I'm excited about his growth and where he is as a player. Um, he's a a very intentional guy, you know, he wants to learn. He's uh one of those guys who's on my hip, you know, trying to get any tips and tricks to, you know, do better and get better. So, I'm excited to see where he goes. >> For sure. >> What's the key to getting the most out of the joint practices? >> Uh being fundamentally sound, man. You know, uh I think um you know, that's one of our football philosophy things, but I think on both sides, if both teams are fundamentally sound, you know, we're able to get good work. You know, the minute you get guys messing up routes and jumping off sides and trying to fight and doing all that unnecessary stuff, you know, we want clean football so we both can see a true test of where we're at. So, you know, on our end, you know, my job is going to be able to get the communication, get the guys ready to play, making sure we're playing clean, calm football so we can actually get work and not, you know, blow everything out of proportion because, you know, emotions are high and guys are trying to, you know, oh, this is joint practice. Like, no, it's football. Let's play clean so we can see a true test of where we're both we're at and u, you know, move on like that. At the end of the day, still practice. You know, some guys get caught. Oh, it's a game. It's going to feel like one, but it's it's still practice. So, you know, we need clean reps on both sides for us to, you know, actually see where we're at. >> Just uh, one more thing on Jacob. just uh how hard is it when you're not getting a lot of reps to learn this defense and then have them just sort of call your number? >> Yeah. Uh I mean I think for him uh you know we've had some guys go down up and down. So you know he he actually has been getting reps in the past couple weeks but you know going into camp he wasn't you know and uh I think this defense >> Yeah. I mean especially as safety it's hard just because you know things move fast when you get out there and if you're not thinking about the communication beforehand you kind of get stuck. So, you know, it's actually kind of crazy, you know, to see a guy, you know, we have a very smart safety room. We have in the past, you know, so to see a guy like him, you know, you can tell why they brought him in. Um, because, you know, he has all the makeup up here. You know, it's not as all about getting this to play just as fast as this. So, uh, it's definitely you, it comes natural to him, I think for certain guys, it's it's harder. Um, but for guys like him is, uh, very natural. >> How do you feel about the performance you expect? >> Uh, I think I think defense played really well uh, from top to bottom. you know, you can see guys um you know, applying our scheme, applying uh the right things, and just playing hard. Man, it's fun to see those guys go out there and play really hard. >> Jamal Adams, you lost. How always hard to see a teammate go down? >> Yeah, it's tough. It's tough. Uh you know, since he's been here, he's really uh been one of the guys uh you know, he's really, you know, played many different positions and he was in uh you know, everybody could see that he could help us out a lot. So, it's tough to see him, uh, you know, go out like that. But, um he's still with us, man. and we're still going to, you know, rally around them. >> You know, this defense is built around linebackers. You get a bunch of guys that can run and are smart and play physical football. >> Yeah. Yeah, man. Those uh from top to bottom, I think everybody went out there and and kind of showed what they can do. Um you know, different skill sets, but going out there and putting it all out there for everybody to see. So, I think um linebackers played um you know, really good game. Um obviously some things to clean up, but I'm proud of those guys. And last, to get in concert with the defensive line does light in your body is the key as well. >> Uh just I think being on the same page. Uh we got a lot of moving parts. You know, sometimes guys play different positions. Just being on the same page, communicating, and really just playing team defense. >> So now you get to go against another live team this week. What What's that like when you these scrimmages like this? >> Yeah, scrimmages are great because you get live reps against different fronts, different players, and uh you get to test your technique against different guys. Some people say they're even more advantageous or you get more out of them than game preseason games. >> Uh I mean I'm a little too young to say that in my career for sure. I mean but uh I just know I try to you know make the most out of every day I'm out here. >> What' you learn the first game the preseason? >> Uh first game in the preseason. I know that um uh there are things we need to clean up, but we also did some good things out there. Um I mean that's just the wonders of preseason. You know, you put stuff on tape, you see how it works, you see how uh you can improve your fit and your technique, and you roll from there. It looks like a lot of running backs will play uh by NFL standards. What do you see different running styles from each one or how is it for you guys? >> Uh for us there there really is no change. You know, whoever's back there, we try to make um the running lanes as big as possible. Um sure, some guys have different attributes in their game, but to us, you know, our our main job is to move the line of scrimmage. >> Blocks the guy with a different jersey, right? >> Exactly. >> What do you What do you think is the biggest thing that's just sort of clicked for you so far? I think the playbook I feel really well with right now. You know, being comfortable making communications out there, you know, having comfortability with the guys. Um, yeah, I just feel very comfortable with my teammates out there right now. >> How much did your phone blow up late Saturday afternoon? >> Very much so. I have a lot of unread text me text messages that I got to get to, but uh, no, it's a lot of love and support from, uh, people that I care about. So, >> what was the process like of learning this playbook and mastering it, then allowing you to go out there and play freely and fast? >> It was tough at first. I will say that. Um, but these coaches have been amazing. You know, staying around after meetings. Uh, you know, we had a bunch of rookie meetings. Um, but they're always here to help you. And, you know, it doesn't matter the amount of questions that you have, they will answer them. Um, and try to help you through it. So, the coaches have been a big help and you know, the veteran players, they've been in the system for a little bit now. So, you know, trying to get little things from them is uh been very, very helpful. >> As a young guy, how much is on your plate being a safety in this defense? >> There's a lot a lot of communication that you have to make. you know, talking to your corner every play, your nickel, you know, talking to the linebacker. So, it can be a little overwhelming at times, but uh once you get comfortable with your teammates and and are good with making communication, it's not too bad. >> What about Minnesota stood out to you like to sign here? >> Yeah, I just thought it was a great place overall. You know, starts with the defensive coordinator. I think he has a great brand and a great style of defense. And, you know, my coach in college tried to do some of the similar things. So, um familiarity with it also helped. But, uh, that's a place I've never been and it seemed very, very intriguing. So, yeah. >> What parts of your skill set and prior playing experience have helped you most in kind of, uh, jelling with this defense? >> Yeah, I think I've said it before, just trying to be rang uh, at the deep post position. Um, trying to go red line to red line. Um, and then just the communication aspect of it. You know, I made a lot of calls in college, so coming here, you had to get comfortable with the guys first and really have that confidence to go do it. But once you have it, uh, it's pretty easy from there. You mentioned the veterans kind of giving you some help. What's the best piece of advice you've gotten so far >> from Theo? Just uh be patient with my feet obviously in the red zone and uh you know, just let things come to you. Um he's been a big help for me and you know, obviously we're playing the same position. So, anything I can get from him, um you know, you take that and try to apply it to your game every single day. So, >> you're still learning, but was there a moment that it felt like things started to click or when did that happen? >> Uh training camp's been good. I probably say in the game, honestly. you know, going out there, it kind of felt a little bit easier than practice just cuz, you know, our offense knows what we're kind of doing out there. Um, so going into the game, you know, a little bit nervous, but, uh, once you get out there, get a few plays under your belt, uh, felt good from there. So, it's been awesome so far, uh, to be part of such a special group, special team, uh, being around a, uh, a great group of football players and everything you can learn from, it's been pretty special. >> And you play a specialty position now in this league fullback. Tell me about that. What goes into being an NFL fullback? >> It's awesome. I just it's it's doing the job that whatever's asked. Uh like a lot of unique unique spots, unique lineups, whatever it takes and it's just a um a role that whatever I'm asked to do, I just want to do it to help the team win. >> Do do you do you look at it as you know, you came from Michigan, you played a lot of high in football. Big help when you get to the NFL. >> Uh yeah, there is some help. There is some help there. There's things I've done before and there's also some things I haven't done before. Um but grateful for my time in Michigan and what it's been able to help me do here. What what what do you think is the most important thing you can do for the Vikings? >> I just do whatever I'm asked to a thousand%. Um whatever that role is. And it like I said before, it's a lot of unique roles, unique spots, but uh whatever I'm asked, just do it a thousand% and be the best at it.

title: STANDOUT STUDS From Minnesota Vikings Preseason Week 1
text: From Myles Price all the way down to the undrafted rookies, here's who stood out to me in preseason week one. >> You are Locked On Vikings, [music] your daily Minnesota Vikings podcast, part of the Locked On Podcast Network. Your team every day. >> What's going on everybody? Welcome to the Locked On Vikings podcast where we're always trying to learn something new. This episode is brought to you by GameTime. Download the GameTime app, create an account and use code locked on for $20 off of your first purchase. Today on the show I want to step away from quarterback discourse. I have another one focused on like just that for later on in the week and talk a little bit about everybody else and so many storylines that came out of this preseason game, Vikings winning over the Giants 13 to 10 that is ultimately fascinating. Some up and down days, some guys that showed me exactly what I expected and some guys that showed me the exact opposite. So we're going to rapid fire through a bunch of different takeaways about a bunch of different players as many as I can cram in. Before I get started, just an FYI to make sure that I'm communicating with you the listener. I'm going to be out of town for the rest of this week. So a lot of these episodes are going to come from an Airbnb that has Wi-Fi. I don't know if I can trust and you know what weird is going to look weird, going to sound weird, might have some artifacts and stuff. So bear with me as I get through that, but I'll be back at home by the time the next preseason game is played and we'll do all the live content and stuff then. So let's talk about Myles Price. Because I think he's the guy that walks away as the biggest winner of the day. He has a couple of major plays. Two of them were on inaccurate Carson Wentz throws. One Carson Wentz was hit as he threw and the other one was that fade that was not a good fade ball. The one where he was hit as he threw was a deeper pass on a corner route and Miles Price was pretty covered. The a better defensive back picks that one off. So I think there's a little bit of like a preseason-iness going on there, right? Where if that's if that was the starters that might have been six points the other way. But that guy doesn't make the play and Miles Price raises his catch radius, gets strong, takes the ball away, right? Comes down with it, keeps his feet, even gets a little bit after the catch. That was a really cool strongman play. But the fade was way cooler to me. So when you throw a fade ball, I'll talk more about Carson Wentz later in the week, but for context, a wide receiver is not expecting a fade ball to come in at that low of an angle. That thing's got to shoot up a little bit more and take a little more time so the receiver can can run that thing down. That's where you want a fade to be. And in fact, on uh some shorts last week, I covered a couple of fades. You can find me by the way, Luke Braun NFL at on TikTok, Instagram Reels, and on YouTube Shorts. I covered a couple of fades from elsewhere in the league. There was a a clip that went kind of viral of a Carnell Tate fade and then one of Caleb Downs covering CeeDee Lamb on a fade. Both rookies looking really good on that one so they went kind of viral and I broke both of those down. And what you want in a fade is to basically jockey for position. The defensive back wants to be chest-to-chest with you so you basically are both kind of locked on to each other and then you're kind of looking up for the ball, right? And the receiver wants to take that whole apparatus and keep as much space as possible so that they can break off at the last second go find it, you know, and and jump for it and go win that. So the quarterback just wants to put it on the receiver's side. So this one was not conducive to that, not cuz it wasn't on Miles Price's side, but because it wasn't the kind of ball that you could really easily break away from and then go catch. He had to really kind of lay out for it and that ended up being this one-hander, which you had Justin Jefferson going crazy on the broadcast and stuff, which was a clip I I I looked back and saw later. Tons of fun. Go check that out if you have not seen that. If you were like me, you were stuck with the Giants broadcast, you got to go watch uh Justin Jefferson in the third quarter losing his mind about Miles Price on that play. Fantastic stuff. Um and a couple of other productive plays as well. So, Miles Price, you know, looks like a receiver. One thing I'm going to do, probably while I'm on the airplane, so you're going to hear the about this one from the Airbnb, uh something I'm going to do is watch down that and Ty Felton and see how I feel about like the route craft, but I have to put a pin in that for now and instead move on to a couple of the other headline players. So, somebody from the first team offense, of course, you know, they only played one drive, but Donovan Jackson had a really interesting day. He starts with a straight-up pancake on that zone play that ended up with Aaron Jones going down the sideline. Donovan Jackson killed a guy on it. Uh then a couple plays later, he gets backdoored. So, what I mean by that is he's it's it's a combo block, so he gets into the defensive tackle and he climbs up to the linebacker and that linebacker goes backside of the play, gets around him, Jackson's got really flexible hips, so uh he didn't react in time to use that, which was unfortunate, to kind of still guy off and that linebacker ends up being able to shoot the gap from there and make the play. You kind of want to be a little more >> [sighs and gasps] >> a little more conservative about that, but it's so hard to be in that much control for linemen. They're just such big dudes. They're like, I'm not too mad about that kind of backdoor play and typically what you will say is, "Look, if he wants like you're trying to seal him off to the play side, right? You're you're trying to seal the play side off from him." That is to say. And if he wants to go backside then play side, and if he still makes the play, I had a coach tell me once, if he makes that play, God bless him. Which is something that's been in my vernacular now. God bless him. Go ahead, dude. Like if you can do that, we're not going to scheme around it. If you can do that, you can do that, and I guess you're just that guy. And he was that linebacker was that guy on that play. I don't know which giant it was, but that was really good play from that guy. Uh and so I'm not too mad at Donovan Jackson about that one. If you want to get really nitpicky, you could say, "Ah, you know, his aiming track was a little off or something like that." But really what it is is you work front side, because you're trying to seal front side, and if they go back side, you do it. You They go back side, you you get it. Um the very next play after that though is what I liked, which was a really strong curtain close. So this is something I probably technically counts as holding, but I would never see it called, uh where you kind of get if you get a hand on the guy's kind of breastplate, if you get it like right on his collar, and you can kind of yank it down and like you're closing a curtain. So they say close the curtain. It's a great way for if you're trying to zone block somebody, you're trying to reach them, but they step with you and they deny you that reach, you get your hand on them, you kind of stab right into that sternum, try to get some control over their upper body that way, and then yank it down. Kind of technically counts as holding, but because your hands are on the inside, a ref is basically never going to call that. So you usually get away with it, and it ended up totally knocking the guy off balance, turns into a really nice block. So Donovan Jackson's day on the whole for me, something I'm pretty happy with. Um I kind of loved Ivan Pace's day. That might be a hot take, cuz the most visible thing that happened to him was him getting mossed by a 6'4 receiver, but I do not put that play on him at all. I I talked about this in the live show afterwards, um that Tyree Ingram-Dawkins, who struggled to set the edge kind of all day, and I should talk about him, too. I think the idea of Tyree Ingram-Dawkins as an edge rusher should be put to bed immediately. I think we found out that that does not work. And the the one that bugged me the most was on that drive, he gave up contained three different times by trying to flash inside. That's a very greedy thing to do. And in the NFL, you get to be greedy if you can make it. But if you flash inside then back outside then lose contain, you lose it. Um and and it actually kind of robbed Caleb Banks of a really cool play, which is unfortunate. On one of those, you know, the runner gets around and then he loses it again. Uh and and then on the third one, that was the touchdown. He lost contain. His job was to prevent Jackson Dart from buying time by rolling out to his left. He tried to win the B gap to the inside, gave up that edge, and now Jackson Dart is out there giving a guy like Malachi Fields a bajillion years, and all he's got to do is lose lose a linebacker. So, back to Pace, this is one of those context things, right? Yeah, it's a rookie and we're in the preseason and whatever. But but Malachi Fields is 6'4 and he's a receiver. Ivan Pace is like what, 5'9? 5'10? He's a linebacker. He's not going to be as fast, he's not going to be as tall as Malachi Fields. I thought Pace hung with Fields pretty well considering that it's a linebacker on a wide receiver, and got his hand up competitively best he could, made that throw be exactly as high as it was, and made Fields go up and get it. Physically, there is nothing more he could really do. And that's why he's not covering receivers all the time. He was in a really rough spot, functionally out of position, and made as good of play as I would expect him to play for that. So, that one doesn't bug me. And outside of that play, there were a bunch of really cool ones, a bunch of awesome blitzes, shooting the gap, good reads. I thought Pace had a really sweet day. I thought Golday was all right as well. Get to the rookies more later. Uh but the last thing I want to talk about with uh regard to kind of the headlines of these games in the preseason standouts, I tried to pay a little more attention to Ben Yurosek and Gavin Bartholomew. title: Jets Training Camp Live: RB Braelon Allen Joins the Show | NFL
text: The New York Jets got back to work Monday morning after making their preseason debut Friday night at Metife Stadium. The Jets, of course, three practices this week before they depart for Pittsburgh and that second preseason game against the Steelers. You are watching Training Camp Live presented by Honda. Eric Allen alongside Quincy Anuna. Let's get right to it. Jets in red zone work today. Gino Smith back at practice. Completes a pass to Bree Hall out of the back field. He goes up the sideline, goes down holding his midsection. >> Yeah. So, it looks like maybe it could be a groin. It could be something else sim similar to that. Hopefully with Bree, you know, he's not down too long. That's always a tough thing, right? You're coming out of a game. You don't want to go too crazy at practice. That's why they did some of the short yardage stuff. Um the hope is that, you know, he heals up quickly. Um and, you know, he's able to take care of himself. >> Yeah. And suddenly the Jets in an interesting position at the running back spot because Isaiah Davis has been out. He's dealing with the knee injury and Hall now sustains some kind of groin ailment. Hopefully, this is minor. And I think we're going to get to Aaron Glenn here in a couple moments. That means a lot of Brilan Allen, a lot of Kane Wan Woo. >> Yeah. That makes it really difficult. You're talking about Sweat, a guy that can really fill up the gaps, make it hard for offenses. Um, and then, you know, as we go down the line, right, OSai is another guy we want to start to see a little bit more. Uh, it's great that he gave those guys a veteran days off because, you know, they played really well this last game. Obviously, the score at the end of the game wasn't what we wanted to see, but it's preseason, right? So each section of the game is an opportunity for you to see how these guys are performing. I thought the ones did a good job in the game and so you know they got their opportunity to kind of take a rest today. >> All right, a lot to get to here. Garrett Wilson the two third down conversions including that beautiful catch from K Clubnik on the opening drive and then Ma Fitzpatrick is blitzing off the edge on play one in the preseason. Let's get to Aaron Glenn and then we're gonna come right back with Brilan Allen. >> Injuries that actually happened in practice today. Bree's uh strain is growing. Um I don't think it was a a big deal, but I want to make sure I I get the evaluation on that. Uh the one good thing about our players, man, they they are honest with their injuries and um if they can go, they can go, but we'll try to be precautionary with a lot of those, all right, to make sure that uh we do the right things. Other guys, Mike Hill Walker Calf um and then from the game, Bomba uh had a knee. All right. So, uh I think he'll be out a couple of weeks, but he'll be fine. Also, um it was good to get a number of our guys back. Uh I think you guys saw Sweat back on the field today. Uh OSA were back on the field today. So, it was good have those guys on the pitch count. Um it'll be good to watch the tape and see exactly how those guys operated. Um but it's good to have those guys back. When it came to practice, obviously, you guys seen it was a number of uh situations that I want to make sure that we hit. And I talk about this to the team quite a bit. um we was in a backed up situation and listen everything is magnified for the offense in a backedup situation. So um and even though it doesn't happen a ton throughout the season when you uh when you go back and study it man they're they're critical critical situations. So I want to make sure that we understand how exactly how to operate in those situation. And on the flip side, defensively, everything is magnified in the red zone for the defense and I think you guys saw that in the game of I mean, I think it was a second down and we get a holding call and we end up giving them a first down at the 2 yard line. So, um, I want to make sure our guys understand those things. Our guys do understand them. Um, and we have to operate, you know, the way we need to, uh, to be the best we can be. So, um, again, good situational practice. Uh, looking forward to tomorrow. Tomorrow will be a good, uh, a long haul. Um, I'm g stress them a little bit. So, uh, the guys know that and they can look forward to it. >> You're watching Training Camp Live presented by Honda. Eric Allen here alongside Quincy and Nunoir. And we're now joined by Brilan Allen. Brilan, just how good did it feel to get back on the field in game action Friday night against the Bucks? >> Felt great. Uh, it was a long road to get back to that point. Um, and I there was just a bunch of I I just had so much confidence going into that game, honestly. Um just knowing all the work that I put in and um you know the rehab and just just thinking about that moment being back on the field again is just when I got out there I was able to play free. >> Yeah. No, that's beautiful. I think you know as a guy that came back from injury a lot of times people are like oh you're proving it to everybody else. But how much did it prove to you that you can go out there be shifty right? Show your speed. I think you showed a lot just on that one run. How did it feel for you? >> Great. It was a lot of everybody pretty much asked me that, you know, right after that right after it happened. And the best way I could describe it was just like a like a sigh of relief, you know, like you like I knew what I could do. I knew what I was capable of. Um, but there's still, you know, that question coming off coming off an injury like that. So, um, once I got that, it's just like, you know, breath of fresh air. >> This is your third year, but obviously it feels a little bit different. Did you have butterflies going to the game? Obviously, you were excited to get on the field, but were there nervous emotions? >> There were there were butterflies. I wouldn't say I was nervous. Honestly, like like I said, I was just probably the most calm, most confident I've ever been, you know, stepping on a on an NFL field. And um you know, a lot of prayer before the game and leading up to that. So, um I just I felt great. It wasn't really any nervousness. Just, you know, a couple game day butterflies early in the morning, but once I got to the stadium, it was it was just go time. Now that you've had an injury, right, it kind of changes the way you view yourself in the NFL. Is there anything that that's kind of shifted in terms of how you prepare for games, practices, anything like that? >> Yeah, I mean, I've always been a guy like that that likes to take care of my that does a good job taking care of my body and, you know, warming up before practice and taking care of myself afterwards and stuff like that. And um I guess that kind of just has gone to another level. Um you know, it's it's it's kind of crazy like um I was talking to my people. I'll be here, you know, we practice at 8:30. My routine starts at 6:30. Yeah. >> And I get on the field, I'm still not like warmed. Like that whole two hours is all warming up and prepping my body and then it still takes me a while to get warmed up on the field. So, as much as it goes into it, you know, it seems like you always just got to do more and more. So, I'm still trying to find my stride and, you know, find out exactly what works for me. But, um, yeah, I would say there's definitely been a a focus in how I prepare. >> So, three carries the other night. Of course, you get into the end zone from 31 yards out. Take us through the touchdown from your perspective. Um man, it it kind of just happened like that really. It was inside zone play to the left. Um my first read, you know, um played outside. So just kind of we're coached to uh cut back one gap at a time, you know. So um just started reading it back and got all the way one-on-one with the corner. Just made a subtle move and um there it was off the races. >> Yeah, that's great. I think, [clears throat] you know, watching that play over, I think it was a great job. I think Tim Patrick has also had a great block on the safety, right? I think that kind of speaks to how this team is working together. What would you say is kind of the new theme this year because it feels like guys are really playing together a lot more. >> Yeah, I think that's the culture we're trying to build, you know, just that brotherhood and um I think everybody's bought into that >> and you got guys and and experienced vets like like Tim Patrick who uh have done it for a long time, done at a high level. um very smart um instinctual and and physical player as you saw on on the block like you know he pretty much washed that that whole part of the defense down and that's really what made it a one-on-one with the corner. So guys like him coming in doing the dirty work like that >> uh especially as long as he's been in the league he's very respectable >> but it wasn't a gaping hole. >> Can you talk about patience in that situation and then because the safety's coming up >> Yeah. trying to take an angle there and you got skinny in that burst. >> Yeah, like I said, it was kind of just like a little subtle like like on on on the tape. [snorts] >> I cut back. I made I made like two cuts. Um once I got to that to that backside, I want to say C gap and I saw the corner. It was kind of just like a little kind of maneuver, I guess, like a little slither. >> Um that's the best way I can really describe it. But yeah, just patience, like I said, not trying to force it, just kind of letting it come to me. Um, and then winning the one-on-one. >> The the hardest thing about being in the league is like a lot of times they put you in boxes, right? This is your role. But, you know, I think everybody knows exactly what they feel they're best at. What would you say? Not to say to the coaches like, "Oh, you're not using me right." But more so like this is what I really love. What scheme is your favorite as a running back? >> That's hard. I I honestly like all of them. I just like the ball. >> Of course. You know, so >> I' I've played in I mean, this is my third offense in three years in the league and I played in three different offenses in college. So, I've got a taste of everything. Um, and I'm used to running everything. Nothing's really new to me. >> Um, so whatever whatever works is my favorite. >> We talked about this in the studio not too long ago. You came back in the off season, full March. You get up to We know you're 6'5, but you got up to 250. How much you weigh right now? I made a joke the other night on the radio broadcast. I said, "You're just like Quincy because when he was playing, anytime he got in the weight room, he started throwing weights around. You can just get muscles everywhere and put on the weight. >> Yeah, as of this morning, um 246 and that's after breakfast. So, I probably wake up like 243, 244 around there. So, >> that's kind of where I want to be. Couple couple pounds left to to lose before the season. Um but I feel good right now. You're probably gonna knock out those pounds over the next couple weeks because Isaiah Davis dealing with the knee injury and then unfortunately today we saw Bree Hall go down after reception from Gino Smith in the red zone. What's your reaction when you see your brother go down like Bree did today? >> Yeah, it's never good. Obviously, you kind of stomach kind of drops a little bit, especially, you know, like a non-cont one and you see him go down. But, um, from the sound of it, don't sound very serious, too serious. Um, so I'm praying for him and hoping that he can get back as quick as possible. >> Can you tell us about practice overall? You got in the end zone a couple times as well. That a lot of situational work out there. Feels like you guys worked on backed up at the beginning of practice, then we saw a lot of red zone towards the end. >> Yeah, that's exactly right. We uh obviously, like you said, the the backed up situation, haven't got a whole lot of work in that. Um, so kind of installed our our um game plan for that. um you know went out to to move the ball in the red zone and um it was a good day at work. You know it was physical those those situations you know obviously they're stacking the box so as a running back you just know you got to get put your head down and get what you can. >> How does the body feel at this point of camp a couple weeks in. Um and now the second preseason game around the corner before you know it summer's going to be over. >> Yeah. Uh overall I feel pretty good. Um some residual soreness from the game still of course but overall I I can't complain. Um, you know, I I' I've done a lot of work, you know, building up my body to to sustain uh throughout camp and throughout the season. So, I can't say I'm I'm too disappointed with how I'm feeling. >> Brillan, appreciate your time. Just coming out and having a practice where he is the guy. So, he's put in a different situation. >> Yeah, I think that's super important. Your perspective, not only from the receiver, but maybe what you want to see from club the next time around. >> Yeah. Kate still got the ball to him and Garrett is one of the best receivers in the league of getting that getting the ball no matter where you throw it.
