He should be the guy to come in and be able to develop that quarterback that they draft next spring. So, um so, that's that's the big variable in this whole equation. >> I don't think we see him unless there's an injury until the bye week. Unless Darren Mougey and Woody Johnson step in if the Jets are two and nine and they say you're going to Klug Nick, we got we want to see what we have aka, you know, we want to basically get the top pick at that point and and we'll let the chips fall where they may. I don't think to your point, Rich, Glenn's going to ever want to go to Kade Klubnik cuz I just think Geno is is that much better than Kade Klubnik at this point. And that's not to say that Geno's great, but to your point, Glenn needs to win games and there's no way he's going to go to Klubnik and and bench Geno if you think Geno gives him the best chance to win. The difference in Aaron Glenn having a job or not might be one or two wins that Geno could provide for you that Klubnik wouldn't be able to as a fourth round pick in his rookie year. >> Yeah, but I preface this with if Geno's not playing well. You guys keep going back and I get it. You guys keep going back to Glenn's got to win. Geno's giving him the best chance to win. That sounds good now. But what if he's not playing well and what if they're not winning? >> Could Kliff Kingsbury worse? >> I mean anything is possible but he could be worse. Yeah, yeah, he definitely could. Of course he could be worse. >> I didn't think anyone was worse than Zach Wilson. They went to Tim Boyle and I go, you know what? I got to I got to take the L on this. So, like if if they're not playing Kliff Kingsbury and the Gino's bad, that would tell me that Kliff Kingsbury is still even worse than Gino at practice. >> But you know what's interesting in this is I wish I could inject Aaron Glenn with some truth serum because I think one of he's admitted that he's made mistakes last year. I mean he went on the radio the other day and said he he blew it by not calling the defense last year. So, I >> Which by the way, can I say one thing on that Rich because this really bothered me. I listened to that same conversation that he had and he said his biggest mistake was not calling the defense. I thought it was incredibly disingenuous though what he was saying because he talked about how his biggest mistake was not calling the defense and that's what got me the job and all this. When we all know his plan going into the off season was to hire Wink Martindale to call the defense and Woody put the kibosh on that and that's essentially what Wink Martindale publicly said on Pat Leonard's podcast several months ago. So, like he's making it seem like well that was the biggest mistake and he learned from it but no, he didn't even want to do it going into the off season. So, I thought that was a bunch of nonsense but whatever. >> Okay, I mean I'm not going to dispute that but the point I was we could go off on a tangent on that too but [clears throat] what I was going to make the the point I I was trying to make was I think Glenn one of the things that he did when he was did some soul searching in the off season was that I think he knows that he has to make quicker decisions and I think last year if you get gave him some truth serum, he would admit he stayed too long with Justin Fields. He I think he he should have got rid of him earlier. I think if he could do it again, he would have pulled the plug, you know, three you know, maybe after three or four games into the season. Now, I don't even know if he has a Tyrod Taylor on the roster now. So, I don't even know if he has that option. I mean >> Yeah. >> Last year at least he had a veteran in the bullpen who played a lot of NFL football. This year he doesn't even have that right now. >> That's that's a good point. You know, and the other thing too guys, the optics of we keep talking about like, well, what if the Jets aren't winning? Glenn's got to go into self-preservation mode. But there's a couple like the Jets and I don't think that they'll be this, but let's just say let's just say the Jets are two and seven, three and eight, or three and nine, something like that. And they're losing more because the defense is just getting gashed and giving up more and giving up some touchdowns and the offense doesn't resemble last year's offense. They're losing now 31-20, 34-23 instead of 46-9 or, you know, 40-3. Uh the offense is much more commensurate with what, you know, you would think it would be based on the additions and all the draft picks and the money. Uh so and and if that if they're two and nine and and Geno's getting them in the end zone, but they're not stopping anybody, Geno's Do you get to play Geno? So, there's a couple of different variables here and and the way it looks is going to matter. >> Well, that's not a good reflection on if his defense is getting gashed on a weekly basis, then, you know, that's his superpower. That's That's his superpower, right? So, UH >> YOU GOT TO FLY OVER THERE. >> AT LEAST HE'S LEANING INTO IT A LITTLE BIT WITH THE FANS.

title: Drake Maye & A.J. Brown Continue to Build Consistency at 2026 Patriots Training Camp
text: Training camp practice number 17 is in the books and the Drake May AJ Brown connection is coming alive. Let's break it down. >> [music] >> Welcome everybody to the Patriots training camp cast presented by New Balance and yes, Patriots are back in pads for a 10th time today guys. It seems like it's been a little bit of a grind here. We had the game on Thursday night. We had back in pads on Saturday, a little walk through on Sunday and then here today on Monday physicality picking back up and Paul, I'm going to start with you and little drill that interests me. It interests Cory Durden, too. Uh almost like we're putting on display some of the younger guys here. The team gathered around. We had, you know, some punt protection, some punt gunners trying to get down the field. Seemed like Mike Vrabel was trying to put these guys maybe a little bit on stage and let them perform in front of their teammates. Kind of fun. >> Yeah, now to quote Cory Durden, it was dope. Um [laughter] you know, it was a little bit different. I've been, you know, obviously at a million of these training camp practices and I hadn't really seen anything really like that where, you know, you and I think Durden sort of explained it. You know, it was an opportunity to get a lot of young guys on display in front of the whole team, got a little juice and energy going and uh yeah, different kind of blocking cuz it's it's gunners going against vice guys. It's interior punt protection. It's uh a running back on a blitz pick up. So, there's a lot of different things going on. One-on-one matchups. It was a little little bit of a break up of the camp monotony. >> Yeah, have you had some standouts in there? >> Yeah, it was pretty cool. I I hadn't seen anything like that before, either. I think the closest thing I could come up with was that at the Senior Bowl they often do this at the very end of the practice. They put the best edge rusher in the practice against the best tackle in the practice and so on and so forth. Uh it was cool, yeah. I thought a couple guys uh stood out. And I Cleil Jacobs had a really nice uh blitz. Riley Wilson continues to kind of bring some physicality to practice. But I thought the biggest one was uh Lomu over Akis. You know, I thought that was a really good rep for Caleb Lomu at on the right side too at at right tackle going up against Aquis. So, kind of you know, usually when they go to one-on-ones they have stations and it's O-line, D-line, and wide receivers and corners and tight ends and safeties and you know, linebackers and running backs. And this one was like the whole team together. So, it was kind of like you know, a showcase I would call it. It was pretty cool. >> I mean, what was interesting to me was just that you saw a lot of the depth guys and these are like things we've been talking about where the roles are. You know, no Britain Schooler. There's obviously special teams jobs, you know, not just here in the preseason but going into the regular season. So, just giving those younger guys an opportunity to kind of really put the put the spotlight on them, let them compete a little bit. I just I thought it was interesting. You can see the camp battles and where like these jobs are down the depth chart a little bit where guys are trying to carve out roles. So, that was fun but then of course we're waiting for the 11-on-11s and and you know, to get into things and you know, I just we talked about Drake Maye's been good, you know, maybe there have been some slow starts during camp. Thought today was one of his most consistent days and let's call it out the big the big play big passing play down the field to Antonio or Antonio AJ Brown. We saw him Paul. We saw him open. We're like, throw it throw it. Nice big play. >> He was open a couple times down the field today. That was the one that they targeted him and what I liked about it is if you remember way back, you know, everybody is like, well, you know, he's gone down field some before that was kind of a double move and they they sort of fooled Christian Gonzalez on that play. This was just, you know, off the line Mike and I immediately were like, it was like you know, the old Randy Moss with the mailbox. Like he was he was open 10 yards into the route. Just really separated. Nice to see. I was joking Ev with Mike during practice. I could really see virtually anything from AJ Brown this year. If you told me he was going to catch 100 for 1,500 yards and 12 touchdowns, I'd say, yeah, okay, yeah, I could see that or something much less than that because there are times where he runs down the field like that and he's 5 yards in the clear on Charles Woods and there's other times where he's getting locked up on the sideline by by the same guy on an out route. So, good to see a big play like that from May though because I I don't think we've seen A.J. Brown downfield all that often. >> Yeah, definitely the most separation he's created on a route down the field and it was good to see. I thought the throw in the two-minute drill was even better. >> Yeah, I was going [laughter] to get to that. Nice crossover. >> The crossing route to A.J. Brown was ridiculous. I mean that was a sick throw. I thought the two-minute drill in general from him Drake Maye today was really sharp. They threw a lot of blitzes at him and they had a lot of blitz beaters that they had planned and snuck Remounda Stevenson behind a blitz for a big gain to get him down into field goal range. That was probably the best, you know, they don't do two minutes anymore is now a minute and 15 or a minute and five. That was the best two-minute drill that they've had all summer. I would have I mean five for five super sharp all the way down the field highlighted by the the Brown play but couple of downfield completions to Brown couple of downfield completions to Dobbs again today especially in that first team period. I thought they were the offense in general was really sharp. >> Yeah, Paul you noticed at one point a little you know, a little cadence work for Drake Maye some of the pre-snap stuff and I think that's an area I'm really focusing on. It's so critical for his development. >> Yeah, you know, like this when we talk about the you know, the teams doing situational work or down and distance stuff, you know, that's the kind of thing I think it was a third and two in that period that we're talking about and they're looking to get a cheap first down. So, they they run to the line they they you know, they get settled up and it's a hard count for Drake Maye. Now, the defense was disciplined. They didn't bite on it but some of those kind of minutia things I I think they can get lost sometimes but those can be really really important plays in the in the span of a drive in the span of a season. So, yeah, it was good to see them getting to work on some of that situational stuff. >> Yeah, successful two-minute drill Borgalis hit the field goal there at the end. I just got to highlight Romeo Dobbs too because it's been, you know, a couple days since we've done a a training camp cast. He was good again Saturday, had a couple catches again today. Uh suddenly, and I know you had a small seat concern that slowly sunk to like two font and maybe off the off the page now, Evan. >> I'm erasing [laughter] it at this point. >> That small seat He's been the most consistent receiver over the last week and a half in in this team. And you see now what A.J. Brown did today and you see what Dobbs is kind of doing. I said to Paul in the stands, I'm like, "All this talk about Kayshon Boutte and and Efton Chism, I'm like, >> [clears throat] >> I don't really care. These two guys are starting to really make it work." Pop Douglas has had a good camp. >> Yeah. >> Offense, I'm getting excited about. >> Yeah, I thought today was even better because, you know, look, with Dobbs, I I love the 50/50 balls as much as anybody, but I don't want to make a living off of those types of contested catches. The couple of throws that he made to Dobbs today in the first team period especially, strong hands, open at the top of the route, balls out on time, you know, Paul's Patriot plays types of thing, right? It was It was exactly that. And it wasn't Look, I I love that he mossed a couple guys on Saturday too, but I again, I don't want them to make a habit out of that's the only way that they're moving the football. Uh he made a catch in front of I think it was Craig Woodson that he kind of had to go back and and grab it. It was a little bit behind him and he just snatched it out of the air and then pulled it away from Woodson to make sure that Woodson couldn't, you know, bat the ball out of his hands. His hands are are really good, really strong. You can see that that strength and uh the ability to attack the ball at the catch point. >> Another one low that he caught that felt like Gabe kind of short-armed a little bit. One other guy I want to bring up though, guys, is Elijah Ponder because Look, we've seen Gabe Backus now for a couple weeks. It's going to be a work in progress with him. It's not He's not coming right in and, you know, doing everything they need him to do. Dre'Mont Jones is a solid player. We've hit on this point a lot, Paul. I feel like the coaching staff is high on Ponder that he had a pretty good day today. I think he's becoming a critical player for this team and could be on the verge of a big season and all works out well. >> I think for better or worse, he's probably going to be your starter opposite Draymond Jones you know, when when the season starts. I can't imagine how our Landry's going to be up to speed that quickly after missing the entirety of camp. Um, and you're right about Aquis. I think it's been a little bit slower. He also missed the start of camp. So, he's, you know, catching up for lost time. I did notice Ponder on back-to-back plays in one of those the earlier 11-on-11s that were down closer to where the media tent is and you know, he flashes a little bit. I think he's got a great attitude. You listen to him talk and he just, you know, he's an undrafted guy and I don't think he forgot that. Like I think he knows how tenuous it can be. I think he's constantly working. They wanted him to work a little bit more in being a three-down player, you know, stopping the run. I think he's taken that to heart working on his techniques in that regard. So, that's the kind of stuff you guys want to see. Like you you have young players. We all we focus on draft picks, but uh, Evan, I know you're going to be working on some year two stuff. That's the kind of stuff you want to see. Year two guys getting better. >> Yeah, it just feels like >> those guys have the most opportunity to increase the ceiling of the team because I I don't know if I'm not to like talk bad about the rookie class, but how many opportunities is that rookie class really going to get when all it's all said and done? You know, Caleb Lom was going to be a backup to start the season. Eli Haroldson's going to be behind Henry and maybe he's going to chip in, but he's going to be behind Hunter Henry. Uh, Gay Aquis is probably the one guy that maybe has a chance to play early and play a lot. Uh, but Ponder's been great. I had him with a couple pressures today. Thought he stuffed the run as well. So, those are the types of things that you want to see. You know, he can rush the passer. He did that last year and did a pretty good job of it. It's going to be can he play on first and second down and set the edge and stop the run and do that sort of thing. I still kind of feel like Ponder and Aquis together as a three-down player instead of just one of them playing all three downs. Like maybe Aquis is your early down edge setter and then Ponder is your third down pass rusher for Akers in the in his rookie season. So, a little bit of like Anthony Jennings and Ponder last year. >> I like it. Well, that's going to do it for this edition of the Camp Cast, but two more practices. If you guys can get down here, join practices against the Eagles on Wednesday Wednesday and Thursday. So, those should be a great take. Last chance to see this team before getting going on the regular season. Two more preseason games to go. It's all coming together.

title: Kayshon Boutte, Morgan Moses, Cory Durden & More Address the Media | Patriots Press Conference
text: Hey, how are you? >> Hanging in there. How are the kids? First day of school. >> Oh. >> First day of school. Yeah, first day of school back home. >> Dad camp over? >> Uh yeah, I mean, I got the phone call this morning and was like, "Yo, Dad, can I get into your cologne stash?" Like, Isaiah's in sixth grade, so he's feeling himself now, you know? He's all about the ladies now, so >> [laughter] >> I definitely did. I I said, "One spray though, one spray." He's like he's like a four or five spray guy, you know? >> How cool is that? Part of dad hood. >> I mean, it's it's it's enjoyable, man. You know, um especially you know, when you get the chance to to have your sons in the locker room after the game and the guys see them and you know, they take them in as uh you know, as family, you know? Um Uncle Will and and and the guys and stuff. Um so, it's just good to just have, you know, especially at my stage in my career is having kids that are and having sons that are able to have the same dreams and aspirations, you know? And they get to see it every day and they get to see the the the camaraderie that we build in the locker room with new guys and older guys. So, um it's just it's a good thing. >> What age did they start to realize Dad's job is different >> Well, I I joke with the guys all the time because like like Drake and those guys will be like, "You know who your dad is?" And I'm like, "Look, they don't care. They just want Robux. They want like they you know what I'm saying? They want they want bubble tea. They want things like that." But you know, I think it's you know, especially you know, coaching them in the off season and doing things like that and then them seeing me prepare for the season and get ready and you know, just them seeing the work that I put in and the days that I you know, the nights that I got to stay up and recovering things like that and um and so, it's full circle, you know? Um I'm I'm I'm glad to be able to set an example for them and I'm I tell everybody I'm probably more proud of them being my sons than them them you know, me being their dad. So, um it's a great opportunity that I get to wake up and show them every day. >> What's the relationship with Marcus like? You know, I saw that relationship with you two last year. >> Well, you ask Mac. Mac will be like, "Yo, that's that's Morgan's fourth son." So, it's like We went out to eat the other night and I had my sons with me and uh and I would they they were getting a little rowdy at the table and Marcus is over there like and Mac is like, "Yeah, that's That's Marcus' son right there." >> As we wrapped up our day 17, >> Say 17? >> day 17 of your starting five on the D-line, where do you feel like you guys are at >> Um just keep on building. You know, every day um just to come out with a with a plan um for yourself individually and for for the offense together collectively and um you know, at the end of the day, everything runs through us up front. You know, we're the engine of this uh this offense. Um no matter all the parts and fancy parts we got outside, you know, A.J. Brown and those guys, but uh it's for us to be able to control the line of scrimmage and um and obviously uh you know, we we had a little conversation about the things that we did last year that don't mean anything, you know, it's but we got to write our own story this year and um and we're doing that. Just you know, you know, you see AVT over there at the left guard spot and Will getting comfortable with him and you know, obviously I played with AVT before and so I know what type of person and type of player he is and what he brings to the offensive line and then just me and Mike um just keep on establishing what we left off last year and then obviously Jared in the middle um his first year playing center and just you know, making sure he he gets all of us on the same page and so um just every day just coming out and just working on the fundamentals, the details and the techniques and um and just let it rip. >> It seems like you guys can be better than a year ago. Do you agree with that? Like how good do you just feel about the group and where you guys stand exactly? >> Um you know, we're not putting no measuring tape on it. You know, we're just going out there every day and just focusing on what we the task at hand, you know, um we got a great defense that we go up against every day and that gives us a whole bunch of looks and um and for us it's just to be able to get to the line of scrimmage, you know, um and be able to operate and play as five equals one and um I think when you do that as offense line, you know, you see a lot of greatness in between the between the plays. >> What do you like to accomplish this season? >> What what what >> Along those lines, just from what you're talking about this whole offseason, what have you observed from how the the organization has sort of transitioned from Super Bowl sort of heartbreak, right? >> Yep. >> And then just resetting and then being sort of a target of the other teams now. >> Yeah, yeah. I mean I don't think it's a heartbreak, man. You live and you learn. You know, you know, what we did last year was was successful. Obviously, we didn't walk out with the with the trophy, you know, like we wanted to, but you you got to learn how to lose before you can win. And I think that we've digested that well over the off season and coming together and adding new pieces, but also understanding that like just because we got new pieces and new receivers and new DBs and sorry, defensive players and things like that like, you know, football is football and we still got to play, you know, we got to put the ball down. We got to play in between the line of scrimmage and we got to move the ball and we got to you know, we got to stop the ball and we got to continue building and iron sharpens iron. So, I think you know, just coming in every day with with something to work on and not like a whole menu of things to work on and just get better 1% better every day. >> What have you seen in Drake as far as becoming more vocal? >> As in Drake? >> Yeah. >> Um just the comfortability of you know, obviously year two in the offense, you know, getting his feet down, getting grounded and obviously, you know, the playmakers he has around him, but obviously just you know, he's an intelligent player. He's a young intelligent player and he's asked to do a lot in our offense, but you know, he's taking that on the chin and he's operating the way he needs to operate. >> Morgan, you guys had a couple of guys >> Yeah, you know. I got you. >> What would you like to accomplish this week? >> Continue what you did last week in joint practices. You got two coming up. >> Um you know, obviously establish ourselves as you know, what we need to do up front. You know, obviously they got a great D-line. They got a great offensive line and you know, football has never changed over the course of years that it's been played is one in the line of scrimmage. And so we got a great task at hand and to see where we're at and we're going to step you know, step on this football field and and go at it. >> Morgan, what was your message to >> Just wondering how you guys were adjusting. You had a couple guys get hurt in the preseason game. Just how you guys adjust in the offensive line. >> It's football, man. Everybody gets hurt, man. You know, to say we you say what? Practice 17? I mean if to tell people that's not hurting that we've been in pads for 17 days, Um, now, be lying, but um, you know, just uh, you know, iron sharpens iron and you look to the guy to the left and the right of you knowing that he's going through the same thing and you can push a little bit a a little bit harder. So, um, for the guys that are coming in that are that are new, you know, kind of replacing guys that are hurt or whatever the case is, it's just for us to bring them along and and and let them know understand uh, what the uh, the mold and and the the model of what we want to be it looks like. >> I saw you address the team after practice on Saturday. What was your message then? >> Oh, I'm just keep on going, man. Um, nothing simple, you know, the message between me and the team and it stays stays between me and the team, but we just got to keep on going. We got to keep on fighting through these days. I know it's a long it's long days and I try to tell the guys like, you know, when I first got in the league training camp ended at 9:00. So, uh, you know, this is a >> we get out a little earlier. So, uh, um, just to just to grind, man. You just got to you got to find uh, you got to find you got to find a quiet a quiet place in the grind. You know, you know, sometimes sometimes when the storm is is is loud outside, man, you got to sit in it sometimes and and you got to fight your way out of it. So, um, you know, we're we're going to be better for it. >> Morgan, I noticed I'll take one more. I noticed um, you and Elijah having back and forth today in practice. I was wondering, what have you noticed from him and his game? You know, obviously last year you DFA'd and now >> Yep. Yep. >> He's been in a starting role this at this point. >> Yeah, yeah. Uh, it doesn't matter where you start, man, where you where you finish and um, I think he's done a great job of uh, obviously elevating himself throughout the season last year and then working on some things that he needed to work on this off season and um, he's established himself as a as a as a player, you know, um, um, not just a role player, but a a player that we depend on out here and um, you know, I'm glad that we get a chance to go go against him every day, you know, we get different looks between him and Draymond and um, and uh, Jamonte and it's it's been it's been good, man. So, um, you know, iron sharpens iron and we look forward to just, you know, the battles every day. >> I saw the quarterback go down in there and a little exchange with >> Yeah, yeah. >> What happened there? >> No, I was just going to come in at the quarterback at the next play. That's what I I really what happened. Um, but no, um, uh, you know, it is it's training camp, man, you know, um, you know, at the end of the day, you know, we got to fix some things, but you know, he's all right, man, you know, some bumps and bruises, man. I think it's his first hit of the other of the off season, so I mean the preseason, so we'll we'll see how it goes. >> All right, good. >> All right, you have a good one. Yep. >> Hold on. Hold on. Let me finish you off. All right, we good. >> Yesterday, Todd Downing said that the way that you've approached this off season is something that he will take for the rest of his coaching career. Did you hear that? What's that mean to you? How do you feel like you've approached this off season? >> Um I think just blocking out the noise. That's the main thing. Uh we all hear the stuff that's going on and things like that. But like I always said, I'm where I'm at, my feet here, so I'm not worried about what's next or what's behind me, but being present. >> Quez, what do you think you've learned either about yourself or the offense through the first 3 weeks of camp here? >> Uh we're pretty competitive. Um I'll start with the receivers, you know, that's the guys I work with every day. But um we all enjoy coming to work with each other every day. We all make plays, you know. We all cheer each other on. We support each other. We want the best for each other, so every day we come out and push to be the best. >> Is that something that's not always a given in every year? Like you said, you learn that, so that must be something that you're experiencing. >> Nah, I didn't say that, but I'm saying it's it's pretty much every year, you know. Um you got to build those guys. Like y'all work together, you know, there's people you're familiar with, people you got to work with, so building that bond important. >> What's it been like getting to know A.J. Brown? >> Uh been cool. Um great receiver. He's been doing great things since he first got into the league, but um being his teammate been good, you know, he help us on opposite side getting looks. 10 times out of 10 he one-on-one, he win his match up, so I mean that's that's pretty big for the offense. >> Yesterday, um when Todd Downing he mentioned how you kind of are an example that he will continue to use this on professionalism this uh throughout training camp. What does it mean to have, you know, your wide receiver coach saying that to you and kind of that praise? >> Um I mean, at the end of the day, I've just blocked out the noise, you know, I can't control what go on anything like that, but um since Todd got here, he's been a big part of my development and um I trust him, he trusts me. You know, he pushes for us to be the best every day and we come out and give him that. So >> How's he earned that trust from you? You know, you've had a lot of coaches over your career, right? >> Yeah. Um I just say trust start with um doing the right thing, you know? Um somebody tell you how to do something, you got to do it, you know? Um harping in on the little details, the way they want things done, keep continuing doing that the right way is only going to get better. >> What have you seen from Demario Douglas since he came in the draft class driving the second round? How have you seen him progress throughout his >> He always open. Think it's pretty simple, but um he do the little things right. Um we both came in, built a cool relationship, both going on year four. Think we were sitting out talking the other day about how fast time go, but um you know, he continue to get open, catch the ball, make plays when he's supposed to and that's what he's supposed to do. >> You mentioned how fast time can go. >> Mhm. >> It's your fourth year here. >> Do you feel like like when you look back >> when you look back >> Uh just improvement every year, you know? Um like you said, you look back 3 years ago to today standing here today, you know, made tremendous improvement. So shout out to that. Mhm. Uh which group? >> The wide receivers. >> Oh, no. Uh we we cheer each other on. You know, we want the best for each other. When somebody make a play, we all going in his zone. Rome made the uh grabs the other day, we all celebrating. You know, there's no hate. We want the best for everybody, but it's competition everywhere you go. So um like I said, it's all about opportunity, making the best of yours. >> Speaking of you years ago, you Christian both kind of in the public eye with your situation. Do you guys discuss your respective situations amongst each other? >> Uh you talking about Gunther? >> Uh no. I mean, we really don't talk. At the end of the day, we just come out here play football, you know? That's stuff we can't control, you know? Um like Gunther said, you kind of worrying about that too much. It kind of take away your focus on the football field, so. Um, I think the message the message this week is really just uh physicality, you know. Um, Philly coming here this week, a great team. But, um, it all start up front, so we got to handle our thing up front, win our battles outside. You know, they known for winning. They're a good team. They came here 3 years ago. We joint practiced with them. So, I think that was pretty cool. So, another opportunity 2 days to get better. Uh, it's competitiveness, you know. Um, not going against the same guys every day. You know, um, every receiver we get good matchups. This upcoming week we got Quez, DeSean, and we got Woolen. So, I mean, that's good for all us guys seeing different guys. So, yeah. >> Kayshon, given the conversations you have with the front office this offseason, do you and Elliott speak much during the summer when training camp's going on about what he's hearing or dealing with? >> Nah, I mean, as far as the trades, I feel like I pretty much answered everything. So, there's no need for me to really talk about it anymore. So, yeah. >> So, you don't talk to him about it either? >> No. >> You you don't know? Pretty great catch a couple days ago, 2-minute drill. We haven't talked since 2 cents then. Just sort of take us through that moment and those type of plays, what do what do they do for you? >> Uh, 2-minute drill. Big-time players make big-time plays in big-time situations. Simple. >> Thanks, Kayshon. >> Yeah, pretty much. >> How's everybody doing? >> Good, how about you? >> I'm great. >> What's the mentality this week? How important with the two joint practices and >> Just excited. Um, you know, it's always just take advantage of the opportunity to hit somebody else, not hit our teammates. So, just excited to have a good football team coming here, and you know, bring the best out of both teams. So, looking forward to that. >> Sorry. How do you feel like you've been progressing throughout camp specifically when it comes to that nose tackle role that we've kind of talked about you moving into? >> Uh, I feel like I've progressed the way that I need to. Um, you know, I'm right on track where I want to be. Just trying to be prepared for week one against Seattle. So, feel like I'm right on track. >> Mike told us earlier today that some of the best traits that you have you got a high energy and a very coachable. How much of a point of pride is that for you to be able to kind of check both those boxes? >> Um, it's a lot. I mean, you know, I feel like coaches value guys that, you know, that are coachable, that, you know, take the coaching and put it on the field. So, that's that's something that I take a lot of pride in. >> You also said too that you're one of the biggest talkers. >> Yeah, I've always been that way. Um, you know, talking trash is a part of it. I mean, we're some of the best players in the world. So, you know, why not have fun while you're out there? >> Does that help kind of bring energy to to you specifically in in your game if you get talking a little bit? Do you feel good? >> Me personally, yeah, but some of my teammates, you know, it's up and down with them. So, you know, like if a DB, if I'm talking trash to a wide receiver, I don't go against the receiver, my DB is. So, you know, he might be like, "Chill out." cuz he got to go against that guy. So. >> Who's the biggest talker on the offense? >> Um. >> Who's the biggest on the defense? >> On offense, that's probably Pop. Pop definitely the biggest trash talker on the offense. >> Corey, um, that that drill in the middle of practice where it looked like everyone was sort of watching it and it was like highlighting those specific players that were in the drill. How would you describe like that from a player's perspective? >> Um, I think it's dope. Uh, you know, coach give the opportunity, you know, it was a lot of younger guys going in that drill. So, just for coach to give the opportunity for you to perform in front of your teammates. I think that, you know, it's a it's a pride thing, obviously, but, you know, it brings energy to everybody. You know, nobody wants to lose in front of the whole team. So. >> Have you ever seen something like that before? >> Um, no. Not since I've been in the league, you know, in college we did stuff like that, but not That's my first time doing that since I've been in the NFL. >> And how would you describe the energy where you were with the group of players sort of watching it? >> It was fun. Uh, you know, just having energy when a defensive guy wins, you know, we always have energy. So. >> How uh how much of a help is Milton throughout your whole process? >> Uh, he's been a tremendous help. Uh, you know, just being able to talk to a guy like that, you know, Milton's obviously played a lot of ball in a lot of big games, going to what, three Super Bowls, whatever it was, uh, two Super Bowls. So, you You having a guy like that to kind of pick his brain and get his opinion on different stuff. It's it's very helpful. >> How much have you grown over the last year? I I know you came here in the start of the year, the start of the season last year. You've already been here at this point of the season, but how much have you grown in the system and as an individual? >> Um Individually, you know, I feel like I've grown a lot. You know, I feel like I was obviously a good I like to think I'm a good person before I got here, but you know, I enjoy my team. Just trying to be the best teammate I can be. I really enjoy the locker room, so. And then in the scheme I'm playing fast. You know, I know this defense like the back of my hand. It's my second year in it, so you know, I'm I know everybody's what everybody's doing around me, so just being able to play fast is very helpful. >> Does that help with your confidence given that it's your second year at the >> The confidence is there cuz it's not necessarily knowing what to do. I know what to do. It's just how fast and productive to do it. >> You personally, how much have the joint practices helped you? >> They helped me a lot. You know, we obviously it's unscripted, so you're going against a team that you know, we don't know anything they're doing. They don't know anything we're doing, so it's a live football game. >> Corey, it looks like you guys are having a lot of success during these team periods with the run and kind of stopping the run. Has that been a point of emphasis and where do you feel like that success is coming from? >> Um yeah, it's I mean you guys know how last year started. We won what? Seven, eight games in a row under 50 yards, so you know, the pride's there. You know, that's something that we preach every day. Stopping the run. To be successful in the NFL, you have to stop the run and then earn the the right to rush the passer, so that's like a big point of emphasis for our defense. >> Anything specifically you want to work on for the course of next year? >> Um just being an active pass rusher. Um >> You know, my I want to kind of alluded to like your pass rushing skills. >> Yeah, I've I feel like I'm a I'm a good pass rusher, you know, I I want to go get five sacks this year, so that's something that I've worked on a lot this summer and you know, this this off season OTAs just being active in the pass rushing. Trying to get on the field on third down, so. >> Is there anyone who's been kind of like a mentor in the practice trying to progress as a pass >> Um yeah, I actually had the opportunity to work with Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark this summer, so you know, just being able to soak up knowledge from guys like that is very helpful cuz, you know, those I mean Quinnen Williams just got that massive contract. So, just, you know, those are those guys are dominant players. >> Where did you guys work out at? >> Uh in Vegas. >> How did that come together? >> Uh with uh Max Crosby. I got the same agent as him. So, you know, we kind of just all put it together. >> What kind of things did they help last year? >> Um just, you know, pass body movements and like how to manipulate like the offensive lineman when you get them in different positions and stuff like that. Just being able to, you know, work around those things. >> So, you're going to get paid after this >> That's the goal. Don't Don't Don't say that too loud right now. Don't get me in trouble, but that's the goal. >> Thanks, Quinnen. Thanks, Quinnen. >> Thank you, guys. >> How How y'all doing? >> Doing good. >> What do you uh make of your camp so far? it's just a start, you know, we just we trying to get better before the season. So, just trying to take it day by day. >> How would you describe your relationship with Quinnen Williams? >> Yeah, that's my guy. I mean, we've been through obviously, you know, the whole rookie rookie thing together. And um you know, we continue to build that relationship on and off the field. So, yeah, you know, that's my guy. That's my teammate, you know, go go to war with him. >> Day Day 17, how much more comfortable are you just feeling that everything feels sitting where you were from a year ago? >> Yeah, definitely much more uh comfortable, you know, just you know, making uh new relationships with the new guys coming in, but you know, just building on uh the old relationships from last year uh with all the people that were already here. So, I mean, definitely making strides and definitely feeling more comfortable. >> Where do you feel like you've been most improved? I would I mean, I would just say all around, you know, whether that's uh stopping the run, you know, getting to the quarterback. Um and just you just focusing on the little details to do those things. So, I'll just say all around for sure. >> How much emphasis Oh god, my god. Just say how much emphasis have you put on first and second down? Mike mentioned when he was talking about you today like sort of understanding his role in in that aspect. >> Yeah, I mean that that's a big thing, you know, stopping the run is, you know, you can't you can't get to the quarterback if you don't stop the run. So, you know, that's the major emphasis in our in our defense. So, I mean, in the off season just, you know, taking steps, you know, working technique and doing like that to to, you know, better my my craft my game. So. >> How much has confidence been a factor for you to continue to grow? >> I mean, I think confidence does a does a lot for for any player, you know, and when when you you know, come in day in and day out and put in the work and you start seeing yourself grow, you know, your confidence grows as well. So, I think that plays a big part for me. So. >> Why is it you hear a lot about the year two leap? Do you feel like that's real and do you feel it happened to yourself in the >> Um I mean, it definitely feels different coming in year two, you know, with the with the same system with the same coaches and uh you know, just building building all those relationships and building with the team. So, I mean, yeah, it feel it feels good compared to coming in not knowing anybody, not knowing, you know, the system and not knowing really just the NFL and how it works. So. >> Speaking of rookies, being around Gabe now for a couple weeks on the field finally, what strikes you about him? >> Yeah, I mean, the dude loves football and he plays you can see it on the field the way he plays. Um and he yes, I mean, he is a rookie, but we still, you know, still growing our relationship and we're still building off learning off each other, you know, in our our game. So, you know, I can't wait to get to the season, though. >> And how do you view the year two leap? Were there any areas as a first year player that were kind of difficult to really get your head around and now in your second season feel a lot easier to kind of digest? >> I think the main thing for me was probably the playbook, you know, just being able to know what you're doing and be able to play free because, you know, it's you have the knowledge to do so. So, I think, you know, coming in year two having the the playbook, you know, you know, I had a little play here and there, but you know, just being able to hone in on the little details of those plays. So. >> How much too is it just like comfort? Last year you come in undrafted free agent, you got to fight for everything. Not that you're not fighting for it now, but like I did this. I was able to make it through a season. I was able to contribute to a team that got to the Super Bowl. Now being in year two like, just that you're talking about the comfort. It's got to be night and day. >> Yeah, I mean you know coming to training camp you know everyone is still trying to fight for a role and stuff like that but definitely just coming in knowing what to expect you know coming to this training camp. It does does help a little bit. So you know I'm I'm trying to take advantage of that as much as possible. >> What's something you've learned either about your own game and your progress or the defense as a whole? I think one thing I'll say probably like effort and finish probably makes makes up for a lot of you know MAs misassignments or just like not a good play but if you finish finish to the ball whatever you you still get to the to a ball carrier I think it make up for a lot of stuff. >> What comes to mind when you say that? Like what plays made you learn that so far this summer? >> I think it's just like watching tape. You've seen all over the all over tape you know all over throughout the league. You know seeing players you know hustle and that that is just the main thing. You they they just got motors and they just always going constant non-stop so seeing that I'm trying to apply that to my game as much as possible. >> Sort of build on that. There's sometimes where players just don't have a consistent motor. Is that something that you as a player have or is it sort of innately you have a motor or is that something you can really just pick up as you're a professional player? >> I mean I think you you you got to work at it for sure. I mean no one is going to go out there and be completely so I mean we you got to run you got to you know build your stamina up any way you can so some people is running some people is doing other things but so I'm to get better. I mean I to keep it as simple as all it is. You know we got this opportunity to play against you know a good football team and so we just going to take it day by day and just go out there have fun. Thanks. I appreciate it. Hey, how's it going? Good. How's it going? >> I'm good. You? >> Appreciate it. Appreciate it. Thank you. >> How uh take us through getting here and everything else since you've been here, what's been going on? How good do you feel or getting better as far as how you feel? >> Yeah, yeah, feel great. Um luckily when I was here last year preseason um pretty much same coaches, same playbook. So um wasn't a whole lot of learning in terms of um playbook-wise, but uh just getting assimilated and getting accustomed to everything. It's been fun. >> Is there any Given that you were kind of here last season it was Drake you guys were all starting in this new offense with Josh. Now it's been a year and is there any major change you've noticed in Drake given that kind of peace had this time to develop in the offense? >> Yeah, yeah, I think I think now this is Drake's third year. So I mean extremely confident in what he's doing. Commanding the huddle, commanding the offense. Um exactly what you want in looking for out of your quarterback for sure. >> Michael, what was it like when you were gone? What were you up to? What were you working on? >> Yeah, so uh off season training man I was back home in Texas uh with family, friends, training and uh that's pretty much it man. Life was pretty simple. >> Right. >> Yes, sir. >> What's the competition right now in the in the running back room? >> Yeah, I mean competition is um it's a part of the league, you know what I mean? Uh we got some great guys in there. We all just kind of building off each other, feeding off each other. Um making sure we all learning and staying up-to-date and um it's been pretty good. >> What was the reunion with Mondre like when you got when you got back in the room? >> Yeah, it was it was cool man. It was cool man. Um didn't didn't know when I left last year didn't know if we'd ever get a chance to you know at least be on the same team again, but we did link up again and not only just Drake, but you know Trey's still here and uh addition of the young guys laying. So um it's been cool coming back to familiar faces. >> What was it like playing in a preseason game without even practicing beforehand? >> Yeah, uh that was fun. It was It was fun. It was fun. It was a It was a new challenge something I've never done before. So uh just embraced it, attacked it and um just did the most that I could with it. >> What was kind of the message from coach in that circumstance when you come in, no practice or anything and you're thrown right into that game situation. >> Yeah, not really any message, you know what I mean? Just you know, this is my seventh year now, so we're just kind of coming in, you know, being a pro, learning what I need to learn, and just going out to execute. >> You mentioned that you knew the playbook. Did it kind of feel like riding a bike in a sense, or just like coming back in and getting right back to the plays that you were kind of learning last year? >> I'm sorry I cut you off, but yeah, I guess you could say that. Everything, like I said, there were some changes, but for the most part everything is kind of similar to what I was familiar with last year. So, from a learning standpoint, not a huge learning curve, but again, some changes. >> Is it nice also kind of working with Tony again? >> Oh, yeah, most definitely. You know, coach Duz, he's the same every day. One thing I can definitely respect about him, he's going to stay on his coaches hard, you know, and he's going to make sure we know what to do once we're out there. >> What is it about your skillset that makes you fit in with this team? >> I think just being able to be versatile, you know what I mean? Just being able to run, catch, protect, be available on special teams, just kind of being kind of a jack of all trades, so to speak. Yeah, thank you guys. Appreciate it. >> Yeah, I mean, it's definitely a step up from college. You know, we I'm playing center here for now. I mean, it's been it's been pretty fun. Speed's been pretty fast, but I'm just trying to enjoy it, get better. >> Jacob, what's your focus been in those one-on-ones? You've had some good days in the drill. >> Yeah, I'm just trying to get my hands on. That's my goal, just get my hands on and win. >> from Connecticut, went to Harvard for a couple of years. What's it like just being here in New England? >> It's awesome to be back in Boston. Yeah, I went to school for 4 years up here. I love the city. It's a great city. New England's a historic place to be, so I'm very excited to be here. >> What was the mindset when Ben went down with the injury, and you sort of Did it catch you by surprise? What were your sort of those first snaps like for you? >> Oh, you know, obviously, the first thing that crossed my mind was, you know, I know how much Ben has been working and it was really unfortunate to see that happen. Uh Uh you never wish that for your teammates and and you know, that was super unfortunate. Uh but, you know, I knew I had to go play, so I just kind of go play football. Pretty much. >> Jacob, in college, you spent time kind of everywhere on the offensive line. Has there been any talks here of potentially learning other positions on the interior? >> Like I said before, I'm playing center right now. If they want to move me around, they want to move me around, but right now I'm just focused on center. >> Jacob, what's met your expectations coming into training camp? Obviously, your first one. And what's been >> I mean, I don't really know what to expect since it's the NFL, so I've only ever played high school and then college and I knew this would be a step up. Uh it's the game's fast. Um just, you know, trying to find my way around, get better every day, trying to get 1% better every day, probably. >> Being a local guy, have you been in touch with old coaches or old teammates? >> Yeah, I've had a lot of a lot of coaches from Florida State and Harvard reach out, old teammates, of course. Um being from New England, a lot of Patriots fans uh in my circle and and in my high school and all that, so that's been really cool. I've been talking, reconnecting with a lot of people, yeah. >> How many uh friends and family were at the preseason game? >> My parents, my sister, uh my fiance's cousin actually was there cuz he works at uh Whoop Labs. Um a lot and then uh my my college teammate and then some other people as well. Yeah. >> Do you have any memories growing up about Patriots? I assume you're >> I mean, it's hard not to remember the Patriots when I was growing up from, you know, I was born in 2002. I think they went on a little bit of a run. I'm not too sure, but um no, yeah, I mean, it's it's awesome to be able to play where so many great football players have played before me. >> You obviously went to a prestigious college. Did Was the goal for you always the NFL or, you know, a lot of time you go to Harvard, you're probably set up for life just with the degree itself. >> Um I mean, a lot of people like to say that, but I think, you know, it depends how hard you work, no matter what you're doing. I went to Harvard because I really liked my coach there, the O-line coach, and uh coach uh Keegan Kennedy. Uh coach Tim Murphy's a historic coach there. I went up, I visited, I was like, this is the place to be. Um I I didn't have too many offers, and one of the things that they kind of advertise is come here, get your degree for 4 years. If you don't get into grad school, then grad transfer, cuz that's the only way. Uh like if, you know, obviously there's 5 years now, you can't use that 5th year unless you get into grad school. So, unfortunately, I wasn't able to do that. So, they they helped me get, you know, recruited and all that uh to go to Florida State. So, yeah. >> Who was your contact with the Patriots at all in the kind of pre-draft process or even when you were at Florida State? >> Yeah, I mean, I just I, you know, I had I played this through the season. I trained for my pro day in in New Jersey, uh Test uh Football Academy. And, you know, so I guess I was up here, but I just kind of went to pro day and did my best, and then eventually got in touch with them towards like the end of the the process, and then when I was, you know, deciding where I wanted to go, this place seemed like the best fit, probably. >> You mentioned Tim Murphy is a legendary coaching in the area. Do you take any lessons from him still? >> Oh, yeah. I mean, something he implemented that for us as a team, Harvard football time, it's like a just be everywhere 15 minutes early. That's, you know, I try to do that as much as I can. Um I mean, there's so many things that, you know, coach Murphy was there for 30 years. He won 10 championships. Like, it's it's hard not to try to carry over and try to take a little bit of his success with me. Um but yeah, I mean, work ethic, the the things that he he tried to engrain in us, uh I try to take as much as I can, to be honest, >> There's a lot of veterans in the offensive line, Oregon, Elijah, Mike, James. What have you learned from those guys so >> Yeah, we got a a lot of great old lineman here who have played a lot of football. I mean, I'm just trying to be a sponge and absorb as much as I can from them. You know, they played in a bunch of different spots and just really figure out how to be the best version of myself and and and move forward with that. Uh, I've been trying to tell jokes. Uh, I'm not a good singer, not a good dancer. So, jokes are trying to you know, I'm trying to do that. I hit or miss every day. I tell a lot of jokes and it's been a 50/50. Today's was good, I think. I don't know. I don't even know anymore. So, yeah. >> Where do you get your material? >> Last question? >> Uh, I just look things up on the internet at this point. I can't come up with it. Good. Uh, have a good one, guys.

title: Mike Vrabel: "Everyone Knows That if They're Doing Their Job That the Ball is Going to Find Them."
text: Oh, I know. Go ahead, Silk. Yep. Well, I think like a lot of things everything is pretty unique to itself. And whether that's negotiations or that's you know, the players or the play that we're running certainly those are unique and individual situations and I think we'll try to focus on Christian and and I know he'll focus on his own situation. So, we'll continue to to work through that and he'll continue to to try to improve and try to get back out on the field. >> Will we see him today or >> I would not anticipate that. I think he's just in the return to play. >> How about Moore in the same camp? >> Getting closer. He may do a little bit more. >> Coach, you're talking what you see this week will that determine if guys play Saturday or is that something you decide ahead of time? >> No, I think you have to use the work that we get and and and how good the work goes I think and how and how um as long as we get what we set out to accomplish. I mean, two days of of joint practices with with a lot of reps I think upwards of you know, probably 28 reps 30 reps for the first group on on each day is is a good number. Make sure that the intensity is there and then we'll evaluate. >> How do you think the players responded to going into the practice obviously the volume is a little bit higher than the practice outside. How much is going to give you some maybe some noise for you? >> Yeah, it's hard to be able to to um get those types of things outside or you know, at a preseason game and so you know, we're just trying to work on all those things that we're going to need throughout the season and I thought that that would be a good time to do it. >> What are things you learned about the team uh coming out of the joint practice in Indy that you can use into into Philly? >> Um no, but we have to just continue to be more consistent. We have to continue to uh understand that you know, the opponent changes, that the you know, what we see in the beginning of practice is usually going to be some of the same things that we we see in the end. If you don't fix problems, you know, or get get things addressed or recognize uh new plays that, you know, those that's going to be what it's like in the game. So, I don't know if I learned anything other than we have to continue to keep improving and that uh and that's the goal. >> How different is your approach with 2 days, Mike, rather than 1? >> Uh I don't think it's much different. I think that uh you know, we'll be able to do a lot more field work on the first day and then probably focus on the red zone uh the next day. Um but other than that, you know, we tried to put everything into 1 day versus Indy and now we'll have much more concentrated work uh second day in the red zone. >> With Andrew going down and Ben dealing with with his injury, is is that a position you'd like to add more veterans to or do you like the younger group there? >> Well, I mean, I think we have to be able to evaluate the younger group and see what they do here this week and, you know, in a competitive setting and then also in the game and then always, you know, keep our eyes open to to what it looks like around the league. >> Mike, I mentioned earlier in camp that we might see uh Caleb at guard. I don't think we've seen it yet in camp. Is that something that you guys might do now you're dealing with some injuries there? >> Yeah, certainly could. I think we just what happens is is, you know, where where do you feel like he can make the most strides and you don't want to uh you know, derail the in the improvement that he's making in some of those things and so, I'm probably much like you guys and say, "Hey, that it's not that big of a deal to go from from tackle to guard." I've got a lot of coaches that that probably think differently than what you guys and and maybe me think and that it's a little bigger deal, but uh I think Caleb's been working hard. He's been trying to improve. Um But I think at some point we will will need to do that as well. And and that's just trying to be fair to the kid and the player as he's developing and and learning this game and this this league. [snorts] Uh and then at some point in time, you know, we'll probably have to take a look in there. >> Like tight end is a spot that I think can be difficult for rookies just to grasp all the responsibilities and everything. With UY, how is he doing with that process of getting used to NFL speed, getting the playbook down, and seemingly like drinking from a fire hose? >> Yeah, I think um probably um fairly well. You know, I mean, it could always be better. I think that he's done some some good things that I think uh he's he's learning. He rarely makes the same mistake twice. If um you know, we we coach him on something or he didn't like what he did in one day, he usually comes back uh the next day and and does does a decent job at it. You can see him consciously trying to do the things that we're asking him to do. And I think we're you know, headed in a good direction, but uh you know, long ways to go. >> Mike, how how close is the league to having starting quarterbacks not play at all in >> [snorts] >> I I don't know. I really just focus on the Patriots and not the league. I don't know what other teams are doing. you know, that's certainly a question for for 32 teams, you know, so what we're trying to do >> certainly helped that. >> Yeah, I mean, you get a lot of intensity, but you know, and you see a lot of different looks and teams are you know, they're running a lot more stuff than they would run in the preseason and in the game and putting it on film. You know, if that's what you mean. I mean, stuff that we saw from Indianapolis in practice, we didn't see from them in the game. We saw basically a you know, one or two blitzes and a lot of other just base defenses. >> How do you feel the run game is progressing and do you have to manage expectations at all given how important time on task is and all the movement that you guys have had on that side? >> I mean, it's I I it's probably hard to tell. I mean, I think it can always be better. But, you know, it's not live, so you don't know if guys break tackles and you know, receivers are trying to come get safeties that are 3 yd from the line of scrimmage. You know, do you want them to go nail them and then knock them into the other guys? So, I think that there's a fine line there in trying to figure out what the run game looks like and what it will look like and there's been some good runs. Uh there's been some times where it's been one guy, but still not a very good play. So, there's there's I think good things and there's some things that, you know, would have to be better. But, we want to take care of our guys. We want to make sure that we're staying up and we're not creating piles and sometimes those receivers going down to get those guys in support creates a little funky angle and, you know, we we ask them to, you know, take care of each other. title: Cam Skattebo: 'I'm just going to continue being the best football player I can be' | New York Giants
text: Did you like how you felt running the ball the other day in the game and how you guys moved the line of scrimmage? >> Yeah, I mean I felt great, you know, um uh made some minor errors in my details of u what I was doing, but for the most part I felt good having the ball in my hands. >> You still like to get back on the field though, you know, when you come back from that injury, like are you do you think about it? Like how do you like do you try to not think about it at all? Ignore it, recognize. >> I don't really I I don't really think about it on a daily basis. Um, if you go out there and watch me today practice, like >> I meant in the game. >> Yeah, in the game, too. I'm saying if if if it's not hurting me or if it's not bothering me, I'm my mind is clear of it. Um, when I went out there on Saturday, I had no feeling or any recollection of injury in my brain. I was ready to go play football and um, you know, adrenaline gets going. So, everything kind of goes away and you're just ready to touch the ball and go play go play ball. >> As you've been rehabbing, have you and Malik talked a little I mean, you know, you're all you're on different schedules or whatever, but uh have you guys talked about, you know, getting over it and coming back and and regaining the confidence, you know. >> Yeah. I mean, uh, I think with an injury of any sort, um, anybody in the league, um, you fall into a little darker space in your in your mind and, um, just having your guys around you helping you with that is, uh, huge for me and him, you know, and, um, I was able to have him and and as I got more and more healthy and he was still going kind of through the hard stage, I was able to help him get out of that and, um, we were kind of able to work off each other. So, you know, Malik looks great. He's he's coming back and, uh, I'm excited to see him continue to push to be better and better each day. and um watch him play football again. >> And what mistakes do you you said there were a few things sad? >> Yeah, it was it was minor details. Nothing serious. Um you know, stuff I just got to clean up in the film room. Just little tiny things um with my footwork on on on certain plays and stuff. But other than that, I I felt good. >> Har was saying he doesn't think you're 100%. Like what do you think is left to to get to that point where you are 100%. >> Yeah, I think I think he says that um obviously, you know, touching the ball again for the first time in 10 months. Um, I think he knows that there's more to me. And when, um, I start, you know, pushing myself to, you know, get better and better each day. Um, you know, there's there's certain things that bother me here and there, but it's not stuff that lingers around or hangs around. It, you know, it'll hop up on me here and then it'll go away tomorrow. So, um, you know, just working out those kinks and those bruises and stuff, and um, you know, as time goes on, I I'll feel better and better. Ken, last year, you know, before you got hurt, you had such a good rookie year and you kind of become like a mini celebrity in the area. What's it like to have that when you obviously know you're only just started on the field? How like balancing the >> Yeah, I mean it's New York. Um you get publicity, you know? Um what we say is all publicity is good publicity. So if they're talking about you, there's a good thing, you know. So um everyone loves to talk about me cuz I'm crazy and um do a whole bunch of different things here and there. And uh you know, I'm I'm just going to continue to be the best football player I can be. Um I try not to let the outside stuff bother me and kind of stay off my phone for the most part. So I'm either hanging out with my girlfriend or you know, playing video games and staying away from my phone. So um you know, I'm I'm focused right now on football and that's the main goal. >> I know you kind of say that tongue and cheek. Get it. Everybody talks about how you're crazy and you know, they say things about your your personality. You're out there. Do you think people overlook or maybe not give you enough credit for your football skills and what you're able to do on a football field? >> Yeah, I mean that's been my whole life though. Um, as as I've went with my whole life, you know, each each level that I've went up, uh, I think the football skills asset people think is less and less as we get higher and higher. And I think I only get better and better with the competition. So, um, people can keep thinking what they want, but you know, I think I'm a really good running back. So, um, I want to be the best one day and that's the goal. So, I'm going to continue to just keep being me and keep pushing. >> Is there almost an advantage if people just keep focusing on your personality and not your football? >> Yeah. I mean, people know I'm crazy. I like to run through people instead of run around them. Um hopefully you'll see more running around people this year. And uh you know, I I don't really care what people think. If they think I'm not as good of a running back, they still got to play me that week. So, um whether they think that or not, then I guess we'll see that week. >> You seem really happy. >> Has that been an emphasis? like running around people rather than through cuz that's >> No, I mean I think coach Harbs loves that I run right over the top of people. Um, you know, physicality is his number one thing and um it it gets the O line going even more. So obviously I mean as I've came back from injury and learning how to take less hits and um try to maneuver better um around people instead of through them and realizing that I could have got four more yards if I would have just took a step to the left. Um, I think those are things that I'm just going to continue to add to my game and add to my bag of tools that I can pull from to make sure that, you know, I stay healthy and I stay successful. >> You've, um, you obviously one of the loudest people in the league was practicing on Thursday. Just what does that mean seeing him out there? You obviously were a big supporter just cheering. We heard you, but just what does it mean seeing him out there doing these drills? >> Yeah, I mean, like I said, I'm super excited to see him, man. We were we were both in the time um, throughout last season and throughout the offseason. It's like you get hurt and you kind of got to see these guys go through um got to watch these guys play games without you guys. Um knowing that you guys are both key parts and not being able to win games and struggling. Um and then you know we come back this year and we're slowly getting back and you could tell the way we're feeling better and guys are on the field are feeling better. It's just being able to see him out there and you know me obviously getting back has been something that's made both of us more happy. Um just being able to get back on the field and run routes. So, um, it's been awesome seeing him out there and, you know, hopefully one of these days we get to see him with that red jersey off and, uh, we get to see Malik Neighbors back in back in action. >> How do you think he look? How do you think he looked today running routes? I mean, I'm sure you like the rest of us when he's out there when you're on the sideline. I'm talking about kind of like watching him also to see how he does. >> What do you mean see when he does that? >> I mean, most of the time when he's in, I'm in. Um, vice versa or I'm coming off the field when they're running the next play. But, I mean, I see him every day. I see him work out. got to see him do stuff on and off the field. Um, I went through the rehab process with process with him, so I know how much better he's gotten over time. And, uh, I mean, he's he's looked good. You know, he's he's still a little, you know, feeling feeling things out, but and getting back into it, just doing his first couple team reps. And, uh, I think as time goes on, you're only going to see more and more from him, and you're going to see him look like himself every day more and more. >> You mentioned him getting the red jersey off. I'm imagining that they don't have a 44 in red. Uh, I mean, I think the ankle has to be the wrong direction if the 44 red jersey pull gets pulled out. >> What do you think of what do you think of them bringing in uh Naji Harris and how much of you is trying to continue to prove that you can be the guy? Yeah, I mean obviously we had a we had a back go down um you know praying for Turbo and uh what he's got going on, but I mean we had a we had a guy go down and we had to fill the void, you know. So if we have we had a guy to go down and we brought a guy in. Um you know Naji is a great player. I'm super excited to get to know him and meet him and play with him. So uh whatever comes comes. I'm I'm super excited for it.
