I mean, I've always felt like I could work on the pass game a little later, but just working on the run game first. That's kind of, you know, uh, where it starts up front. So, focus on that part of my game for sure. >> When you're when you're a taller guy like you talked about, how how vitally important is it for you to develop like your lower body, especially when you're playing in the interior? And is it more important [snorts] when you're playing in the interior versus like when you wind up on the outside? >> Yes, ma'am. Um, I would say uh leverage uh whether you're inside or outside is always important, but especially inside like and it's kind of good this year having guys like Aan Robertson who's kind of like my uh frame cuz he plays almost the same position as I do. So seeing him like uh in film, he's always helping me out. He's always giving me pointers. We're always talking about how would he play this, how would I play that, just cuz we're like almost literally like identical in frame. So just having him in the room has been better. And then just being able to understand that when you are 6'3, 6'4 uh kind of body, you do have to play with your eyes lower to the ground. You have to have your uh feet, you know, kind of, you don't want to take those big old steps. You want to have shorter, more powerful steps because I do have longer legs. If I take those bigger steps, I kind of get knocked all over the place. So that's kind of things that Aan and Nacho have kind of been helping me with and they have been like really really good vets for sure. >> Have you seen the difference in the strength training like translate to core strength and leverage and things like that? >> Yes ma'am for sure. I would say uh it starts in the weight room. Uh obviously once you build that confidence in the weight room you kind of get more confident on the field. That's kind of uh what I was kind of doing during that whole part of like January up until we got back in April. Just wait room wait room. And then after OTAAS it was all field work just all football football. So that was kind of my uh thing and then once I felt more confident in the weight room I honestly felt more confident on the field. >> What's been the biggest thing that Sean and Nacho have brought to not just the line but the defense in general and the team really? >> Man, just like the energy they bring, you know, like both of those guys have played so much football that like it's hard during camp, man, when you're on day 10, day 11 or whatever day we're on, you just keep going and it's hard to bring that same type of intensity, same juice every single day, but they bring it, you know? So having those guys out here, you know, like even when you're coming out, you don't really feel the same as you did the day before, having those guys, you know, like cuz I I probably know that they're not feeling great every day, but they bring that juice. So it kind of brings the whole whole group along. And when the D line's playing good, I mean, believe it or not, the linebackers follow through, the DBs follow through when we're out there making plays, being loud, talking a little trash, you know, everybody kind of just follows through. >> How much uh how much weight did you gain? Where do you want to be at? Uh man, I came into OTAAS about like 3:10ish, 31:15ish. Uh right now I'm playing at like 303, 305ish. >> Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. I'll probably play season around here like 300 to 305. >> You feel >> I feel great. >> Yes, sir. Yes, sir. I feel great. I don't really think the weight kind of slowed me down at all. I still feel good. Still twitchy. >> Healthy. How much does it feel like a different room? >> Man, that room's great. Like we honestly have so much depth that like when when I roll out there, when uh Kart's out there, when Jay Jones, Elijah Simmons, it's like it feels like there's no drop off, you know? Everyone's out there, everyone's still going. Obviously, uh Kart um has a lot to learn with him only being here like a few months, but he's been learning. He's been growing. Even in the game, he had a few good plays. His hands are getting better. His techniques is getting better. And that's honestly where it starts up front. Even for me, like there's so much more I have to get better with from a technique standpoint. But having the veteran guys in the room who just let you know, bro, when you just play, like, everyone's good at something. Everyone has a special talent. So, just play to your strengths. And that's kind of what they tell me all the time, man. Like, be that fast guy off the ball. Everything else will just come, you know, everything else will follow through. >> What do you think about the preseason game? >> Man, it was good. Uh, obviously it was good to get back out there, uh, make some plays on another team, but now we're on to a new week, so I got to be able to do it again. >> You guys have the joint practice last week. Now you guys are just practicing. >> Yeah. >> Against yourselves again. Uh how different is that to kind of you know switch mindsets? >> Yeah, I mean um I feel like uh everybody kind of likes a joint practices in a sense because you're not really going against yourself anymore. You're going against another team. It's almost like you play three games in a week, you know, like last last week was almost like you played three games that one week. So it feels good to have joint practice, but I mean uh at least with us out here, you get to have our guys out here just still going against each other. It's still good work. It's not like anybody's going to let off the gas or anything like that, but then it just makes it that more that much more fun when we play against another team on Saturday. We didn't get to see Ruben Bane Jr. this past week, but he's gonna play this week. What have you seen from him in practice? >> Man, everything you guys uh saw from him to make him a first round pick is is pretty much what he's doing out here. He's a great dude. Uh I feel like he's he's a better person than what he is a football player, and that's what people really don't get to see. Obviously a quieter guy, but man, he's a great dude and obviously on the field, he kind of turns that switch. He's a different guy for sure. Elijah, what's this part of camp like for you when you're kind of at that halfway point where the regular season opener is so far away yet you guys are in the throws of of a long way into training camp here? >> Yeah. Um I would say right now is just staying consistent, not really like you said, uh looking too far ahead and not really worrying about what we've already done. I mean obviously focus on the things that we haven't done good and try to fix those up and then the things that we have done good try to uh make those better. But honestly, right now, even like coach said yesterday, man, we're kind of entering those quote unquote dog days where it's kind of just back to back to back. So, we need consistency. That's really the biggest thing in our room for sure up front, staying consistent. If we can do that, man, like during camp when it's a lot harder than season, it should be a good year for sure. >> Elijah, if you you talked about the rotation, you guys are really deep there. If you have to play without V, you guys pretty confident you can get get the job done. >> Yes, sir. I mean, uh, we've done it all camp. Uh, camp, we've looked great. I mean, obviously having been out there is a lot different, but we uh honestly we're so deep that anybody can not go for a practice, not go for a week, and I think there won't be, you know, as much drop off. >> You talk about the Go ahead. >> You talk about the energy that Nation bring. Just there are guys who have been in the league for a long time, too. Just what type of institutional knowledge do they bring to the defensive line that that maybe you didn't realize about the game before? Both. How helpful is that? I would just say uh like how they how they see the game like their instincts and how they kind of see different things is something that I really haven't heard much of obviously I mean I've only been in the league one year now but having those guys what Nacho's year 10 Asan year 11 those guys I mean every time in the meeting room it's like it's like we're like in a class you know like my notebook is uh has so many notes from like the things that they talk about and things that just just like what they see and how they help us out how they help the younger guys out. I think we have like four rookies in our room. So having having those guys and then where you got three second year guys in that room. So it's a pretty young room but having those guys honestly has just been so much help from a technique standpoint and then a mindset standpoint. Those are like really two violent guys. Really violent dudes. Asan is a little wired wired different. >> Thank you guys. How you doing? >> What's up? How y'all doing? >> I'm doing well. >> You always want to play well when you get out there but you know have a night like you did with two sacks. Just what does that do for your confidence? Yeah, it's uh it was a great thing but at the end of the day that I'm an outcome I'm not an outcome oriented guy. I'm a processor oriented guy. Um a lot of times in my career, especially in college, you know, it's hard not to look at the outcomes of things and get focused on th those things. But, you know, kind of throughout my whole process, I've just learned how to just be processoriented. So, it's it's expected for me. You know, I expect to go out there and dominate and play my best. And, you know, every time I step on out on the field, I'm going to give it everything I have. >> What type of feedback did you get from the coaching staff after that? Yeah, they were happy with the way I played. They thought I played hard. Uh my techniques looked good and um you know, they were they were pleased with it. >> Anything you saw in those players that enabled you to get to the quarterback? >> Again, just my process. You know, I've studied the film study, the amount of hours that I put in, you know, my free time and, you know, working on my footwork and studying the art of pass rushing. You know, it's all kind of accumulates into putting on in game day. Is >> there somebody that you've been leaning on since coming here that's that's been helping you along the way? Um, yeah. I mean, just my room in general. You know, Coach Foot's been a great mentor. You know, the way that he understands the game of football is incredible. You know, being able to learn from him and it's been I I can't even say how grateful I am that, you know, he's been my coach and been able to mentor me. You know, as well as leaning the guys in my room like, you know, Yaya and, you know, Muhammad and, you know, just stuff I've learned from him. Then being able to work with Bane a lot, you know, doing a lot of extra work with him and, you know, it's just a great room of guys and, you know, very talented room. >> Uh, you're obviously a Jacksonville guy. Do you have friends and family coming to make the trip down for this game and obviously next week you get to go home. Just how exciting is that for you? >> Yeah. No, it'll be cool for sure to go back home to Jacksonville. But yeah, my family will be here uh this weekend. They they try to come out to all my games, man. I got an amazing family and I'm so blessed that um I have them in my life. >> It's got to be especially helpful too when you enter into this new phase of your life and there is a lot of uncertainty. You don't know what's in front of you. You know, you don't know if you're going to continue to be here with this team as the year goes on. >> Yeah. Again, it just comes down to my process. you know, I'm not really worried about what the outcome is of anything. I'm just going to continue my daily process and at the end of the day, try to be the best player that I can be and hopefully one day that's one of the best in the league. That's my goal. >> I'm sorry. How um you mentioned the the process many many times. Where where did that belief come from those ideas for you? >> Yeah, you know, I've always been a good football player and had a good college career, but didn't perform how I wanted to perform. And part of that is, you know, a mental side of the game that I didn't fully tap into um and and a confidence aspect. And when I sat on my couch on the day of draft and I didn't get drafted, I had to look at myself in the mirror and decide who do I want to be? You know, do I want to say why me? Why me? Or do I want to say why not me? And in that moment, I chose why not me and I've worked, you know, harder than I've ever worked in my life to be where I'm at and I'm going to continue to work even harder >> on a human level, like rejection is such a difficult thing and not everybody handles it that way. What allowed you to be able to flip that switch? Um because some people like they hear that and it's like I'm not good enough and and it just spirals into negative self-t talk but you flip a switch and you come out here you have two sacks and your debut. What what allowed you to be able to flip that switch? >> I just think it was the way I was raised. uh it's a mentality I've had most of my life and a lot of things in you know things happen in college and you know there's ups and downs but I just got back to my roots and focused on you know what got me to college in the first place and what got me to have play my best ball and refocus on those things and you know find a new level you know I've cut out I haven't had social media for months I just downloaded the other day just to post a I don't know Instagram story like yesterday or whatever but I haven't had it yeah I haven't had it for months like I don't I don't need it in my life I cut out all the distractions that I didn't need in my life that were I feel like hindering me because at the end of the day, it doesn't matter what anyone else says about me. It's what I believe, you know. It it it does not it just simply doesn't matter. You know, it's everything that I believe and what I know I can do. Most of my life I've tried to pro prove people wrong and I'm just trying to prove myself right. >> Was your decision to go from Florida to LSU give yourself more rush opportunities. Do you feel like you have more of a chance that way? >> Yeah, I mean a lot went into it. Um it was a definitely a difficult decision for me. You know, at the end of the day, I just my entire college career, I just don't think I worked hard enough. You know, when I reflect back on it, no matter where I was, whether I was at Florida or LSU, I just did not dedicate my life to it and simply this is everything that I've ever wanted since I was a kid. You know, my screen saver is me as a little kid playing football and it says do it for him. I I look at that every day when I wake up at 4:30, 55 in the morning, and you know, that's what I'm doing now. New chapter. >> You didn't think you worked hard enough? >> No. Was it because it wasn't like a singular focus for you or maybe you didn't go to failure enough times in the wait room or or you didn't stay late after practice? What was it? >> It's No, I did I did all the extra work I did but not to a level that I want to do it because like I said, like one day I want to be one of the best. You know, how however long that takes, I don't care. I'm going to continue to work like that. And you know, in life, that's going to carry me farther than I could ever hope to for it to carry me. Um whe whatever I do in life, I want to be successful. And you know, you just have to swallow your pride. You know, pride is the number one downfall of most men. And you know, when you swallow that and just accept your reality of situation and say, "I got to do more. I got to do more than everyone else." You know, that's the reality. >> You said you uh you cut out social media. What did you learn about yourself? How did it affect your life? >> Man, it's the most incredible experience. You know, I tell people all the time, you know, if you can get it out of your life, it it's incredible. You know, you don't have to. Part of the problem was I would look into all the negative but all the positive. Like it doesn't matter. Like it again like I go back to it's the process, you know, not having social media, not looking at what everyone else is going on. You shrink your circle and you know, you realize who are the people that really care about you and who really matters to you. Those are the people that you still text and you still communicate with. Like I I don't need to see all that's going on. You know, I don't need to sit there on Instagram and sit on my couch for 5 hours out of the day and scroll. you know, I can be out outside, I don't know, tanning, being on the water, you know, doing something healthy for my mental, doing something for my mind. You know, it's better out working on football, film, studying, you know, it's just being connected. And I feel like a lot of times social media just it's not that. >> You think that's the downfall of a lot of young athletes? >> Oh, for sure. No, I I I really do. And I hope to, you know, stress that more and more, you know, I hope to gain, you know, more of a voice in the space to be able to, you know, tell people that you you don't need those things in life. You know, a lot of that's just fake. The people on there are fake. They don't really care about you and all that matters is you're a close circle of people. I mean, that's what's reality of the world. >> Jack, if you're going to stick as a backup outside linebacker, you get a help on special teams. It looked like they were trying to use you on the kick block kind of in the middle, getting that big arm up there. Is that something you've had success with in the past? >> Yeah, you know, at the end of the day, um, Coach Danny does a great job. Um, and he's kind of coached up the technique and again, I just practice it and, you know, it's the same, it's a dip, lean, and rip and it's it's what I do for a living. So, I hope I'm good at it. anybody on this team in your position group that's been a big influence for you learning from here? >> Yeah, like I said, Yaya has been great. Um, the whole room's just been awesome. You know, uh, Nelly, um, and those guys are great and just working with Bane. Like again, I can't stress y'all enough how talented that guy is and I cannot wait to watch him play. Um, and he's just tremendous person as well. You know, it's been fun to be around him, you know, because most people I don't that are my age, you know, are not as focused on just the ball side of things. and to see him have that similar mindset to me on just the ball is what matters right now, you know, it's incredible. So, >> thank you guys. >> Appreciate y'all. >> I hope you do get more question. >> How y'all doing? How y'all doing? >> Has the excitement worn off at all for you in that that big six? >> It wore off a little bit yesterday. It was still like a a roller coaster for me just because um you always dreamed of that. Like you dream that's something you literally like that's in your dream getting to pick six in your first NFL game. So just having that opportunity to go out there and do that was a blessing for me. >> How much is it just the work that you put in? I mean, we've seen you make some plays earlier in training camp. Yes, sir. >> See the hard work pay off. How rewarding is that? >> I mean, that's that's what practice is for. Like if you you going to practice how you play. That literally how it happens. Like if you come out here and um not give it your all, that's how it's going to be in the game. And I try to give my all in practice. Like even on hot days like this, just trying to give my all cuz I know today I got the rest of the day to chill out and recover. So just giving my all like tech having my the best technique I can even when I get tired is what I try to do. >> W to Arizona. You're no stranger to to working your way onto a roster team. How has that helped you as you try to work your way onto this team? >> Yeah, I mean that's what I take it. I take it as like that's been my whole career. Started at Dukane um my first year my first year senior wasn't playing well and I end up getting it starting like the second third game of the season. My first game got a pick, got a forced fumble. So like that's that's just been my whole career. went to West Virginia, it was a lot of big recruiting, like a lot of big five stars, four stars, and by the third week of camp, I was in I was with the ones and I never left. So, like just having that mentality to just go out there, it don't matter who's in front of you, who's in back of you, just continuing to just put my foot forward. >> Aiden, take us back to the whole story to a stranger. >> Yes. Um, take us through that story. What motivated you to do that? Um, so my uh my defensive coordinator, Coach Craig, like as one of the um closest people in my life. Um, and I used to go in his office all the time. We just sparked different conversations. One of the conversations was when the um the drive was getting closer and his roommate in college almost died from it and end up getting um um a bone marrow transplant. And that sparked me to actually do it cuz I was nervous. I'm like, "Ah, do I really want to like enter myself into this thing that I don't know?" Like it could be tomorrow. it could be 10 years from now. And um I signed up for it and um 6 months, eight months later um I get a I get a note in the uh mail and my mom, she actually threw it in the trash. She thought it was like spam. Like she thought it was just spam. So she threw it in the mail and my aunt was like, "Man, go get it." It was right there on the top of the trash. It matched the email I had and I knew soon as I seen it that I wanted to do it. >> But you didn't think about your football career? Um, I thought about my football career, but like once I looked at it and once I researched it, like man, you can take you could take this from me. Like that's saving another person's life. That's taking that's saving another person's life and she had a daughter. That's saving two lives. Like just seeing some like I would be heartbroken without growing up with my mom. So just taking that time out even if I'm I was out three weeks. I couldn't do winter workouts for three weeks and then and save somebody life. So I would never forget that. What's that process like? >> Um, the process wasn't wasn't too bad. Um, >> your hair's painful and some people even have complications. >> Yeah, it's not it's not as bad as it used to be. It used to be really bad, but it's not as bad anymore. Um, it's like it's just stem cells now. So, they they put two incisions in the back of my hips. In the back of my hips, like near like the top of my u top of my um lower back. Really? Your pelvic? >> Yeah. Two uh two incisions, but they did 100 incisions inside those two incisions. So, it wasn't the worst. Like, obviously, like just think of squatting. Think of squatting for a week straight and your legs get heavy, your back is tight. That's exactly what it felt like. And I didn't care if I was out a month, two months. Like, I didn't care. I knew this game was going to repay me and I knew God was going to repay me for the things that I did um things that I did for the woman and they and just my family. Like, now my family get blessings that they may have that that I put upon them. So, had you have a chance to meet I mean I know sometimes with those like with my aunt she never got a chance to meet her donor. It was kind of confidential. Have you met >> uh I'm still working towards it. It was just a lot like going on obviously just working through college trying to like finish that and I knew it was going to be a time when I do have a lot of free time probably this offseason try to get in contact with um be the match and get with those people so I could be able to meet her soon. >> Hey, you're in a pretty young quarterback room here guys and Jacob Parish football. What are some of the biggest things that you learned from them as you stepped on this team? >> That technique. That technique is probably the most um important thing at this level in this game. Like if you don't have good technique, a lot of people you're going to get beat. It could be from the first receiver on the depth chart to the last receiver on the depth chart. Everybody's good. So having good technique and and tweaking your game like um like I I try to have a bag just like they say the wide receivers have a bag. You got to have a bag of your own as a defensive player. just knowing splits, knowing different dividers, knowing if I need to press this, knowing if I need to press the outside leverage, knowing I need to slow down because it's third down just like I did on on Friday. Just different things that I continue to just take from my game from those guys. And it's some of the stuff that I'm doing that that they was taking that we've been watching in film. So, just continuing to um get closer with those guys obviously towards the season get closer. >> You got here maybe not knowing if you were going to get a rusty spot, right? And then now you got this momentum going. >> Yeah. How much would it mean to you to to get arrest? >> Um, it would be um obviously something I dreamed of, but something I wouldn't be shocked about. Like I came here to win a job. I didn't care if I was the last person on a dep chart or the first person on de chart. I came here to win a job and nobody's going to get in my way for that. Like I told my family, hey, y'all could talk to me in September when all this is over. Like I just want to have a clear mind. And that's what I have. I have a clear mind and I'm have one goal. One goal is to continue to get two goals actually. continue to get closer with this organization and make this team. >> Obviously, you can run. You got cover skills. The physical part of the game, playing the run. How important is that to improve? >> And that's that's my main that's my main goal. Like just continuing to take these next couple practices, these joint practices, preseason games, continue to work on my um my tackling because that's the biggest thing everybody like says about me is the tackling and the physical ability this game. And I know it is. I felt it on um sat Saturday I mean uh Friday just going against Bree obviously going against him in practice seeing different things but something I'm not scared of like obviously I have to take that step everybody has to take a step in the league you might be not the fastest guy you got to get faster and I'm not the biggest guy I have to get bigger I have to start to fit the run but I'm not scared I'm take the opportunity um I miss I miss I miss I could send it back to my help but I can't miss and not send it back to my help so I know I know how to do things so I'm going just continue to um build that through the preseason and um pray I could take it into regular season. >> We see you compete out here a lot whether it's you know against Ibuka getting a PBU or Ted Hurst. Who has pushed you the most or maybe taught you the most from lining up against them? >> Um it may not even be a player. It might be Tai Bose. He pushes me um every day just to do different things, try different techniques. He pushed me when we were in um when we were up in adjusted to do different things, try different things out, things that I might did here that I was like not nervous about, but just new to going against different people. But he pushes me obviously IA uh Jaylen McMillan and y'all can see me and Ted Hurst go against each other a lot and u obviously he's going to be a phenomenal player in this league. So just going against him, him learning things as a rookie, me learning things as a rookie and just bringing them together. And that's what we did on Friday. And we're gonna continue to bring this um through regular through the preseason and into the regular season. >> Thanks, guys. >> I appreciate y'all. Thank y'all. Appreciate you.

title: Devon Witherspoon On His Contract Extension "It Feels Special To Get It Done" | Seattle Seahawks
text: How's it feel, Devin, to get the contract done? >> Feel good, man. You know, long time coming, but it feel good to get it done. >> Julian said that it's going to be your turn now to cover some things in the DB room. >> Yeah, that's what he said. You know, I take the challenge on, man. I'm going to be ready. I'm going to be ready. I got the gifts ready. >> He says that you're pretty frugal. That you still got stuff you're wearing from from high school. >> Oh, yeah, yeah, yeah. I don't cheat with it. No, I don't don't don't don't ever get that confused. You know what I'm saying? I'll always be cheap with it, but I I'm going to take care of the guys for sure. >> Devin, how involved were you in the process? Was it like don't tell me until it's done or were you kind of keeping updates as it was going on for you to kind of to know what the landscape was kind of working through? >> No, I was updated throughout the whole thing, you know, but but my my was here and focused on being with my team and going out here practicing and getting better every day, but my my mind wasn't on that, but I knew what it was. >> To be able to have these next few years knowing it's going to be with this team, this franchise you really carved out something. How special is it to know that future is in cement now? >> It's special, man. It's kind of something you already dreamed of, but it's kind of something that I knew as well. It's like we we talked about it before and and everything like that. It's like I know I'm going to be here. I know this is where my heart is. So, that was never coming into question. So, it just it just feels special to get it done. >> You said it was a long time coming. What do you >> Long process, man. You know, a lot of back and forth, but it was easy to get it done. Thank you. >> Is this exactly where you pictured yourself being after you got drafted? Like how the first three years have played out? How's this extension played out? >> Uh kind of, but I didn't have idea how it was going to go. Um only thing on my mind when I got drafted here was to be the best me every day um and try to win this city a Super Bowl. So. >> Devin, you you and Jackson obviously coming in together. You've been kind of kind of tied at the hip ever since then. To have both of you guys get the deals done this offseason kind of know you're foundational pieces of this team to build around. What does that kind of mean to you guys to kind of have that under you for three years here now and going forward? >> It means everything to us. Like I said, we talked about it when we first got here and what we wanted to do. Um and then as the years passed we just continued to grow and build. You know, it changed at a point of time in the year cuz it's like stuff happens and then we got to adjust and adapt, but we just always talked about building on that how could we be better in everyday. And how could we take this program to elite program, so. >> Do you remember that boat ride after you guys were drafted and and what you guys talked about on that ride? >> Uh, really we didn't really say too much though. We were just we were just happy to be here. You know what I'm saying? We were like this crazy. We all remember that though. >> Highest paid cornerback in the NF NFL history. What do those credentials mean to you? >> Uh, it mean a lot man. Just it's the it's a thing that you don't kind of think about for real, but when it happens like that's really real. Like it ain't it ain't fake, but you know, for me it means a lot to me, but at the same time it it's nothing to me at the same time cuz it's like I got a team here, you feel me? And I'm trying to win though, so all that is love. I appreciate all that and but I'm focused on building with my team right now. >> Before you stepped to the podium we saw you joking with Mike for a moment. Just wondering playing for him for a couple more years. What how excited are you for that and how has he kind of helped you develop and and maximize what you can do? >> I'm ready man. You know, I told him when he first got here like I'm thankful. I know what you going to bring to the team. I know what you do. And I'm going to be the guy here for you, so it means everything to me man. You know, just to continue to build with him, continue to learn from him. The way he game plans, just to be involved with that. It just means everything to me man. You know, I know I got his back. I know he got my back, so it means everything to me. >> What is that badge on your jersey? The the sledgehammer or whatever. You have to say that one. >> Uh, I have no idea to be honest. I ain't going to lie to you. I didn't even know that was there. >> [laughter] >> When you guys first started the draft process, Stephon, how realistic was almost a decade with the same team? A team that drafted you you can stay eight plus years. Was that even in >> That's not something I was really kind of thinking about at that moment. Like I said, I was just coming in and try to be the best me everyday, so it wasn't something that was on my mind. >> Does a deal like this add pressure or take pressure off of you? >> Uh, I don't think it does neither though. I think it's a little bit of both, but I don't think it does nothing to me. You know, I'm going to be me everyday. I ain't nothing going to change about me, so I don't really see it no type of way. >> How do you feel about that you and Josh now both having Josh having contracts together for the next 3 years you guys get to continue playing together the continuity on that back end. >> It feel good you know like that's my that's my dog right there for sure like that's my boy so you know being together it's not just in the building but outside of building everything like that like we got a real good relationship and it's still going to this day but knowing that we going to be here and knowing how we practicing and what we chasing like off the field and stuff like that it means everything to us so we chasing greatness for sure. >> When the negotiations were going on how did you stay grounded you mentioned staying focused on being out here like who helped you how did you stay focused? >> It was easy my teammates man like I said when you coming in you coming to work with guys like this like D Hall E J and Leo and them like Murph I mean kind of guys when you come to work with guys like that it means everything it's easy to take the pressure off you cuz now I know what they are about and they know what I'm about so it's just easy to come out here and just focus on football. >> Who's the first person you called or texted when the deal got done? >> My mom. >> What she say? >> She was just happy. >> Devon as a blitzer what what do you think makes you as effective as you are as a blitzer? >> Um my ability to win so I mean I know how to win on pass rushes and stuff like that but it's it's a study that I have to continue to work on. >> Mike has said that how effective you were in the Super Bowl and we've seen it in other times but in the Super Bowl especially he said that that makes him think about maybe using you more in that role what do you think about that? >> I mean I mean whatever you want me to do I'm able to do it so just let me know coach. >> Devon obviously the plan to bring Terryon in Terryon Arnold in do you know him at all have you asked about him what do you what do you expect from him when he when he comes in here and be a part of this organization? >> Yeah I do I do know him you know I did send him a text and stuff like that but I haven't got a chance to have a full conversation with him and stuff like that but yeah man I know I know he can play ball though and I know he he's going to be easy to you know come in with this culture and how we do and the way we go about our business over here I think it'll be easy for him to follow in line you know and just adapt to this situation and I think it's going to be the best for him so I can't wait till he get here you know ready to work with you bro. >> Anything else? >> Thank you. >> Congrats.

text: No, this is not I'm not conducting a class here. Huh? All right, good to see everybody. Uh good workout. Be in pads tomorrow, so uh looking forward to that. And uh keep attacking this week. What you what might you have >> Yeah, yeah, um same same feeling, honestly. I think it's good for our team, you know, we need we need to see those things and and I think we're going to grow from it. But I think it's it's a lot of the things we said right after the game. A lot of good There's a lot of good stuff, too, you know, a lot of a lot of great individual play. But not not enough great individual play to to um kind of earn a better result. >> What what did the film show of Drew and Jaylen and what you kind of thought of how they played? >> Yeah, I I you know, I I think um I think there's there's room to grow, but I think both had solid performances, frankly. I mean, um it wasn't much for for for Jaylen to um make the come to life. There's some better decisions he can make, you know, more decisive in a couple situations, but I mean, that's going to be every quarterback. I I was I was pleased with their performances. I felt like it was a good start. >> What did you uh hear from Brian Flurry about his first experience calling plays? >> Uh it was like it was in in practice. Wasn't really I mean, we're not we're not we're not doing a a lot schematically right now, so it's pretty par for the course, for honestly. >> You talked about operational stuff not being there >> Yeah, yeah, we can be we can be we can be a little bit better. I mean, it's really everybody. Starts with me. Goes to the coordinators down to the guys with the green hat. How the information kind of trickles down. How we sub. You know, all of our coaches on the sideline. It's just it was a good good wake-up call that we got to we got to get better. >> What did you see from Drew Lock last night when you went back and watched the film? >> Yeah. I feel like I actually watched the game. It's funny when you're not calling the plays, you probably see more things. Yeah, he's he very similar to what we saw right after the game. Played played really well. Played really great. Did a really great job. I think he had like a tackle every two plays he's in there or something. Pretty crazy. >> He talked after the game about playing some off the edge and he did that quite a bit at UTEP. Is that something that you envision trying to see >> I don't know what you're talking about. >> Is that something you envision potentially him maybe being able to at least in passing downs to be a way to get him on the field right >> Um yeah, let's just say he's he's It's a good problem to have from a coach's perspective of trying to figure out a way to get him out there and what's the best for the team. So, I think we're working through that right now. >> How does your game day change when you are not calling plays? >> I'm a lot nicer. Um more talkative with my wife for sure. It's it's a pretty drastic change. I mean like your mind is but I mean if we if I wasn't calling plays, I'd be in a real in like a regular season and I'd be really I'd still be like really involved with what we're doing. So, I'd imagine I'd probably feel the same. I don't know I really don't know what I don't really don't know what it feels like. >> And Mike, going back to today's practice, back to Saturday's operational things, you had meetings this morning. What did you like about today's practice today? >> Yeah, our intent our intent it wasn't it wasn't a crazy crazy long practice or intense practice but the ones workload was heavier which is good get their wind up. But anytime we challenge our guys to do anything their their intent has been fantastic and we did it again today. So, I'm you know, we trust our guys, you know, this is this is like our first kind of first opportunity to work through a not perfect situation. I wouldn't call it adverse but maybe maybe you do call it adverse situation where it's just say things didn't go your way. You know, we said we're going to operate a certain way. And so now let's go uh let's go do act and do and act as we said we were going to, you know, and then try to solve this problem together. >> Why is that so important for them to understand that because in the season that >> Yeah, that's the way it works. That's the way it works. There's something every week. Um you're always trying to you know, solve challenges and solve problems and and it's again, it's not just me in a closet figuring it out. It's it's all of us kind of having those conversations and understand how we see things and how we want to how we want to be and all of us coming to, you know, solutions. That's so we did today. >> Talking about the joint practices, how much more can you do or show Black Mamba return when it's a practice and it's not broadcast local kind of TV preseason game? Is there any >> Yeah, it's a little maybe it's a little it's uh mean, you're going to practice the stuff you've been practicing in camp. There might be some things you hold back. but it's different than a game. You're not you're not game planning the team. So, you're just kind of running running the greatest hits sort of speak but there's also times where, you know, we need to see guys in certain match-ups and guys in certain positions and you know, you're you're trying to compete and do very well, but not at the expense of, you know, evaluating your team the best you possibly can and put them in those situations. So, I think it's kind of a combo for combo platter for all those things. >> Do you have any more clarity on when Julian will be able to get out there at practice team? >> Uh he's working back he's working his his way back now, but no new timetable or anything. >> Do you have any more firm timetable for Terrion and when he'll report? >> Uh yeah, no update on on his front. >> Where is Flurry going to call plays from the sideline all year? >> I think there I think he might call this one from the booth. Um you will quote me on that, but don't quote me on that. We'll have an I'll I'll we'll kind of confirm. I think that's the plan right now, but we haven't like stamped it yet, but we'll let you know. >> What are the pros and cons of upstairs, downstairs? What do you like going? >> I'm not really sure. I just I think it's a personal preference on how well you can see it versus how you can communicate, where the rest of the staff is, like their roles. Um some guys, I don't know, they kind of like just being away from things so they can some guys like being in it. I I prefer to be in it, you know, be in the fight and you I'm you're kind of used to seeing it from a certain angle, so Um never really called offensive plays before unless you count like JV Cedar Shoals. >> Is it easier for you to reach out and touch an offensive play card on the sideline than staying downstairs? >> No, no, no. I just I'm on their frequency and just it's just as easy, yeah. >> It seems Sam looked pretty sharp out there today. What what did you kind of think of I guess practice today, but then overall where he's kind of at in camp >> Yeah, Sam's had a great camp. Um think feel like we got a becoming crisp like becoming clearer plan on how we want to operate from now to to go play the game, the first game. And uh he's been right there every step of the way. He's been he's been tremendous. >> Any Kimen worries or any anything with him? >> no update on Nick, sorry. >> Um couple guys we didn't see out there yet. Tory Horton, is he okay or is he >> Um Yeah, Tory's working through some things. Yeah, not a lot of updates on the injury front right now, but they're with a couple guys down today. >> Seemed like Jared Ivey was extremely disruptive in the game on Saturday night and then we didn't see much early in camp, but how have you seen him take some steps forward here and >> Yeah, did some good things on the edge. great competition there, but uh he definitely had some really good plays, so that was that was positive. That was good. >> What Jaylen Gaines in in the same vein, what do you what do you think of his camp so far and kind of what he's done? >> Yeah, um Jaylen's had a good camp. He said he said again he said some splash plays. I think uh I think his like Jaylen just he he cares so much like it just matters so much to him. And so sometime like sometimes we we just want him to let it go rip, man, because he's a talented guy. He's strong, he can play the edge. He can rush, you know, he's plays a lot energy and when he does the when he does that, he's he's a dang good football player. When he kind of you know, thinks about too much or whatever, that might slow his game down a little bit, but he's doing a really good job. >> Anything else? >> Okay. All right, thank you.

title: Cam Jurgens & More on Improvements During Training Camp
text: talk about uh during practices just what you get out of there. >> Uh honestly, it's just nice not going against your own team, you know, every single day. So, it's like a breath of fresh air. You get to go and see another team and kind of work all your stuff and it's always fun when you're going on the road with a team for a week kind of bonding, coming together as a team. So, that's the best part. You know, we're we're all there together staying in a hotel and enjoying it. You know, it's kind of kind of wish I had it like 20 years ago or they travel elsewhere and everybody stay in some old dorms together. So, this close as we get to it. >> Air conditioning though. >> Air conditioning. >> They didn't have it in the old days. >> I don't think I would have made it. >> What you watched on Saturday do you kind of take into joint practices for yourself? >> Uh, from this last game? >> Just haven't watched it. >> Yeah. I mean, uh, the main thing is just like, are you saying ask that again? >> Uh, just from what you saw personally Saturday from the sideline, do you take anything from that as you're going into joint practices, just things that you were dwelling on? >> Uh, no, I wouldn't I wouldn't say that for for a lot of it Saturday is just seeing those guys go out there and how much effort they're giving. And then, you know, we're still working on our craft and getting everything, you know, with the new offense, things are going to keep coming together and we just want to keep going here. You know, try not have too many setbacks. >> When you see guys like Jake, guard, how challenging is that? How impressive? >> Yeah, it's kind of, you know, what you have to do? Uh, I mean, my second year I started at guard here and now I'm going back to center. And these guys, they have to learn center position, play guard, and and a lot of it, you know, when you're playing center, you're going to you're going to have to know what everybody's doing. And then when you're guard, it's it's kind of switching that off and making sure, you know, your technique changes, your feet changes. So, being able to be very smart and vocal, you know, just going out there, communicating your ass off helps with everything. helps you be more confident in what you're doing and helps everybody around you. So, those three guys, you know, they're doing a good job at that and just communicating with everybody and, you know, it makes everything easier when everybody's talking and speaking the same language, if that makes sense. >> Specifically with Willie, you're someone who is comfortable or has experience going up against guys who outweigh you by a lot. How would you explain like how Willie makes it work at the size that he's at against bigger defensive tackles? Yeah, I mean he's he first of all, you got to have good technique and you got to have your hands in the right spot and you know, same thing with everything. You got to have, you know, your levers at a lower position than theirs and you got to take their power producing angles out. Um, and he does a great job of that. You know, he plays low and gets into people's chests and you know, he like I'm saying from Saturday, the main thing we're looking for and you know, all these coaches is effort, effort, effort. And that's one thing Willie gives every single play is effort. So, that's huge. You know, you can't always coach effort into guys. >> Cam, we're pretty deep into camp here. How do you feel physically? How are how are you managing uh anything that you know, you've had in the past? >> Uh, you know, I'm feeling good, but it's always tough in camp because, you know, you kind of you're beating yourself down. You're kind of getting into a valley to come out for the season. And this is kind of like a little bit past the hard days. And but yeah, feeling good. I'm excited for the season. Um it feels like it's so far away, but then you know a week from now it's going to feel a little different. >> Communication you were talking about before with with the younger players. How's that come along with you guys as far as the new offense, the first team and you know the protection things and everything? Is it is it on track from your perspective? >> Yeah, I think it always takes a little bit more time when you're learning new languages and and verbiage. you know, we'll go out there and we'll try to make a call and then, you know, in the, you know, we'll go in and talk about in the offense like, hey, I think this call may get confused with this. Let's change it to this. And so, there's certain things get tweaked throughout camp. And, you know, by the time we get to game days, we want to make sure that's kind of iron ironed out. And, you know, we went through some of that today. And it's just tweaking little things and make sure we're all on the same page. Um it's kind of hard to divulge into everything, but I think uh we're doing so much better. You know, every week it's big strides. >> With the changes in the blocking scheme, I'm curious just are there different places for in terms of like what's called a to hold or not called a to hold or where your hand placements are. Does that change a lot from what y'all are used to? And how mindful kind are you looking into that? >> Uh no, I don't think so. Um, I would say it's more about, you know, your feet. Uh, you know, when you're always locking into a block and and once your feet stop and that guy's still moving, your hands are on there, you're you're going to get called for a hold and and seems like, you know, the these refs are going to be looking for that. And that's why I'm saying with effort and finish, you know, with this scheme, it's it's all about keep running your feet and working through your blocks. And, you know, if if you're being active, that kind of takes care of itself. Um, but another thing, just having good technique and having your hands where they're supposed to be. >> It's it's pretty well it's it's well established here that obviously the starters don't play in the preseason games. Would you feel any more prepared for the season if you took, you know, a series or two or the way it's worked here? Are are are you ready for week one no matter what? >> I mean, yeah, we'll be ready no matter what. That's what you got to be got to. But I think, you know, the coaching staff here, they do a good job of having a culture of, you know, we come out here to practice, it's a game. You know, we're going against our defense, it's a game. We're going to go to New England and these joint practices, we treat it like a game. And all these situations, I mean, we do so many different situations, you know, end of the first half, end of the game, two minute, four minute, and just putting yourselves in game-like situations to where when you get to the game, it feels like you've already been there. And I think if we weren't practicing like this and putting ourselves in that situations, I think I would be apt to say, "Yeah, I'd like to get a series." But Coach Sap does such a good job of putting yourself in, you know, gamelike situations. >> Every time we talk to Shawn Mannon, he he preaches pre- snap limiting confusion, all you guys being on the same page of all the things to focus on right now. Why do you think that seems like such a priority to him? >> Tyler Ste is in the mix. Um it's I mean from the offensive st like offensive coordinator position to the quarterback to the O line setting the huddle it's just like that's that's a stuff that doesn't take talent necessarily doesn't take physical attributes and you know it's it's listening it's learning and it's being active with everything. So that's the things that we can really focus on and you can always coach technique but you know those those little intangible things are is what wins and loses a lot of games that you know fans and media does don't see and we do and so that's what we need to be harping on and getting better at. >> Tai Robinson so far this summer you got a sack on Saturday like one last week he was starting to really progress and do well there too. Yeah, just giving good effort, you know, going back there. I mean, just playing hard and going to the snap of the whistle. Probably went a little too far on the one, but that's, you know, I think he was ready to hit somebody besides our own guys. We don't get to hit our quarterbacks here. So, yeah, I'm I'm excited for him. I'm excited for I mean, our our D line, it's it's deep, very deep this year. So, I'm excited to see all those guys play. What's it like going up against? >> What's it like going up against Williams? >> I'll be excited to see him. Yeah, I mean I'll be excited to see all my former teammates up there and that'll be fun. So, thanks guys. >> Thanks. >> Getting there. Yeah, we're getting there. It's uh football's still the same in the essence of it, you know, but there's just a few caveats that are added to the minute responsibilities that, you know, they're going to take some reps figuring out. It'll take a little bit of time. >> Figure out. >> Uh well, I mean, the big thing is my coverage aspect. Uh you know, um haven't been asked to do that very much in my career. And so, um slowly but surely I'm gaining confidence in that world. And uh I think that's just going to be all that matters is more reps I get, the more times I see it, you know, I won't be so unfamiliar. Um Vic is known for that uh requiring his edge guys to drop into coverage. How much difference is is that in your history? >> Oh is it's uh it's completely different for me personally. Um you know I was asked to to drop maybe once or twice a game in the history and uh or in years past and now uh it could be every other play and it's just a matter of like I was saying a moment ago there's a few little caveats that could make the whole thing or break it. whether it's just having my eyes in the right place and um those will come with reps. >> You had a couple interceptions a couple years ago. How how did they come about? Were you dropping then at all or was it just >> Those were a little mixes. Those were um a little mix of me being able to get off the ball and kind of see some some key things to know a screen pass was coming. And I think majority of those came off those quick screens off to the outside. Um, and I was able to get a paw up and maybe bat those down or try to tip one to myself when um, I'm kind of put in a different situation now where I won't be able to get up as field get up the field as quickly as I have in the past. >> I'm curious with how that's presented to you from Vic whenever you haven't done that a lot in your career. Does he say all right simply this is what you're going to do or is it come with like a sense of here you've done this here's some video we think you can do more? >> Yeah, there's Well, uh, you know, I believe they wouldn't they wouldn't have me here if they didn't think I could do what the whole job entails. Um, and so, um, I've seen myself do it. We've I've shown it on film a few times here at practice. Um, and you know, I think part of the reason I was playing so well, or not so well, but part of the reason I was playing, um, on Saturday was to get me some game reps in a position I've never been in before. And a huge example is that route u, that wheel route I had to cover. And, um, you know, I don't think I was too far off, but there's a few things that I can do to really make that even tighter. like I kept I looked back at the quarterback and you know first time being out there doing that you're not supposed to look back I'm supposed to keep my eyes on my work and so you know having the guys help me out with that too. It's simple things like that that can make all the difference. >> You played twice uh during the regular season previous years got them in the joint practice. How familiar are you with them and does it bring any extra juice for you? >> Yeah. Um I'd like to think I'd know these guys uh pretty well. you know, I've probably played them close to 14 times now in my career and um uh obviously a lot has changed over the years, but um at their core, they're still the same team and um I'd like to think that I know what's coming for me. >> Any extra juice playing against them from? >> Uh always. Um you know, the Patriots are a great organization. Um obviously they went to the Super Bowl last year. Um but it's just going to be another day of practice for us and we're just going to try and do our best every single day. >> You mentioned that real route. When's the last time you can remember that you were kind of in open field running? >> First time >> ever. >> My first time. Yes, sir. >> Dating back to high school. >> I was 270 lbs in high school. I was 280 in college, so I wasn't covering any wheel routes back then. >> Uh, for sure. This has definitely been a challenge. Um, but the guys I've been surrounded with have made this into a really fun endeavor and they've made this um, challenge become more enjoyable just from a sense of I like challenging myself, but I I'm going to mess some things up and no one the world isn't falling apart just because AJ messed something up, you know, and everyone's been very helpful. I'm encouraging, you know, that's honestly what's been help propelling me forward in this situation is um, having these guys around me. That's honestly a huge help. you talk to his first ever football game. What was your takeway from that and then also like >> how far he's come? >> Yeah. Um I I I wish I had the chance, but I never got to see him during OTAAS to kind of see his fresh fresh start. I got to see him. He was showing me he was teaching me how to to read some of the things when I first got here because I it was a new world for me as well. And um just to see his confidence rise and grow, it's um it's been awesome to see. I mean, he's done nothing but get better. um his game and his mentality. What what do what do you like about what do you like about him? How he runs it >> and the guys [clears throat] in the room? >> Yeah. Um you know, Wash Wash has been awesome. He's been great when it comes to just listening to his vets. I think me and JG are the two oldest guys in the room. And um between us, we've got a lot of a lot of plays under our belt, a lot of games under our belt. And Wash has been awesome when it comes to just trying to take this and that from the players that he's had and guys that have been in a lot of games. You know, he he really listens to what they have to say and and and puts that into some of our meetings and we kind of build things around things that we've experienced firsthand. And so I can really appreciate that. And I think that we've gotten better and tighter as a group because of that. you and you and Evetti have uh >> lined up as bookends >> uh Saturday night. >> Yeah. >> Two new guys on the team. What's your relationship like uh you know on the field off the field? >> Yeah. Um obviously during camp it's a little tough um off the field to kind of get into things especially when we get off around 7:45 8:00 at night. We have Katie coming in now. >> You guys doing? >> How are you? >> Oh, well. >> How'd you feel uh Saturday night getting out there? You had a pretty good run. >> Yeah, I feel good. You know, anytime you get the chance to go out there and play football, I always feel good. You know, I know it's preseason, but it's always good to get ready to kind of get in that groove. It it helps come when it comes down to the to the regular season. We were just talking to AJ about the coverage responsibilities you guys have in this scheme and big asked you to drop occasionally. Uh the biggest thing was get getting comfortable with this game. I feel like now I'm in a good place. What was your take away from watching Joshua play his first ever kind of football game and how far he's come so far? >> Yeah, I mean Joshua, he's a pretty talented player.
