Two new guys on the team uh growing together, that kind of thing. >> Yeah, I feel like we have a pretty good relationship. That's something that we have built uh during our time here. I mean, he came at the end of OTAAS and so far in training camp like given the fact that we both new into this defense and we for the most part I've been going out there with him. So, we try to communicate every time we out there, make sure we on the same page. I feel like so far he's been great. Uh, couple things I get from him, couple things he able to pick up from me. So, we work well together. >> What do you like about the group as a whole? >> Um, I feel like everybody's a little bit different in terms of like things that they do pass rush wise and I'm able to pick a little bit little bit from everybody like AJ got his own rushes, Nolan, JX, uh, JG. So, being able to work with each other, kind of pick up from each other and learn from each I mean, it's always a great thing. >> What do you expect from the joint practices in New England and going against them in their >> uh obviously going against another team? The expectation is always to go out there and whoop ass. And I think the biggest thing for us is trying to see where we compare and come out uh the better team after those two days. >> Thanks, man. >> Uh yeah, I thought the line was really good. I thought protection was really well. Um we watch we watched it early today. Um, so it was really cool to see a lot of the a lot of the young dudes go out there and be able to perform. Um, you know, it's a lot of things to work on and uh I think we're all excited to improve on that. >> There's been a little bit of a tension, not tension per se, but you know, things have gotten a little heated here in the last couple of practices between guys. Are you guys ready to go and hit somebody else now? >> Yeah. Yeah, for sure. I think uh this is what happens in camp. We've been we've been hitting each other for the past like three weeks and I think uh you know it's it's it's hot out here and I think sometimes tensions boil a little but at the end of the day we're all we're all family and so uh you know you know brothers fight sometimes but I think uh you know we're we're fast and we just keep moving forward. >> Speaking of the joint practice, you know um you guys did not you did not see any action and um you know a lot of the starters are not seeing action during the preseason. So, how valuable is that joint those joint practices um for you guys? >> Yeah, I think it's extremely valuable just cuz you get to see a different look. Um you know, we've been going against our guys for the past few weeks, so you get to go against different players. Um and I think just getting that uh just new exposure to to different things and and different looks and maybe some things that we don't expect and uh kind of working working through that I think is really good. Tyler, I was I was curious, you know, I know you guys didn't have the stars out there on Saturday, but just reflecting on some of the holding penalties that were in that. I It got me curious about the scheme change. >> Has things changed with that in terms of where you might find your hand placement in terms of what you had before and are there things that you're more mindful about in this game? >> Yeah, man. I think that sometimes this guys playing hard. I think, you know, penalties are is going to happen. You know, you know, it's not it's not like anything I don't think too major. I think uh you know, all in all of offensive line play, you kind of want to get your hands inside and I think our guys were doing that and so um I'm not I'm not sure that's really a a scheme issue. No. >> What has uh impressed you about guys like Willin in the guard room for young >> Yeah, they've they've you could tell they taken a big step this this year. It's it's really exciting to see them grow. Um they uh they're high effort players. They're really really quick, really strong, too. Um it's been really cool to see those guys go out there and compete um not only in the game this past Saturday, but every day. Um they've been doing a really good job. >> Where have you seen Drew Willie, I guess specifically grow just over the last year? >> Yeah, I think Drew Drew's definitely gotten a lot stronger. Um you could tell um you know, the offseason helped him out a lot. Um he's always been a really smart dude, always been like really really quick and I think that extra strength has been able to um been able to really help him uh grow this off season. And uh Willie um I mean we didn't really get to see too much of Willie. He wasn't with us in in in camp last year. Um but you could tell just as far as like his understanding of the game, his understanding of the scheme has really uh taken a big step forward and uh it's been really uh really cool to see Willie go out there and perform. >> Tyler, what about you? Why is your game taking the next step this off season into this training? >> Yeah, I think uh I think confidence has a has a lot to do with it. Um, I think just being just being uh more confident in in your abilities and what you can do. Um, I think I've honed in uh a little more on the schematic things and kind of understanding what we're trying to accomplish as a offense and what the defense is trying to do to us. Um, and uh yeah, I think I think those those things have been have been major. >> Where did the confidence boost come >> Um, I think just just playing games. I think just going out there uh you know, sometimes you fail, but sometimes you succeed. And I think uh just going out there and having an opportunity to to play a play a long stretch and then seeing yourself have a have some success I think just naturally allows you to build confidence and become a better player. >> How's this new scheme unlocking your abilities? >> Um I think it uh it gives us a better opportunity to go out there and and run a little bit a little bit more on our angles. I think uh I think it allows us to to not think as much. I think um in this scheme uh the points are kind of really already determined like within the play. So uh you don't really got to think too much about you know the the motions and how that affects where you're working to and things like that. So you can kind of go out there and play a little faster. Um and I think that's that's that does a good job too with um cuz we're we're more outside zone, you know, mid zone focus. So I think uh when we go and actually do duo run duo around inside zone, it uh it kind of scares those D linemen. they kind of start moving a little bit a little bit more and makes it a little easier. >> Looking forward to going against when you face the Patriots and how much will going against you know their top defense defensive line? >> Yeah, it'll it'll be really exciting. Um really exciting. We we all know Mil's a really good player cuz he was with us for a while. Um and so it'll be really exciting to go against a like a good defense. It's >> it's always cool to to uh to have a new challenge in front of you. So I think all the guys are really excited to do Is that is that kind of like the game for you guys starters and everything, you know, these joint practices? >> Yeah, I I would say so. I think uh I think that just it just ramps up intensity a little bit when you get to go against a different team. Um and a really good team, too. So, I think uh I think all the guys are ready to do that. >> And is that do you think that's enough to get you guys ready for the regular season? Because I mean, obviously, you guys probably aren't going to be playing. Yeah, I mean we we trust the coaches with uh what their plan is for the for the offseason and training camp. So I think whatever their decision is on on that, I think we're all on board with that. >> And Tyler, every time we talk to Shawn Manny, it seems like of all the things to focus on, he really focuses on pre- snap, everyone being on the same page, no infusion on the offensive line, >> why of all the things to focus on, do you feel like that's priority number one for him? >> Yeah, I think that's that's really important cuz, you know, we want everybody to have an understanding of what they're doing or what their role is on the offense. And then I think when everybody has that very clear understanding of what they're doing, it just allows everybody to play faster. And uh if you're playing faster than the defense, then you're going to have a better chance of of uh running good plays. So >> I know it was a few days ago, but the the fight that you got in with Fred Johnson, what happened there that >> um you know, it's football. Um excuse me. Um it's football emotions and you kind of fight with your brothers and um I don't know, it was just it was just football. Got a little heated. Um, it was wrong and it's not a standard that we set out here and um, it was a mistake and I messed up. >> Did you talk to Fred after you guys are all good? >> Yeah. Yeah, of course. That's football, guys. You guys just happen to be out here, you know what I mean? That's how football is aggressive. >> What about with Nick? Did you guys make it all about the fight? >> Yeah, I mean, Nick is a leader and he set the standard straight. Um, that's not acceptable. It's not something we do at this organization. Um, you know, and yeah. Uh, >> are you guys excited though to finally >> see somebody else? Yeah. Yeah, 100%. You know, um, at this point, you've been hitting each other so much. Um, you want to kind of create that camaraderie and go versus someone and, you know, ultimately like we want to get the train rolling, right? We're trying to have a great season. Um, and you started off with a great joint practice versus Boston. How important are those joint practices for you guys, you know, especially when a lot of you are seeing very limited, if not time at all during these preseason games? >> Very important. And um I think Nick kind of harps on that. Um you know, and it's a controlled environment to see a different picture. Um you know, at the end of the day, that's a Super Bowl team from last year. Um you're not going to get much better competition than that, right? So, you know, we're very excited and we're going to we're going to try to give them our best shot and I feel like likewise from their their part. >> Does it matter to you that you play in a setting like that rather than a preseason game where you get a couple of series? Is it >> um I mean, you know, I think that the point of the preseason, similar to like the end of the game, end of the season games is like if it's a game that doesn't matter, why do we put the risk of injuries or risk of players out there? Um, you know, I think that's kind of the mindset, especially if we can have controlled environments where we can still get the work and yeah, like why would we go and do that? >> Will you take a peek at all at the guys we're going to be going up against in New England beforehand? >> Me? >> Uh, maybe not a ton. I know they had a winnow. We went there two years ago and I think that's why uh Neil ended up getting paid. He had like a great great practice up there. Um, you know, but yeah, I mean, not a ton. You know, I think that we're confident and we want to go out and dominate and yet I think that they want to go versus us, right? We're good competition as well. >> I was I was going to ask you about Yeah. the >> If you think back, what did you learn from the way he he navigated his last year in Philly and from him in general? >> Yeah. I mean, Mill, you know, um didn't get as much opportunity till that last year and he took it and ran with it, right? So like kind of that's the mindset and you know he was a hard worker, played hard and um yeah I mean you you look back even all the way to Hardrave um Eagles kind of had a history of a DT doing really well and you know ended up somewhere else. >> How did that help you in general when you first came in terms of how he showed you how sported? >> He's just a super super uh down to earth guy, super um encouraging guy. Um wanted to see everyone win, you know. I think that's the the key with our room. Like I want to look back at our room and see a room of just like great BTS. You know, I don't I had it in college and I want to do it in the league. In college, I think all six of BTS I was with got drafted. You know, one of them is like all of Byron Murphy, Alpha Tins, like they're all all went super high, right? So, yeah. >> Watch. Yeah. Yeah. We were uh me and JD were golfing the other day and we faced that Mil. He's doing good. to watch him use his opportunity and get paid like that. >> When you were a younger player, did you watch that and and kind of >> be encouraged? >> Be encouraged by it. >> Yeah, I think everyone's encouraged by that, you know. Um, everyone's encouraged by seeing when someone ball out and um ultimately get to that second contract, which is kind of that like big abstract goal for players. >> You mentioned going up against the same guys every single game, practice. It seems like he got a sack today on Jaylen. What have we seen from this new offense now? >> Yeah. Um, you know, I think that it's a really cool offense. The hardest offenses we go versus are kind of this under center offense. Um, which really helps us to be able to see this in camp, you know, in practice against it. And, um, yeah, those those guys are confident. I think Squan's super excited to be in this kind of system. >> Got rolling available. >> Yeah, >> especially the offensive line. They keep talking about how they know exactly what the play is happening. They say they're playing faster because of that. Are you noticing that here in training camp? >> Yeah, 100%. I think that um I think this is like a really player friendly offense, if that makes any sense. Um you know, it gives guys the ability to kind of like not not be as much of an on the island. Um you know, the best offenses, it's that like um what's his name in the Packers and then you got the guys from the Rams and 49ers, right? And it's that tree, right? So like why would you over complicate it? Why not just get what already works? What makes me run uh steam particularly hard to defend? >> They can go right to left. He's going he's looking downhill. He's got a full head of steam. Um and then you start if you do it very really well, the linebackers start playing close and you get all these shots and you get all these like hide routes like the tight end will look like he's blocking. It's a play action. He'll be here. He'll go all the way here and he's on on the back side, you know. Um, and yeah, I mean they've those offenses have dominated, so why not run that similar offense? >> What did you think of Lu? >> Um, I mean, guys, it's day six. Um, he's strong as hell and, uh, he's learned. >> Was it fun just watching him get a chance to fight again? >> Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. It's his first ever live football action ever in his life, you know what I mean? So, yeah, it was cool. >> He was telling us, sorry, he was telling us just how proud he was of himself to be in that moment. Do you go back to being a little kid and remembering your first moments in football because that's technically what he's going through right now? >> Yeah, man. I remember when I was a little kid, I came I went to like um I tried I didn't I'd never throw the ball with my family cuz they don't know American football and I try to throw the football and it was horrible and they're like put me in the O line group, [laughter] you know. So, um yeah, it's it's been cool. If I could ask just, you know, you, JC, and JD, I mean, it seems like you guys are pretty well established and everything. Like, how how are you, how are you guys approaching camp, and how do you think it's been going for for you >> Yeah, I think we're all competing to be better, you know? Um, like I told you guys, I want to be the best team in that room. And I think everyone has that mindset, right? Um, so no one no one is even after you get the payday, now it's what are you going to do? Now you're the guy, right? So, um, yeah, that's our mindset. We're pushing for greatness and trying to become better players. >> And do you see that intellect they're questioning you just as much as you're pushing them? >> 100%. Yeah. I mean, you see JC out there dominating, you see JD out there dominating, they're like, what can what can you not like you you have to be motivated. Um, you know, the other day Clint put like some of the best defensive lines up in the meeting room and was like challenging us, you know, and that's that's the mindset, man. Like we're doing this. Why not? Aim for greatness. Where did you guys rank us? >> No, he was showing us some old school guys. It was like uh Deacons. It there was like it was like the Tampa Bay one. I don't know remember who was all on that, but then he showed us like Deacon Joneses. It was a couple of them with like some Hall of Famers and stuff like that which was sick. He should have showed us Reggie and um what's his name play next together? >> Jerome. Yeah, that was another >> Yeah, that was another good uh good deal on >> seasonwise. How do you view it? >> Man, we got our same goals and um we just hang our hats on certain things at this facility and in this building and that's what we do and that's what we try to get better at. I'm not going to tell you what we hang our hat on, but certain things that deal with, you know, the team goals. >> Uh joint practice is on the way. What do you expect those to be like, >> man? Exciting, man. Joint practices are always fun. You get to see somebody else um do different moves and, you know, get to fly around still and go hit somebody else. Uh, one of them being AJ potentially. What do you think of that, >> man? AJ a good rod receiver, man. It's no it's no bad blood this way, man. You talking about one of the best in the game. Like, y'all y'all make it out to be this and that, but you know, iron sharpens iron and I don't got to go up against him, so I ain't worrying about it, but you know, hopefully, you know, he don't catch too many balls and we do our job. For someone on the outside who might not understand, you know, with these limited snaps or or no snaps at all in preseason games for some of these guys, how vital are these point practices to really kind of, as you mentioned, like iron to represent? >> Man, you just get excited to hit somebody else. You know, they're very valuable, you know, cuz you get to see how your scheme works against other people's scheme and all the stuff that you've been working on all offseason. You know that it has a benefit. You just don't want to work all offseason and then, you know, you get there and be like, "Oh, well, got to throw that out." So that's really all all it does is build builds confidence in your playbook and what you believe in. >> Is it nice to be away with the guys for a couple of days too to build that camaraderie even off of the off the field? >> Oh, I mean shoot we build a camaraderie in the locker room even when we travel on on the plane we crack jokes and have fun man the whole nine yards and even from the coaches all the way to the players. >> What are your personal goals for your four for you? >> Play all 18. I talked about that and um you know just being available all 18 for my teammates and just personally for myself and the things how I carry myself. You know them last last year I missed six and it kind of hurt me and I just want to make sure I'm there for all 18. >> Jonathan's obviously a veteran through a lot but I would imagine it's difficult for him to not be on the field. How do you help him in the spirits and just being engaged? >> Oh yeah man that's OG man. He um he a vet. He help our room a lot man. just all the things that he talked about, all the things that he sees. Um, and you know, he been playing football for a long time. Not to say that, but you minute. So, I just like I'm a sponge every year. You know, I took everything that I could from Hos. I took everything I could from Sweat. Took everything I could from BG. I'm going to be doing the same thing. Just sitting in there asking questions, learning from him. How he see run blocks, how he see this, how he see that. You know, you just sit there and ask some questions. >> All right. So, when you call BG an OG, that made sense, right? But like, what is the cut off? He hasn't been in the league that long. [laughter] >> I say I don't know. I call Andy OG. You know, JG OG. We got a couple of them, you know. Shout out my dog Marcus. I don't want to do it like that. He triple OG. You know, he holding he holding his name. It's a couple guys that's up there. >> Cool. >> What's impressed you about Weir and uh and and who are >> who? Uh we Josh Josh Weir and And >> Josh. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. You butchered that, my boy. Oh man, he he a good guy, man. He got tenacity. He got effort. Um he got stamina. I tell him, man, long as you play in the outside linebacker group with effort and toughness, you'll be you'll be good. So, um I was really impressed with him and you know, he made our group look well. >> What did you see from Arnold AK? >> AK, man. I love his game. I always respected his game when he was at Atlanta. You know, I'm a Georgia boy, so I just, you know, sometimes turn on their film and stuff like that. So, um, just respect his game, respect his work ethic, respect his talent. Um, learning a lot from him, too. You know, certain rushes, certain moves that he do, and so is AJ, man. We got a got a hellified room. And, um, I just tell them boys, I take privilege in coming to work every day cuz you never know who you learn from and what you can take from somebody. >> Milton was here when you were a rookie, right? >> Yeah. Millionaire Milk. >> Are you excited to see? >> Yeah, I'm excited to see Millionaire Milk, man. We used to call him Mayback Milk before he before he had the Mayback. Now he got the M back for real, man. I tell him, uh, I'm excited to see Milk, man. I'm excited to see guys, you know, especially when they play on the same side of the ball cuz we we crack jokes defense on defense and, you know, when they go to the other team, it's more serious. So, but man, I just wanted to crack jokes with my dog. I miss him. >> How about AJ Brown? >> Yeah, man. I mean, it's the same thing, man. You miss seeing guys, but you know, y'all trying to make it seem like, you know, that's one of the best NFL wide receivers in the game. And um he's a great teammate, great guy.

title: Sean Mannion on First Preseason Game & Training Camp Progress
text: How's it going, guys? >> So, what was your uh I guess initial thoughts on the first time out there? >> Yeah, obviously, you know, want to have a uh a better performance offensively than we put on tape um the other night, but um you know, we got things that obviously we need to correct. I thought the biggest thing that stood out in the game is we were just we weren't staying on schedule, right? We had a lot of first and long, second and longs. You know, penalties led to a lot of that, a couple negative runs. So, I think if we were be able to better stay on schedule and kind of eliminate some of those miscues on early downs, we'll keep ourselves in more manageable third down situations and uh and hope, you know, lead to a better result. >> How much of that is a product of still learning the scheme and getting comfortable inside that? >> You know, I think a lot of it comes down to just fundamentals and execution. I I feel like we're in a good place mentally as an offense. Um there really weren't a ton of mental errors from the game, which is encouraging. You know, a lot of young guys in there their first time with live game action. and it's it's not scripted, you know, it's all calling it from the sideline. So, I was pretty encouraged with the with the mental side of things. I think it's just carrying the fundamental work, you know, that we've done in practice to the to the game setting. Um, I think that was the biggest takeaway for me here. >> The thought process for having Eli Sour um in that role and we've primarily seen him just the third unit not doing a lot of blocking in team situations. >> Yeah, I mean, we want to see what all these guys can do. Um, and tight end's a position that requires a lot of versatility. We're going to ask all these guys to uh be productive players in both phases. Um and the preseason is a great opportunity to to push these guys and evaluate what they can do and give them things to work on every day at practice and then see them take it to the to the game. I know Eli's, you know, put a lot of work into improving as a blocker and and um along with that entire position group, there's a huge commitment to being productive in both areas. So, we want to see what all all of our players um in that room can do in both phases of the game. What's the process like with you on the field with calling plays and and are you indeed going to call the next game from the group? >> Yeah, it was smooth. I I felt comfortable. I thought um our staff did a great job. The communication was clear. Um you know, we didn't have any substitution issues. We didn't have any um you know, play calls get jacked up where you know, we got caught with them substituting late or anything like that. I thought the lines communication were clear. I was happy with um you know, how the quarterbacks were able to get us in and out of the huddle. We weren't really up against the play clock at all, so I was happy with that. Um, yeah, I am I'm planning on calling the next game from the booth. I think it's an opportunity to get a feel for both and um and then go from there. But it was, uh, you know, that's been the plan all along and, um, I think it'll be an interesting perspective, but um, you know, I think through this preseason, an opportunity to kind of experience both. >> What differences do you expect? What differences? >> How would you still play with Andy and Tanner in particular, just how they >> Yeah, you know, there was there was some good and and and some that can obviously improve. You know, I think, you know, the third down third downs got to be better there. Some of them were tough spots to be fair. You know, you're in a third and extra long situations. It's going to be it's going to be an uphill battle, but you know, I think just play the play. Just stay with the process, stay with your read, your footwork. Um, you know, there were some some good examples. You know, Tanner hit a slant route. Cole hit one to EJ over the middle of the field. You know, um, we had to get back on track on the first series of the game. Andy had a nice ball to Coupe on an out route to get us into a third and manageable. Then we take a penalty to go back to third and 15. So, um, you know, there were some glimpses there of of of what we want to see, but I think the biggest thing that, you know, the whole group can improve on is just stay within the play, trust your footwork, trust your training, and, um, and and go cut it loose. >> What differences are you keeping an eye on in the operation when you move to the booth? >> You know what? I think it'll just be more for me and just how I feel I can see the game from there versus the sideline. You know, I've spent the majority of my life on a on an NFL, you know, on NFL sideline, a college sidelines. you know, I've seen the game from that perspective. I spent a year in the booth in Green Bay, so um but in a different capacity. So, I think it'll just be to get a feel for it. Honestly, I just kind of want to experience it once and I think it'll offer good perspective and um like I said, it was comfortable in game, but the plan all along was to kind of get a taste of both and and then [snorts] move forward with the you know, with a plan of attack for the regular season. >> Yeah, he ran around made some plays. you know, his athletic traits, you know, those are the ones that sometimes in a practice setting with a red jersey. Um, you can't always get a true um representation of that, right? The quarterback's not live in practice, but you know, he ran around, did a nice job. You know, there's some things to clean up. I think, you know, a couple just again just smoothing out some of those decisions, right? You know, I'm sure there were some um nerves his first NFL action, you know, third down, kind of thrown into traffic there, but really settled in from that point forward and let us on a nice drive to to score and and get us on the board at the end of the game. >> So, what was your your personal self scouting process like after looking for out of your >> Yeah, you know, I felt I felt comfortable. I felt um the call sheet was well organized. Like I said, I was really satisfied with with you know, our staff, our players. I thought the communication with Nick, the communication with the players on the sideline, substitution was clean. Um, so yeah, I I'd say, you know, one game in, I'm I'm very very happy with our process and, you know, we'll keep always, you know, like anything, whether it's scheme or or the process on the sideline and calling plays, we'll always try to see if we can make it better. But honestly, through one game, I I felt really good about it. What is something that you learn something that you can't learn unless you actually >> Oh, that's a No, that's a good question. You know, I think it's, you know, you when you're in a game and, you know, especially when you're kind of up against some long yard longer yardage situations, you know, I [snorts] think it's just always having a feel for the quarterback, especially when, you know, in the preseason it's dictated that a new quarterback's going into the game. You know, we're rotating all of our guys through, but how do we get them into a rhythm? You know, I I I feel like that's something excuse me. um you know just new quarterback enters the game, might be in a tough spot early, what are his comfort calls? And that's something we get a feel for every day at practice with the guys and then certainly in the game that you know it kind of came to life there with a couple long yardage situations early. >> Did you have much communication with Jaylen during the game in terms of how he was seeing things from the sideline? >> Yeah, you know he was on the sideline with the QBs the whole time. Um great teammate. You know, he was he was always around. He was engaged. Um so, you know, between him and Parks, there was a lot of resources there to support the quarterbacks on the sideline. Markel Bell. How did Mark Bell show? >> Markeel did a nice job. You know, I really think, you know, we talked about I think last week. Um, you know, there's a crop of young linemen that we're really excited about. You know, Markeel, obviously, you know, some of our interior players, Willie, Drew, Jake did a really nice job. So, um, a lot of them, you know, and I I could name all of them, but, you know, a lot of them are, uh, you know, have done a nice job in practice. It was cool to see him in live game action. Um, you know, but you could feel the play style, the effort. You know, that was the one thing that stood out. You know, I know we didn't have the performance we wanted, but the effort was there across the board and um you know, Markeel certainly had a big part of that. >> With Mark, I noticed there a few times where he was in a two-point stance and the rest of the line is in a in a three-point stance. Is that just because he's so tall it's hard to get down on the ground? And I guess what goes into that decision making? >> Yeah, we use both and we we we train all of our guys um to be in both. Sometimes it's based on the alignment um you know, where they they may be in a two, they may be in a three. Um, but Coupe does a great job. You know, we're going to train all of our guys to to be able to use both stances. >> How limited was the menu, so to speak? And as you watch the game back, do you think this is what I would call in this situation if I had play at my disposal? >> Yeah, you always do you kind of a little afteraction report and and a self scout in terms of how you call the game and things you could do better, things that things that you want to lean into further. um you know, the scheme and the and the um game planning in the preseason is is almost a little bit secondary to wanting to evaluate the guys in terms of their execution, their fundamentals. We just want to kind of keep him on the path that uh keep him on track with what he's been doing so far. He made a one really nice throw I like, but listen to what he said after. >> How quickly do you anticipate going to that tape? >> Oh, definitely right after this. I've nothing nothing else to really do tonight. It's not practice where it's like, okay, incomplete pass, next play, boom. It's It's not scripted. It's It's the real game. You don't under- There's no saying what could happen. All you can control is that present moment. So, I look forward to learning from it, and it it's a great moment, especially as being able to play football in the NFL and having so much gratitude, but also want to take advantage of the opportunity. >> You guys can all draft the guy that wants to hang out at the cool convention. I'm going to be grinding tape with Fernando Mendoza. Raiders have had a lot of guys. Wanted to be the cool guy. I got a I got a news for you. Between Mendoza and Kirk Cousins, I mean, it's a nerd fest. I love their quarterback room. I really do. Kirk Cousins is another one. He just goes out, family guy, works hard, bed early, has squeezed every ounce of talent out of his career from Michigan State. So, I I I love it. I thought he looked really, really good. And listen, I went to the Bears-Browns game. You watch two to three series, that's it. I'm I'm not making any, you know, it's it's kind of fun to go watch the draft picks. I went and watched the Bears draft picks. I went and watched the Browns draft picks. By the way, Concepcion, that receiver for Cleveland, that dude is fast. He's going to be a really good pro if they can find somebody in Cleveland to get him the ball.

text: from practice for throwing a punch and then Trubisky is getting looked at for his bicep. I mean there's every every week we're not playing an FCS opponent, you know, it's not Alabama versus FCS or Ohio State versus FCS. So, he's there's going to be a lot of peaks and valleys with all these young kids. Um they just got to keep If they go out there and fight and play as hard and strain as as much as we ask them to strain and communicate to the level that they need to communicate, you at least give yourself a chance. >> Is that a tough balance to act in the secondary? You want a certain amount of physicality, but you probably don't want them going in headfirst either. >> Yeah, again unfortunately, you want them to have a little bit of control going up there. Uh it is a competitive period in two minute and they're trying to win. Thanks, dude. But, uh you want him to be mindful of where he is on the football field and take care of his teammates for sure. >> What's your take on you, Robert, about about JC as he's progressed through camp through preserve? >> The You know, the one thing that he's done that uh uh I don't feel like we saw a year ago is the physicality at which he plays. You know, he's at a really good weight, so his foot speed is at is where we want it to be and and we felt like he was always strong enough, but you combine the foot speed with the physicality that he's playing playing with and uh I mean, he's moving people. He's strapping people at the line of scrimmage. Um you know, the challenge for him is not to not to take his flowers, you know, right now. Just stay on the grind, stay where he is, uh try to improve not only physically, but mentally. And um but he's uh he's tracking to have a really nice year. He's just got to stay the course. >> When you have guys who are When you have guys who have missed a whole year like Wilson, like even Leavitt, what's the What is the hardest part for them to kind of get reacclimated into the technique and the timing of everyday work? >> Um you know, I I'd probably be be a question, you know, I I like I'd like to think just a real life action in terms of like for the quarterback like getting hit for the first time is is is healthy for them. You know, cuz everything speeds up on game day. You know, so it's just it's just a matter of getting reps, getting yourself acclimated. But again, these guys are professionals. They've been playing football their entire lives and uh I don't want to say it's like riding a bike, but at the same time, you know, we're we're heading into week four of training camp and uh you know, they they should be able to start picking up steam. >> Going back to J.C., is that him making a conscious effort to be more physical to like challenging him? How does that affect >> I I think it's all encompassing. I think it's always in there. You know, when we evaluated him coming out of college, uh we felt like he was a big, strong, athletic, physical human being and uh but it's all encompassing. You know, when you have when you he's always been massive. And that's what we've talked about with J.C. when we got here and I'm sure it's been a a topic of discussion for him in the past, but he doesn't have a weight problem. He has a I he can look at a weight when he's when he's working out, he'll go look at a bar and he'll gain 5 lbs of muscle. So, it's more of a like he's an elite person. He's got elite work ethic. It's he's just got to be very conscientious. He can get as big as he wants to get. It's just going to affect his foot speed. So, there's a balance of understanding that he's already plenty strong enough. How much can he work to keep his weight at a spot where he doesn't lose his strength, but he gains a bunch of speed? You don't want him to go down too much where he gains a whole bunch of speed and loses power. And so, right now he's at a sweet spot and he's just got to be able to maintain that. >> Are the push-ups for who lost the day and how do you determine it on a close >> So, yes, good question. So, every day at the end of in in the second half of practice, we have a team comp. Um and so, today's team comp was 2-minute end of game. Offense needed a touchdown. Um they didn't score in either one of those, so it goes to the defense. And sometimes it'll be a efficiency period where it's move the ball and we're working off the NFL standard of efficiency where first down, second down, third down, you know, you're winning and losing based on the down. Sometimes it's a third down period, whatever it is. And so whoever whoever loses that day has to push-ups. >> Do they know that? >> They know going into the day. >> What's the scoreboard looking like when that two-minute practices and and is there any kind of a motivating handicap or offense defense who wins the most times? >> Uh it's it's more pride. You know, that's a good question. I'll get the update from our chief of staff and get that to you. But you know, they do there are there are there several different things. You know, we do this uh You know, we call it a king of strain award in each position group and you know, the winner gets premier parking spots out there for the season, but uh Um but there's little things, but the these guys you know, credit to the players, they've been working their tails off. I don't I don't know what it's been in the past or anything, but today was a very very physical, hot, steamy practice and and I thought our guys answered the bell. They worked from from snap to whistle, from drill one to to the last drill and um absolutely captured the day. So it was it was a really productive day and hopefully we can do it again on Wednesday. >> I know they're working hard for you guys. >> Board and Board had mentioned that the game has started to speed up for him. And I know things speed up on game day, but there were a couple times where it looked like he progressed through too fast. Do you talk to him about like balancing that or how do you go about coaching that? >> It's the same thing, you know, it it's all reps. Like like I said, on game day things actually go faster. So it's a whole new stimulus, right? So it's good that we're able to get out there, get those reps. Um you know, hopefully it progresses into a I mean, we got a whole new stimulus on Sunday night. That's Sunday night football. These kids haven't really had national exposure. Um you got the world champs coming in the town. So there's there's a whole new stimulus that they've got to go to attack and uh and I think it's awesome. You know, like you can't you can't expose a team especially a young team like ours to enough of this stuff as we as we continue to grow and develop to the team we want to be once the season hits but uh you know, for Cam again like everyone it's reps. It's trusting in your technique. It's trusting in your fundamentals. It's trusting in your preparation and just going out and executing. >> How's Joshua Williams done? I know he's got the yellow non-contact jersey on but that doesn't seem to be hindering him in terms of going out there being physical. Seems like he's maybe closing some of the gap that maybe was there at the start. >> Yeah, he's getting closer to full contact and so there's there's moments where he's testing it and uh uh he's he's at least being smart where he's not catching guys off guard. But um but but I like him a lot, man. He's a big long corner. He's physical at the line of scrimmage. He's very smart. He's instinctive. He's also a great special teams player. So um you know, he's he's a he's definitely a a NFL caliber corner. >> I know you got your time and they're doing you a favor to a degree. You talked about the officials yesterday and you're not at risk of fine here. Would you like to make a statement about the inconsistencies on the pass PIs? >> Uh here? In practice? You know what? Some of them I overrule. Some of them I keep the So a lot of times, you know, even though it's a move the ball period, I might disregard a penalty just to keep the drive going cuz while it is move the ball we're still trying to have like an eight simulate an eight play drive. Um you know, so we're at that part of camp where you know, you know, I've always said forever that a a player's capable of going 70 plays in a row if he gets if it's all three and outs. Uh the hard part is when you hit an eight play drive and then the other side of the ball goes three and out and then you're out there for another eight play drive. That's where you get taxed but I have no issue with the officials here. They've they've been doing a great job. They give us the reports. They're not going to be 100% but uh but at least it's something we can all learn from.

title: JC Latham, Wan'Dale Robinson & Jermaine Johnson at Titans Camp
text: I guess it's a casualty, maybe more in his first time really around you. Making him more of a conscious effort to play more physically or you just noticing that? >> Uh, I think it both ends of that is true. Um, I think he's definitely making the conscious decision to play more physically, but I think the other end of it, as I said last time when I was up here, is, you know, being the team that it was in the past, you know, when you're looking to establish yourself not only as a as a player or as a unit as an offense and team and franchise, you know, there's there's no revolution without bloodshed, you know, so you're every single day you're going to you're going to step up and you're going to be as physical as possible and pose your will day in and day out, so that's what you're going to see. Tensions rise, tensions flare, and I mean, cuz we're it's a it's a very emotional, very tension game. Um, but yeah, I mean, just playing with physicality every single play through and through the whistle is something that we pride ourselves on and one of our pillars of our our unit. >> Is it challenging that they're rotating so many guys through when they guard and I know that most of you are comfortable as going through so many guys been a challenge for you or >> Uh, no, it's just an opportunity. You know, you look at it. I mean, that's what training camp is for. That's just football and and at the end of it, I mean, you know, you look at last year, I was hurt. The right guard had you know, some injuries. You know, center had some injuries, unfortunately, so you know, I mean, you you have the idea like, yeah, I want to play with the starter the whole time, you know, that's the guy you build your chemistry with, but at the end of the day, um, you you build chemistry with everybody because you never know what could happen. You know, you see guys moving from position to position, you see guys lining up different places, you see guys doing a whole bunch of different things, so um, it's not necessarily a challenge per se, you got changing your perspective to look at as an opportunity to just build those chemistry, so you know, God forbid something does happen to where I'm out or somebody else is out, whatever it might be, it's not like a shell shock that you're lined up to somebody. That's amazing. Yeah, I mean, chemistry with everybody >> is amazing. But I mean I love the kid. He has a immense amount of potential. It's a very dangerous word cuz you know you haven't really done anything yet, but you know I love his attitude every single day. I love his mindset every day. He's humble. Every single day he gets here he looks to work. He doesn't make any excuses. When he when he messes up or he feels he could have did better, he's blunt. He's extremely transparent about himself and communicating about himself on what he himself needs to do to be better. And you want to you want to be around a guy like that, you know, a guy who is not going to sugarcoat it, a guy who is going to line up and and give everything he's got to the whistle blows and through the whistle and establish the tone with everybody else. >> So what's the most weight you've ever lost during a practice? >> I've never actually lost weight. I don't know how. Yeah, I don't I don't know. I like yeah I'm I was 347 this morning and I was 348 after practice. So I don't Yeah, I don't know how that happens. I don't I'm not eating on the field. I'm just drinking water, so Yeah, I don't I don't know. >> I know you talked about him a little bit, but what do you think about the growth curve for Carmona and and what kind of duo could you be if he's the guy? >> Um I mean he's I feel like he matches my I mean all the guards really, but playing with him longer throughout this camp I feel like he matches you know the craziness that we have. You know, we all have handshakes out there. Our handshake is just two two hits to the chest and a head bump. Really heavy head bump, so Um but yeah, I mean he matches the intensity and I really like to see it. He he's not flustered. You know, a lot of times you when you play O-line you can't you can't be consistent with every single call. You got to be able to you know have some dummy cadences, dummy calls. He's not allowing that to throw him off his rhythm at all. So I mean it's it's really exciting to see and then I mean the curve I mean he's a rookie, so you you know, you go out there and then some level of learning curve to to the game and I feel like he's done a great job thus far. But then the guy he's lining up against is the best three tech in the league. So, you know, he's going against Jeffrey Simmons and there's times where it's like, you know, he does pretty good and there's other times where Jeff gets the best of him and, you know, part of us is like as a whole like we all try to help each other out where we're like, "Hey, we could do this better. We could do that better." But then at the same time that's Jeffrey Simmons. So, it's like, you know, you line up and you say you're going to do it this, do that, do that and execute as best as you can. And sometimes, you know, they get paid too. So, they might win a rep every here and there, whatever it might be. So, we try not to look at it in a sense of like hold ourselves down or, you know, put our heads down, whatever it might be. Understand that we can always get better with every single rep. >> How much are you looking forward to the opportunity to to go against Leonard Williams again in camp? I know you had that chance to go >> I mean, I'm just excited as a whole. I mean, you know, respectfully they're the Super Bowl champs. I mean, this is a amazing opportunity. They got a lot of great players over there. Him, Derrick Hall, you know, the three techs Murphy's incredible. So, you know, we're fired up. But I mean, honestly as a whole we're we're I think we done practicing them on Friday or something and we're we're not worried about that in the sense of, you know, we're focusing on finishing off today strong. We got a walk through later and then we got to finish off whatever comes with whatever today's challenges is. So, we're we be where our feet are and so we're not really looking forward to head or anything. >> We see you so many times when there's extra curricular after the play you and Jeff you guys are mixing it up. After the last one he said that he spoke to you for like two hours and he said that he actually, you know, doesn't have an issue with you but you you know, you guys talk a lot. What's some of the things obviously you know, I'm not going to disclose exactly but what's the gist of like the conversation you have and how has he kind of been a leader on this team for for you? >> Yeah, yeah, coach felt that um I needed I owed him an apology for uh going up to him uh trying to basically get him off uh Slidell. Um and I also felt that, you know, it was a time for we had to talk my rookie year. I can't remember what week it was. It was all the way till the end of the year though. And I was basically we were basically trying to get on the same page. It's like like, you know, he he's amazing obviously. And um I wanted to be the guy that challenged him that made myself better going against him every single day. And you know, um sometimes that a guy like him um people kind of see him as, you know, this amazing player that they don't look at it. They look at it as a challenge more than opportunity. So, you know, and I wanted to I wanted to be blessed with the opportunity to go against him every single day. And we had that talk. And unfortunately, you know, it seems like so long ago. But, you know, just getting hurt last year I felt like I didn't have the that chance as much. I missed a few weeks in training camp, few weeks in the season. So, um you know, we didn't have that rhythm that we'd like to have. So, you know, I also wanted to talk to him about like, "Hey, like let's just establish ourselves. You know, we we pride ourselves on being fast and violent um and being physical. So, you know, we're just talking about everything on how we both can do better um how I can do better, how I can um receive leadership better, how I can be a better leader myself for, you know, our group. And um you know, part of being a leader is being a good follower, a great follower. So, how I can do that as well. Understanding that um you know, it Jeff and Tajae gets into it all the time. But, you know, they're like best friends. And um you know, we were talking. He was like, "Yeah, like you got [snorts] to understand like Jeff's always going to pick on Tajae. Tajae's always going to pick on Jeff." Right? And we were getting to the point where it was like, "Hey, okay. Like we're we're not going to stand for it. Even if you guys are best friends, we got to have a standard for ourselves, you know?" And he said that's what he wants to see out of um O-line. He wants to see the guys, you know, sticking up for each other. He wants to see the guys going to fight for each other because he's showing, you know, checking guys' temperature to uh seeing if they got backbone or not, you know what I mean? So, um just getting on the same page as that. Understand that nothing was personal at all um with anything that happened. Just understand that like that's just how you know the game gets played. You play with a high tension and a high emotion. So at the end of the day if you're going to defend your brother, sometimes you're going against your own teammate in doing so. So >> What type of a baseline do you think that the front five set in the first preseason game which is the Bill Walsh? Um I think we have this thing in our room that good is the enemy of great. You know if you're doing things to be good you're not going to be great. You know so which one do you want to be? I think it was good. I think there's areas where we can clean up on as a whole. I think we can you know just be or just all continue to over communicate, continue to be consistent, continue to strain to finish. We've we're only in I think it was it tallied up to 23 plays. So playing with that intensity through a whole four quarters of football. but I don't look to establish a baseline per se on you know what statistically things could look like more as you know we we try to control the the controllables which is why you know we say every single day we want to play fast, violent, play physical. Those are the things that we can control. So you know however it happens, you know whatever happens and whatever with the ball or whatever it might be, controlling the controllables is what we set out to do every single day and we're more of a process oriented group than a outcome oriented. >> James has made a play and he made a big one today obviously. What's been like for you watching him kind of just go through the process and how has he handled everything? >> I mean he's been great. I think ever since he got here he's picked up the offense really well. Just continue to be a pro each and every day and I just think he's continuing to get better. Just going against pressure and just doing a lot of different things than he may have had been asked to do in college. So he's doing great though. >> How much has he maybe been in your ear as a guy who knows Daboll's offense so well. >> I mean, he's pretty much asking me questions just about whatever route it may be. Just about how to remember certain plays or anything like that. So, just always trying to be into any type of resource that I can for him. You know, being in this offense for quite a while. So. >> When you look at Daboll and the history of slot guys, you know, like Edelman, etc. Yourself now. What are some of the things that you really been able to pull from his experience to add to your game? >> I mean, I would say just learning all the different option routes. I would say in college I didn't get to run as many of them. I was going a lot down the field and then just getting to the league and knowing how to change up different routes, making routes look the same. Just being able to play off of those routes and being able to do a lot of different things. >> What have you learned I guess from the from the joint practice but the preseason opener? >> I think from the joint we just realized how good we can actually be. You know, just figuring out just a little things and little details that we can figure that we can hone in on and the offense will be clicking from there. >> You get to go against these DBs every day. You know, they caught a little bit of flack >> last week. Just What from what you're seeing from them, what do they do well and what are the places that you guys have had success kind of beating? >> I mean, I think all of them can play a lot of different positions. I think obviously Alontae's played in the he's played in the slot but now he's playing on the outside and you know, I go against Marcus quite a bit and I think he's gotten better as as camp's went on and you know, Flaherty played against him for quite a while too just being teammates. So, I think they all do everything pretty much well playing off playing press. You know, just continue to just see different things from other teams and get honed in from there. >> You guys have had two practices now since the the preseason game. How do you feel like offensively you guys have taken what you did on your first couple of drives and then kind of elevated back out here? >> Yeah, I mean, I think that was kind of the big thing. It was like, you know, we saw what that first drive looked like and just continue to be try to be that offense each and every day and each and every period no matter the play just continue to try to have a positive play. >> You know you had the joint practices. You guys like those distances. Is there something more though to having the Super Bowl champs coming in? >> Um, I mean, I definitely think everybody knows what it what that looks like. And, um, you know, I think we really get to see where our team stands at whenever you're going against the team that that won the Super Bowl last year. So. >> Is there a good individual matchup for you with with their secondary? You like that one? >> Oh, yeah. I mean, I love competing anytime. And, um, whenever it's against some of the better guys in the league, it's always fun. >> I know you talked very early on last year about how fast Cam gets the ball on you guys. Can you tell me a little bit about the difference between the ball being on you fast and a fast ball being on you fast and how maybe Cam's working on differentiating that? >> Yeah, I mean, I'd say that like getting up on you fast is more like you just made your break and the ball's just already right there. Um, I mean, he just does a really good job of anticipating when he wants to throw the ball. And, um, sometimes he throws the ball harder than he thinks he he's throwing it. And, so, um, it's just us communicating with him like, "Hey, you can take a little bit off of it right here." And, um, obviously, you know, we want to get run after catch more. So, we don't want to worry too much about, "Hey, we got to worry about the catching." I want to really run through the ball and be able to get YAC for him. So. >> Is there a I mean, a couple of those on uh in San Francisco were pretty hot. >> Yeah. >> I I imagine there's a degree like eating wings that's too hot. >> Oh, yeah. Yeah, we I mean, we talked about it. And, um, I think that's part of it just him this first game and, you know, getting jitters out and stuff like that. So, um, I'm not worried about him at all though. >> What are you You have such a good relationship with him that you put out early on. What what are you in his ear most about? >> Uh, I mean, it just depends on the day. Uh, I mean, I feel like it's a little bit of everything. I mean, um, whether it's just talking about different routes, talking about different throws, um, being in a different spot here, um, just a little bit of everything. So, just always want to be friendly for him and just being in the right spots. >> Have you seen him take some of what you said and translate it out here? >> Oh, yeah, for sure. Yeah, no doubt. I'd say there's definitely been some passes that we may have had in early in camp, um, that you know he just wanted to zip it on in there. I'm like, "Hey, you can you can take some off of it." And then I was being great so. >> How is this maybe brushed during the first 2 weeks of camp? >> Oh, really good. Really good. Obviously, we got a lot a lot of work to do if we want to be the be the unit we we say we're going to be so yeah. We we we're doing good. We're progressing well but a lot of work to do. >> When you talk about the unit you guys want to be, is that something you guys have actually put on paper this is what we're going to be or is it an expectation that you guys >> Well, I mean I'm just a strong believer in saying what you're going to do, believing in what you're going to do. All that matters. So, don't be scared to say that to me if you're scared to say it, scared to talk about what you what you want out of life, what you what you want out of like you're talking about this defense and our goal, well then you got doubts already and you know that's the first battle so just saying what you want, what you expect out of yourself and I'm talking about me, I'm talking about all the guys looking at themselves and then how we look at each other as a unit so it just starts in setting that goal, setting that expectation and staying true to it and living up to it every practice. >> If you're looking at a guy like Carmona who's starting out on the other side, got some promise, going against a Jeff every day in practice, what do you imagine the challenges for a guy like that at the start of that match? >> Well, in my opinion the guys that we have in this locker room, it shouldn't matter who you're going up against. You you got a standard how it's supposed to look and there's no knock on Jeff and and it's I don't think it's an unrealistic standard for him. Doesn't matter who's across from you, you have a standard for yourself that that whether you look yourself in the mirror, you're going to tell yourself you have to uphold or you're going to fold under pressure and I don't think we have guys like that in this locker room. >> When you were with Robert with the Jets, did you guys play this much in the preseason? >> Uh I don't think so. I don't think so but doesn't matter. This is all a new group of guys. A lot of guys learning this this style even offensively for the first time so those game reps are very important so I think it's good for us. >> Do you think you'll get like 25-30 this game, 30 in the next game? >> I have no idea. >> do you like This time of year, I like playing football. So, if I'm out on the field, I'm having fun. >> Coach said today that he called this a hot, physical, speedy practice that he got to see a lot out of what some of you guys can bring. >> What do days like this mean to you? >> Oh, this is In my experience, this is what I refer to if it's a close game, two minute, and we got to we got to get a stop. These are the days I refer back to because it I've been tired like that before. I've been here before. You need to make it You need to go and do it, and you've done it before in practice. So, if you don't have days like this, you can't just go into a game and then decide that oh, I'm going to flip a switch now. I'm going to do something I haven't ever done before. That's not That's not thing that's applicable to any any way of life. So, we're practicing that now. We're We're Like coaches likes to say a lot, we're callousing now in a lot of different ways, and that'll definitely help us in the season. I don't care who's in front of me. It's my job to make it look a certain way. So, like I love playing football, and I have a standard for myself. So, >> Any consideration to the contract year part of this? Do you think about that at all? >> Keep the main thing the main thing. No pun intended. But, you just focus on ball. Don't focus on that other stuff. Guys, myself included, when you when you guys when anybody starts focusing on stuff like that, you forget what's getting you I mean, eventually get you that, and that's being focused on the main thing, and giving it your best. And just like I said a lot of times is putting your standard on tape over and over and over again. And you're not going to do that if you're worried about the wrong thing. >> Imagine yourself in your position where you only get one year here guaranteed. Like, what are you learning about the culture here? Is there a part of you that's like, yeah, I want to see this out." or do you are you able to even think >> I love it so. Um I love the Titans. Uh I love everything that I've experienced uh this far. I know my family does as well. but I mean, my job is to be the best teammate, the best Jermaine Johnson number 11 that I can be this year. Let all that other stuff handle itself. >> What's the main thing that you get out of joint practices? >> Um it's like a really it's like a game. I mean, it really is a game. Um you're just not tackling to the ground. So, I mean, essentially you're getting two games in one week when you count the preseason. But uh it's a great opportunity to go up against the guy that you're going to go up against in the game. And uh you don't get that in the regular season. So, everybody should have a leg up when they go into the game because you played that guy already literally uh 48 hours ago. So, uh you're just seeing the guy twice in one week rather than once compared to the regular regular season. >> Jermaine, we see you line up both sides but even inside sometimes. How do you like the way they're allowing you to have that freedom to rush the passer or something like that? >> Um I mean, I just take it as uh there's a lot of stock in me. They're counting on me to do a lot of things and they're putting me in places to do those things. Um and like I've said a a lot of times, it's going to get boring sounding. But I have a standard for myself. Whatever my job is, it has to look a certain way. Um especially uh for what I expect from myself. And I know they expect um the same thing. I probably expect more of um to be quite honest. Not knocking them, but I'm just aiming for the stars and land on the moon kind of guy. So, um it just got to look a certain way no matter where I am. >> That's not something they do with everybody. What what is it you feel that allows you to bump inside and rush the passer? >> Uh that's how they used me in '23. I did it I've done it already. Um and had some success doing it. Um so, yeah, I've just done it already. It's tried and true. So, it's nothing new. >> A lot of stuff went on in that first during practice. Do you anticipate the same round two? >> I don't know. >> Why do you say that? What kind of part do you play? I mean, this camp is week two or three, I don't even know what day it is. Um, so, I mean, guys are just, honestly, tired, uh, frustrated, short fuse kind of thing going on, but again, it's a great opportunity to cuz you're going to have a short fuse, you're going to be tired in a game, what are you going to do, punch somebody? So, we can't have kind of stuff like that, but at the same time, it shows the fight that your team has in certain situations. So, there's a pros and cons to this when it comes to scuffles. Um, but, uh, I don't know. We'll we'll see, we'll see on Friday.

title: Recapping the Preseason Win, Joey Slye's Perfect Night & the New Uniforms | The OTP
text: [music] It is the OTP. Welcome back. I'm Taylor Zarszer. I'm joined by my dear friend Rhett Bryan. By the offensive line guru, now sideline analyst for your Tennessee Titans, Brad Hopkins. Good to see you, Hop. and by the lead analyst for the Tennessee Titans, my man Raone Foster, lifelong Tennessee and and now the Tennessee Titan analyst. That sounds pretty good. >> It was really good this past week. Okay. Thoroughly enjoyed myself in the booth with you guys. Our exchange we had with Brad and I on the sideline, the back and forth that we have, it felt like we played our own game up in the booth. >> Yeah, we did. We had a lot of fun. Um I loved seeing how fired up Rhett Bryan was. uh to see this edition of Titans Radio. And I know our dear friend, Coach Mack, was smiling down on us. He would have been laughing at us the other night and enjoying himself. >> He would have. He absolutely would have. And I know we're going to get to the football of all of it and what we observed. He would have been pleased with some things in that part of it, too. But, uh, we got off to a nice start and I'm very happy and proud to be teammates with these two guys and certainly with UTZ. But, yeah, we we pretty good start. Very good start. Hop, what did it feel like to be on the sideline again? It's been a minute. >> It almost felt like it was game day for us, you know, like we're actually going to take the field and compete because Rhett's words of wisdom before the show started, Will Bowling, who obviously is a part of the cast, too, uh, doing push-ups and shadow boxing to just get rid of some of that energy. Uh, these guys were ready to play and it was something that was new to me just watching you guys get prepared to articulate this game and I'm just so blessed to be a part of it. Well, you certainly had a lot of enthusiasm, Raone, to be up there in the booth with us, and I loved hearing it pour out of you. Let's start with you. What did you think of the Titans in preseason game number one? >> Man, I thought early on, especially with the ones, you got more of what you wanted to see. Most definitely to start at the five yard line and just march it down the field. I know Coach Solace spoke about a pitch count that the guys were going to be on. I thought they were going to knock it out on the first series, man. Um, it's still evaluation side of this thing. some good, some bad, some in between, and it's just the first step of building this 2026 Tennessee Titans team. And I thought it was very entertaining, and some guys took some steps in it as well. Thoroughly enjoyed myself. You know, I uh I said this at the very beginning of the game that I got chills and really almost overwhelmed in the production meeting the day before by something that Robert Solace said about this team because Dave McInness said it every day of his life. And I don't know that coach Salah knew that. Um, but it was a little eerie, uh, maybe bordering on Coach Mack being with us to hear Coach Salah say, "We need more time on task." And it's obvious. It's a brand new football team, Brad. It's a team that's going through a completely different scheme. Um, you have new coaches on both sides of the ball, and it's a really young football team, which is why what Ramon just said needs to happen. The first team needs to play meaningful snaps in the preseason. >> Yeah, I saw Cam being very confident when you see the offense start on its own five yard line and march 95 yards down the field, beginning the drive with a run, ending it with a run, being very physical uh in the trenches. That to me was a setting of an identity. But like you said, this is preseason. They just want to see if the guys can go out there and compete. You know, there wasn't, you know, any sort of intricate detail or plan going into the game. They just wanted to keep it base, keep it vanilla, just to see if the guys could put their hands in the dirt, right? And really just get after it >> and they did. Uh that that first couple of series was exciting. The first one certainly uh and and that was the big takeaway for me is just they always talk about it takes 11 to run the football. That's what they did and they ran it effectively, but they did that throughout the night when you're talking about, you know, in in 2025 they ran 93 yards per game as a team per average and 4.2 too a carry and they did 166 yards as a team, you know, at the end of this thing and yes, I know it's the preseason and I know there's plenty of things to work on, but there's encouraging things that all these backs contributed and I think that's the biggest takeaway. Look, Tony Pard did Tony Pard things. He is the consumate pro and it's like, yep, he's just as sure as death taxes, rain coming, whatever. Like, he's just there. And then Taj puts on a show. Julius Chestnut puts on a show. Nick Singleton puts on a show. I mean, there's some there's some horses in this stable now. Yeah. And that you you absolutely um hit on the thing that really stood out to me. It was how effective the ground game was. And Red, it wasn't just in the game on Thursday night. It was in practice on Tuesday. You know, all of us remarked at how effective they were running the football. You can't be effective running the football unless you have some Hopkins and some Fosters in front of you that are pushing the defense around. And you guys noticed that on Tuesday against first team 49ers that the Titans first team offensive line was doing it and it carried over in the game as well. Raone, there was no brother-in-law in that practice on Tuesday. >> Was not. No, it felt like they were born enemies on Tuesday. >> We saw JC setting the tone. We saw a young Carmona setting the tone. Pete Skansky definitely worth the bag. He set the tone. These guys really came out with the mindset to play and you saw that guys on the field on on Thursday night when linemen are staying on their blocks. Obviously, great reads by the backs. Tony Power, like you said, Rhett was doing Tony Per things, but the line giving them opportunities, making holes, and then staying on sustaining those blocks. That's what helped them getundred what 66 yards rushing in total in that game. >> It was. And not just that, man. You seen a lot of athleticism out of this group as well. You got size, you got power, but these guys can pull left and right. I think it showed um just on the uh Gunner Helm screenplay, guys were down the field moving bodies down. They have some explosiveness to this offense. And of course, in the preseason, you don't show everything. Brad and I were talking recently about how there wasn't a whole lot of motions beforehand because this is, as Coach Sol said, they are in evaluation mode. They want to see these guys do the baseline, right? so they can start stacking those practices, stacking those movements and starting being more advanced the closer and closer we get to the pre I mean get ready to for the regular season. So, I was glad to see it. Hoppy and I, man, we were we were pushing and hitting each other on the sideline. Um, and uh in that 49ers practice because those types of things, they translate over. You want to see more of that. >> Yeah, you do. And you saw some new faces. Austin Schlotman at center, Fernando Carmona at right guard, Cordell Volen came in there and was effective at right guard as well. And also some improvement from Dan Moore and from JC Laam the tackles in the game. And I love Brian Baldinger who's been a great NFL analyst for many years and of course played in the league. He was giving Pete Scaransky his flowers on social media showing Skeransky manhandling some 49ers. So it was good to see how physical they were up front. I would say Rhett, the biggest thing that needs improvement based off of what we saw in San Francisco on Tuesday in the practice and Thursday in the game is just better timing in the passing game. But I would also think that that's probably the hardest thing um to do when you have a new scheme, a new coaching staff, and you got new players that you have to build chemistry with. Cam Ward is trying to figure out exactly when Carnell Tate is going to get out of his break and when Juell Robinson is going to do the same. Let's go back to what coach Salah told you in the production meeting. Time on task. You haven't had a ton of that. And considering you've just installed this offense in the last couple of three week, you've just finished that part of it and you're peeling back the pages of this thing. And listen, considering Cam is still learning and and learning a second offense in not even a second full uh second year in the league, there's some things to be considered there. He he has his moments of throwing on time. There just needs to move more consistency with that. And I think there's, you know, they're all working together to get to that goal. Um, you know, Cam has some teachable moments from the other night. And he's not alone in that. Like that's not just singling him out cuz there's a couple of plays he I mean, listen, uh, there's some throws he made that was decent uh, and and kind of made you, you know, go, "Yep, there there's that." There were some ones where he needs to be more, you know, head on a swivel. Um, thinking about this receiving cord, too. Um, listen, David Martin Robinson, that catch he had while taking just missile heat from a defender >> and did, you know, hang on to that. Really good stuff there. Um, but yeah, there's there's three or four players in this that really took last week and won last week. And I know we're going to get into some of who those are.
