I can acknowledge as well my practice reps were different than my game reps. My nerves were a little bit different. I didn't feel pain as much. I was more hype about the process. And I think when you look at cams and the wide receivers, you know, the misconnections that they had or lack of connection that they had it is that that's why you want guys in stadiums under the lights in front of the TV where you realize Cam, you can get hit. That's pressure on the offensive line to be able to handle that. These guys aren't your teammates. You can't just break them down. There's film study that goes into this and how I step on a DB's toes and break out. And the same thing defensively as well. I mean, we speak a lot about the offense, but defense missed some tackles for loss in the back field or some sacks. Like all of that is the steps you take of acknowledging I'm building myself up for training camp. Again, you're not preaching patience. You just acknowledge that there is some patience that go into getting this thing right. because what this team will start off as in September is not the version you want to see when they hit December, January football. >> Yeah, it'll continue to evolve. I I'm not concerned at all, Raone, U Taylor, about the level of comprehension that Cam has with this offense. U Brian is feeding him nicely the things he needs to do. Now, it's just playing quarterback. You know, accurately putting on the ball, putting a receivers's hands so that way he can get the yards after catch, things of that nature, but also playing within the scheme of itself to what the defense gives you. So, uh, I think that overall, obviously, like you just mentioned, Taylor, there are some things that that everyone's needs to work on. You know, this is still a developing just one step in the three steps it takes to get to regular season working against other an uncommon opponent, but for the most part, I thought these guys, you know, they play within themselves and weren't getting out of character, out of sorts. The first drive was different than the second drive, but the second drive also was featuring more more uh longer developing plays to where timing wasn't as much of an issue uh as it was in the first one. But for the most part, I really was kind of pleased with how efficiently they moved the ball up and down the field. >> I want to ask both of our veteran offensive linemen this question because I see Cam trying to feed the ball uh to as many guys as he possibly can. And and that's a wealth of riches to see that this tight end core and this receiving core is is on paper and so far in practice and a preseason game better than it's been in quite some time. where where what does the the quarterback do to get past the I've got one football and I'd like to get it to about seven different guys because you did it with Steve McNair, you did it with Ben Rothosberger and that's a real thing. >> I think sometimes quarterbacks and offensive coordinators are trying to be less predictable. You know what I mean? Because >> how many times do we see Deon dribbling catch the ball over the middle? Whether it was Martinez, whether it was Ror, these guys were definitely keying in on where he was on the football field and he was making plays and there's almost no disguise of where they were going with the football. I just think that Cam wants to be and Brian maybe wants to be someone that kind of balances out where they go with the football. I think at some point in time as this thing develops, whoever has the hot hand will be the guy that gets featured in each one of those series. But for the most part, Ramon, it's not um them really delegating what guy to go to. They're just trying to find out going through a progression who actually has the most separation and can make a play after they catch the ball. >> Poppy, I go back to what you said a second ago. It's also um Cam's ability to give take what the defense is giving them too as well. And that's part too when you have all of this talent. I do think it's a lot of talent when you look at the wide receivers, the running backs and the tight ends. Like that's a lot of pressure for a young quarterback, for any quarterback, but especially a young quarterback. He's got to get to a point in my opinion and Cam, he'll get that point because he wants to be so great. Like I'll come to you Ell. I'll come to you C, but not right now. The defense isn't allowing this. I'm not going to put us in harm's way by forcing something to you because I know they're keying in on you. And I thought he had a couple of those moments with Cardell because he and Carell are coming up together. They're both young. They're both going to be in this together. And like I tell people all the time and Hop, you know this, you've been around good teams with good receivers and a good quarterback. The quarterback does have to get kind of >> cocky on them. I'll get to you when I can. You know, those are the things you have to do to build on that hop so that you don't I don't want to hurt us >> by trying to please you, >> right? But I will say real quick, um, it looked a little clunky because normally you've got tape to watch to discover tendencies, right? Things that you want to exploit, things you want to take advantage of from the defense. They were just rolling the football out and playing football. Basically, we got plays that we want to run. We want to get and see what they look like against the defense, but it's not schematically designed to really attack any sort of part and that's why it looked like >> preseason. I love that everybody played though and I love that back to your point. I love that the first team uh got so many reps and we'll talk about the next couple of games. Going back to uh kind of breaking down each position group or or each unit. You know, we talked about how effective Rhett talked about how effective the Titans were running the game. How about stopping the run? You know, that was just as impressive as the the Titans ability to effectively run the football. >> It was, man. And and of course, when you got Jeffrey Simmons being double teamed almost anytime I was watching from up top just like the others, two on Jeff right now. Somebody else got to eat. But it's not just that front four. Those linebackers were hitting the hole and making tackles as well. I thought co I thought Cody Barton had probably one of his better games in the small sample size that he's have to just be the very veteran savvy guy that can just get a guy down. Man, it's attacking. But also cool part for me is watching the smaller guys, outside guys put their face in the fan. Ammani getting in in the run game as well. You guys know like I know you win this game by winning the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball. >> Yeah, this team was disciplined in their rush lanes. This isn't a team, Brett, and you've seen this that basically stops the run on the way to the quarterback. [laughter] They're they're reading nuances. They're staying disciplined within their lanes, and they're not giving the offense any kind of uh cavities to run through. So, that's why I thought that they were really effective in basically shutting down that run and making them one-dimensional offensively for San Fran. >> What did you think about the defensive performance, Rhett? >> I you can tell the structure. Obviously, the base alignment is different from what we've seen in previous years, but just the operation of it all. The fast and violent part, like, okay, I can see where that's going to live, how that's going to work. I mean, you look at the final game book, you had seven tackles for loss, and I think four of those came in the first half. I mean, they were they were effective in some spots. Yeah. Again, they have places they need to work on and knowing that, you know, as you got into the game, there's twos and threes playing and, you know, different parts of the depth chart, but uh I think they had the moments. >> 20-year-old Kellrick Faulk, shout out to him. Won't turn 21 until September the 7th before his first game. It's a lot of young Bucks out there on the field and they look good. Now, we certainly can talk about how effective the Titans were running the game and stopping the run. If there was an MVP of the game, I think Brad Hopkins spoke to him afterwards. [laughter] Joey Sly was five for five in the game. He made his extra point. He made all four of his field goals, three of which were over 50 yards in length. What a night for the kicker. What an entire trip to the Bay Area. He was perfect for the entire trip. Yeah, I I'm sure that Brian Dal and the offense wanted to give him shorter distances to kick from getting into the red zone, but when he needed to basically finish drives with points, that's what's important. The worst thing, Ramon, you can speak to this, is to leave the football field punting when there's no points on the board. But Joey obviously made that not an issue by putting some points on the board regardless. >> We had to use real math to calculate how far he was. [laughter] >> I mean, how long is that again? >> Exactly. But but it wasn't just that though, too. looking at the elements that were there. He kicked in, you know, away from the wind with the wind be behind him and then he also kicked in it. The last one they had where the flags were coming at him and he's got the leg plus there was distance behind him. But I I just give a kudos to him for you know the week before wasn't his greatest showing and everybody's got a day hop. You know this trainer camp it was my you have no excuse for why you missed the block, missed the kick or missed the throw. And that reset, man, is is necessary this time of the year. And you want to see guys redeem themselves. And I thought he did a real good job. >> That leg strength doesn't surprise me at all because he looks like a little MMA fighter. You know what I mean? Just a stoutness with his legs. Exactly. >> And read every single one of them bullseye. It wasn't like he wasn't any question. No, it wasn't like they're barely going in. >> This wasn't like that was one kick we saw from Eddie Panero. He tried to kick the what a 58 yard or whatever. just kind of went >> fell short fell short of the the crossbar. U in my opinion there were four guys who won last week and Joey Sly is the leader of the classroom in that one by what we've just outlined. The other is JC Laam. He has channeled the nasty like he I don't know what has made him angry but man more of that please because that is working. Fernando Carmona has started to work himself early into situations. I'd like to see more of that because I think they're still trying to figure out who is the right guard of the Tennessee Titans. And the last one for me is Fime Dejio. They had seven tackles for loss. He had two of those five tackles total. He starts to flash in places. You mentioned Kendrick Faulk who had some pressures the other night, but those four made the best of last week. title: The Only Way the 49ers Can Prove or Disprove the Substation Theory

title: Coach Mike McCarthy Press Conference (August 17) | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: Well, you have to juggle what you're doing, huh? Now, what's the thought process, Mike? >> Well, um, we're going to break camp early. Um, you know, in some ways disappointing to leave here because this is such a great environment for us to train in. Um, you know, it's disappointing, frankly, for the fans. So, we'll get a full day Wednesday, get some competitive work, padded good padded practice, you know, mock game and get another full training camp day, you know, on the south side Wednesday. Then we'll have the Saturday type practice Thursday. You know, kind of because I'm trying to integrate what the inseason schedule is going to look like for our players and our coaches. I mean, there's there's classrooms I'm going to flip next year. I mean, just, you know, just you want to get it to, you know, what's you feel is the best, you know, classroom environment for your team, the best practice environment. You know, I I I I really think this is not only a special place, but this is this is a great place to train a football team. You know, just the whole environment and so forth. So, no, I'm you know, players might not want to hear this, but hell, we'll look to see if we can stay longer next year. Was that more preparing for different situations that might arise during the season or do you still feel like that's uh an unsettled unresolved uh competition between a couple guys? >> I think it's both. I mean, it's um, you know, we got to decide if we're going to get into left side training, right side training, you know, flipping tackle for tackle. He's play he's thrown the football a lot in his life, you know, go back to his high school days. So, um, and that that's important.
